title: Specialized Areas (SA 800, SA 805 & SA 810) – Special Purpose Frameworks, Single FS/Elements, Summary Financial Statements
description: CA Final – Auditing and Assurance | Advanced MCQ practice bank on the Specialized Areas chapter: the meaning, examples and acceptance of a special purpose framework and the SA 320 / SA 260 / SA 700 consequences that follow from it, including mandatory alerting of readers and optional restriction on distribution; audits of a single financial statement or a specific element, account or item, covering practicability of the engagement, adaptation of the other SAs, element-level materiality, separate opinions, publication together, the five relevance factors and the three conditions for a clean opinion on an element after an adverse or disclaimed complete-set opinion; and engagements to report on summary financial statements, covering applied criteria, management responsibility, the seven required procedures, subsequent events, permitted forms of opinion, references to matters in the audited-FS report, elements and dating of the report, auditor association and the SA 700 / SA 720 / SA 800 cross-references. Every question is independently usable; case studies are repeated in full inside each question.

questions.question:
SA 800 and the meaning of a special purpose framework are expressed in the following statements. Which of them are correct?

**Statement 1:** SA 800 itself prescribes a self-contained financial reporting framework that an entity may adopt in place of its general purpose framework.
**Statement 2:** The SAs in the 100-700 series apply to the audit of financial statements, and SA 800 deals with special considerations in the application of those SAs to the audit of financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework.
**Statement 3:** A financial reporting framework designed to meet the financial information needs of specific users is a special purpose framework.
**Statement 4:** In an audit of special purpose financial statements, SA 800 dispenses with the SA 210 requirement that the auditor determine the acceptability of the financial reporting framework applied.
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 800 is not itself a financial reporting framework; it deals with special considerations in applying the SAs of the 100-700 series to audits of financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework, which is exactly what Statement 2 says. Statement 3 gives the definitional core that separates a special purpose framework from a general purpose framework, namely design to meet the financial information needs of specific users. Statement 1 fails because the framework comes from the entity's own reporting requirements and not from the Standard. Statement 4 fails because SA 210's requirement to determine acceptability of the FRF continues to apply; SA 800 only makes the intended users' financial information needs the key factor in that determination. Therefore only 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** While auditing the regulatory accounts of a power distribution licensee prepared under financial reporting provisions issued by the Electricity Regulatory Commission, the auditor applies the SAs in the 100-700 series and looks to SA 800 only for the special considerations relevant to such an audit.
**Reason (R):** SA 800 does not lay down a separate body of auditing or reporting requirements of its own; it deals with special considerations in the application of the SAs of the 100-700 series to audits of financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Commission-prescribed reporting provisions made to meet that regulator's requirements are one of the examples of a special purpose framework listed in SA 800, so the engagement in Assertion A is a special purpose audit. In such an audit the operative requirements remain the SAs of the 100-700 series, because SA 800 only adds special considerations for applying them; that is precisely what the Reason states and it is the reason the Assertion holds. The Reason is therefore not merely a true parallel statement but the cause of the position in the Assertion. An auditor who treated SA 800 as a self-contained code displacing the 100-700 series would misread its nature, and an auditor who denied that regulator-prescribed provisions are a special purpose framework would misread the examples.

questions.question:
**CASE:** A research trust receives a project grant and is required to submit statements drawn up strictly as per the reporting clauses of the sanction letter. An article in CA Prakash's firm writes in his acceptance note: 'The sanction letter itself shows the purpose, the format and the recipient, so SA 800 does not call for any separate understanding on our side; and as the donor has fixed the framework, there is no acceptability work for us.'
Evaluate this note against SA 800 and SA 210 and select the MOST appropriate conclusion.
options: He is right on both counts, because a donor-prescribed framework is automatically acceptable and the understanding requirement is discharged by the sanction letter.

He is right that no separate understanding is needed, but wrong that no acceptability work is needed, since SA 210 asks the auditor, and not the donor who fixed the format, to determine the acceptability of the financial reporting framework applied in preparation of the statements.

He is wrong on both counts: the understanding of the purpose and of the intended users is the auditor's own obligation under SA 800 and cannot be presumed from the existence of a prescribed format, and he must still determine acceptability of the framework under SA 210.

He is wrong about the understanding requirement but right about acceptability, because a framework fixed by a binding contract between the parties is by that very fact incapable of being found unacceptable by the auditor.
questions.explanation: SA 800 states that in an audit of special purpose financial statements the auditor shall obtain an understanding of the purpose for which the statements are prepared and of the intended users; a 'shall' obligation of the auditor is not discharged by assuming that a document already on file supplies it. SA 210 separately requires the auditor to determine the acceptability of the FRF applied, and in a special purpose engagement the financial information needs of the intended users are the key factor in that determination. The decisive fact is that the note treats both obligations as satisfied by the donor's own papers. Only the conclusion which rejects both limbs of the note is complete: the conclusion which accepts the understanding limb but rejects the acceptability limb, and the one which does exactly the reverse, each leave half of the article's error standing, and the conclusion which agrees with the article is wrong twice over.

questions.category: SA 800 – Considerations in Accepting Such Audit
options: I and II only
II, III and IV only
I, II and III only
All of I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation: SA 800 requires the auditor in a special purpose audit to obtain an understanding of the purpose for which the financial statements are prepared and of the intended users, covering matters I and II. SA 210 requires the auditor to determine the acceptability of the financial reporting framework applied, and in a special purpose engagement the key factor in that determination is the financial information needs of the intended users, which is matter III. Matter IV is the decoy: what the bank might alternatively have accepted has no bearing either on the required understanding or on the acceptability of the framework actually applied to these statements. The existence of general purpose financial statements alongside is likewise not decisive, so the correct set is I, II and III only.

options: It is a general purpose framework, because Sanjay maintains a complete set of books of account on a systematic basis and separately gets audited general purpose financial statements of his business, which go to members and creditors generally.

It is neither general nor special purpose, because a framework written by a lender on its own template can hardly be described as the entity's own financial reporting framework, whichever users it may reach.

SA 800 is not attracted to this audit, because a layout supplied by the intended user is not a framework designed to meet anybody's financial information needs in any meaningful sense of that expression.

It is a special purpose framework, being the cash basis of accounting with cash-basis information prepared for creditors and designed to meet the financial information needs of specific users, so the special considerations in SA 800 apply.
questions.explanation: The test is whose information needs the framework is designed to meet, not who drafted the paper it is written on or how systematically the underlying books are kept. A cash basis of accounting with cash-basis information prepared for creditors is one of the three examples of special purpose frameworks given in SA 800, and these statements go to one named bank for one named credit decision, so the users are specific. The decisive fact is that Delta Bank is the only intended user; the mere coexistence of general purpose financial statements of the same business does not convert the cash-basis statements into general purpose statements. The two alternatives which turn on authorship wrongly treat the fact that the lender wrote the template as disqualifying, when a framework prescribed by the party whose needs it is designed to serve remains a financial reporting framework.

questions.category: SA 800 – Considerations in Accepting Such Audit
questions.question:
**CASE:** Sanjay runs an auto-parts trading business as a sole proprietor and keeps his books on the cash basis. On 15 April 20X5 he asks CA Meera to audit his cash-basis financial statements for the year ended 31 March 20X5, comprising a statement of cash receipts and payments and a statement of cash balances. The statements are to be submitted only to Delta Bank Ltd. in support of his request to enhance his working capital limit from Rs. 1.2 crore to Rs. 2.5 crore, and the bank has itself specified the formats and the line items to be reported. Meera notes that Sanjay's business also prepares general purpose financial statements under the applicable general purpose framework, and that Delta Bank has asked only for the cash-basis statements. Meera has not previously accepted an audit of this kind and, before accepting the engagement, discusses four matters with her article:
(I) the purpose for which the cash-basis statements have been prepared;
(II) who the intended users of those statements are;
(III) whether the cash-basis framework is acceptable having regard to that purpose and those users; and
(IV) whether Delta Bank would have accepted a report on the general purpose financial statements instead.
Which of the following actions should Meera take in connection with this engagement?
1. Determine the acceptability of the cash-basis framework by reference to the financial information needs of Delta Bank as the intended user.
2. Obtain an understanding of the purpose for which the statements are prepared and of the intended users, before concluding on acceptance.
3. Treat the framework as acceptable by definition, because it was prescribed by the very lender to whom the statements are to be submitted.
4. Apply the SAs in the 100-700 series to the engagement, taking into account the special considerations set out in SA 800.
options: 1, 2 and 3
1, 2 and 4
2, 3 and 4
1, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: Actions 1, 2 and 4 follow directly from the source: SA 800 requires an understanding of the purpose and the intended users, SA 210 requires the auditor to determine acceptability of the FRF with the intended users' financial information needs as the key factor, and the 100-700 series SAs remain the applicable requirements with SA 800 supplying special considerations. Action 3 is the error to be rejected: it confuses who prescribed the format with the auditor's separate duty to judge acceptability. The decisive fact is that acceptability is assessed against the intended users' information needs, and the fact that Delta Bank designed the template is evidence about those needs, not a substitute for the auditor's determination.

questions.category: SA 800 – Examples of Special Purpose Frameworks
questions.question:
**CASE:** Bharat Infrastructure Ltd. has received a project grant of Rs. 240 crore from a national funding agency for a metro rail package. The sanction conditions require the company to prepare, each year, 'Project Funds Utilised Statements' drawn up strictly as per the heads of account, formats and valuation instructions set out in the grant agreement, and to submit them to that agency. Separately, the company's wholly-owned subsidiary, a power distribution licensee, must file annual regulatory accounts prepared under financial reporting provisions issued by the Electricity Regulatory Commission to meet the Commission's requirements. CA Rohit is approached to audit both sets of statements. He also notes that Bharat Infrastructure files general purpose financial statements, including consolidated statements, under the applicable general purpose framework, and that the funding agency has not asked for those.

Match the items in Column I with the description in Column II that fits best.
Column I
(A) The heads of account, formats and valuation instructions contained in the grant agreement
(B) The financial reporting provisions issued by the Electricity Regulatory Commission
(C) Bharat Infrastructure's consolidated general purpose financial statements
(D) A statement of cash receipts and payments prepared by a trader solely for one specific trade creditor
Column II
(1) A special purpose framework of the kind described in SA 800 as financial reporting provisions of a contract
(2) A special purpose framework of the kind described in SA 800 as financial reporting provisions established by a regulator to meet the requirements of that regulator
(3) A framework designed to meet the financial information needs of a wide range of users rather than of specific users
(4) A special purpose framework of the kind described in SA 800 as cash basis of accounting with cash-basis information prepared for creditors
questions.explanation: The grant agreement is a contract and the project grant is SA 800's own illustration of financial reporting provisions of a contract, so A matches 1. The Commission's provisions are established by a regulator to meet that regulator's requirements, so B matches 2. Consolidated general purpose financial statements are designed for a wide range of users and therefore fall on the other side of the line drawn by the definition, so C matches 3. Cash-basis information prepared for creditors is SA 800's first listed example, so D matches 4. The trap in options 1 and 2 is swapping the contract-based and regulator-based categories, which are distinct examples.

questions.question:
**CASE:** Bharat Infrastructure Ltd. has received a project grant of Rs. 240 crore from a national funding agency for a metro rail package. The sanction conditions require the company to prepare, each year, 'Project Funds Utilised Statements' drawn up strictly as per the heads of account, formats and valuation instructions set out in the grant agreement, and to submit them to that agency. Separately, the company's wholly-owned subsidiary, a power distribution licensee, must file annual regulatory accounts prepared under financial reporting provisions issued by the Electricity Regulatory Commission to meet the Commission's requirements. CA Rohit is approached to audit both sets of statements. He also notes that Bharat Infrastructure files general purpose financial statements, including consolidated statements, under the applicable general purpose framework, and that the funding agency has not asked for those.
Which one of the following statements about these two engagements is NOT correct?
options: For both frameworks, the key factor in determining acceptability under SA 210 is the financial information needs of the respective intended users.
The intended user whose information needs drive the acceptability assessment differs between the two engagements, being the funding agency in one case and the Commission in the other.

Because each framework has been laid down by the authority to whom the statements are filed, SA 210's requirement that the auditor determine the acceptability of the FRF does not operate in these audits.
Both sets of reporting provisions are examples of special purpose frameworks given in SA 800, and SA 800 supplies special considerations for applying the 100-700 series SAs to them.
questions.explanation: SA 210 requires the auditor to determine acceptability of the FRF applied in preparation of the financial statements, and SA 800 makes the financial information needs of the intended users the key factor in that determination for special purpose financial statements; that requirement is not switched off because a third party drafted the framework, which is why the third statement is the incorrect one. The first and second statements follow from the same rule applied to two different intended users. The fourth statement is the correct characterisation of the two examples in SA 800, and the decoy fact in the case, namely the existence of consolidated general purpose financial statements, does not alter either conclusion.

questions.question:
**SCENARIO:** A chartered accountant is appointed to audit a manufacturing concern's statement of cash receipts and payments prepared under a cash-basis framework prescribed by a bank, to be submitted only to that bank for sanctioning a working capital facility.
Which ONE of the following changes in the facts would make the auditor most likely to reconsider whether the framework being used is a special purpose framework?
options: The bank requires the statements to cover three years instead of one and to be re-submitted every year.

The statements are put into general circulation without any restriction and are relied upon by a large, unspecified group of existing and potential users for their general financial information needs.
The entity changes the measurement basis used within the statements from pure cash receipts and payments to a cash plus outstanding basis, while still reporting only to that bank.
The bank transfers the borrower's account to another branch, so a different branch manager becomes the recipient of the statements.
The entity engages a different audit firm, which had not previously accepted an audit of this kind.
questions.explanation: The definitional core of a special purpose framework is that it is designed to meet the financial information needs of specific users, so the fact that changes the answer is the one that removes the specificity of the user group. General circulation to a large and unspecified set of users who rely on the statements for their general information needs takes the framework outside that definition and calls for reconsideration. Period, measurement basis within the same specific-user design, the identity of the individual officer receiving the statements and the identity of the audit firm all leave the users and the purpose unchanged, which is why they do not disturb the classification.

questions.category: SA 800 – Examples of Special Purpose Frameworks
questions.question:
The following are described as frameworks used by auditees. Which of them are examples of special purpose frameworks as given in SA 800?

**Item 1:** A cash basis of accounting, with cash-basis information prepared for creditors.
**Item 2:** Financial reporting provisions established by a regulator to meet the requirements of that regulator.
**Item 3:** Financial reporting provisions of a contract, such as a loan agreement or a project grant.
**Item 4:** A framework designed to meet the financial information needs of a wide range of users, which SA 800 brings within the special purpose category whenever the auditee is a listed entity.
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 800 illustrates special purpose frameworks by three examples: a cash basis of accounting with cash-basis information prepared for creditors, financial reporting provisions established by a regulator to meet that regulator's requirements, and financial reporting provisions of a contract such as a loan agreement or a project grant. Items 1, 2 and 3 reproduce those illustrations. Item 4 is the general purpose side of the distinction, since a framework designed to meet the needs of a wide range of users is not one designed for specific users, and listing status is irrelevant to the classification. Any option that admits item 4 therefore misreads the definition.

questions.question:
**CASE:** CA Niveditha receives two approaches within a week. Client 1 is a hospital society whose 'scheme-wise income and expenditure statements' are drawn up strictly as per the reporting clauses of a research grant agreement with a government department and are filed only with that department. Client 2 is a private company whose financial statements are prepared under the applicable general purpose framework for the benefit of its members and creditors generally. Niveditha must decide how SA 800 and SA 210 operate on each engagement.
Which of the following analyses is correct?
options: Client 1 is not a special purpose engagement, because a grant agreement is a funding arrangement rather than a financial reporting framework and supplies only the money; Client 2 is, because a wide range of users is a less specific description than one named department.
Both engagements are special purpose audits, so SA 800 applies to both and the acceptability of the framework is judged by the government department's information needs in each case.

Client 1 is a special purpose engagement in which the department is the intended user and acceptability turns on its financial information needs; Client 2 is not a special purpose engagement, so its framework is outside the special purpose definition.
Neither engagement is affected by SA 800, because SA 800 replaces the SAs in the 100-700 series for every audit that is not on financial statements prepared under a general purpose framework.
questions.explanation: Reporting clauses of a research grant agreement are financial reporting provisions of a contract, which SA 800 gives as an example of a special purpose framework, and the statements serve the specific user that is the party to the grant. In that engagement the auditor must understand the purpose and the intended users, and must determine acceptability of the framework under SA 210 by reference to the department's financial information needs. Client 2's framework is designed for a wide range of users and so is not classified as special purpose. The alternative which denies that SA 800 affects either engagement states the opposite of the source, since SA 800 supplies special considerations for applying the 100-700 series rather than replacing them.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about an audit of financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework. Which of them are NOT correct?

**Statement 1:** The key factor in determining the acceptability of the financial reporting framework applied is the financial information needs of the intended users.
**Statement 2:** The auditor determines acceptability of a special purpose framework by reference to the needs of users at large, precisely because such statements serve a narrower audience.
**Statement 3:** Where the framework is laid down in a contract or by a regulator, the auditor need not determine its acceptability, since SA 210 gives way to SA 800.
**Statement 4:** The auditor shall obtain an understanding of the purpose for which the financial statements are prepared and of the intended users.
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are the requirements as stated: SA 210 obliges the auditor to determine acceptability of the FRF, and in a special purpose audit the financial information needs of the intended users are the key factor, while the auditor shall understand the purpose of the statements and who the intended users are. Statement 2 inverts the rule by substituting the needs of users at large for those of the intended users. Statement 3 wrongly treats a regulator's or a counterparty's prescription of the framework as displacing the auditor's own determination under SA 210, when SA 800 is only about special considerations in applying the SAs. The question asks for the incorrect statements, so 2 and 3 only is the answer.

questions.category: SA 800 – Examples of Special Purpose Frameworks
questions.question:
**CASE:** One of three partners retires from a partnership firm carrying on a textiles trading business. The continuing partners and the retiring partner ask the auditor of the partnership firm to report on 'Retirement Accounts' of the firm as at 31 March 20X5, prepared strictly using the valuation and profit-allocation formulas set out in the partnership deed, solely so that the retiring partner's claim can be settled. The partnership firm does not prepare financial statements under any general purpose framework. A relative of one partner, unconnected with the firm, casually asks for a copy of the report.
What is the MOST appropriate evaluation of the reporting provisions of the deed, and of what the auditor must do?
options: They are not a special purpose framework, because the intended users of a retirement settlement are the owners of the entity themselves, and proprietors of the auditee can never be specific users within the meaning given in SA 800.

They are not a special purpose framework, because the deed merely fixes the sum payable by way of settlement of a departing partner's dues and prescribes no basis on which financial information is to be reported.
They are a special purpose framework, but because the deed is a binding contract between the partners the auditor may presume its framework to be acceptable and need not form a view of his own on it.

They are financial reporting provisions of a contract, like SA 800's illustrations of a loan agreement or a project grant, so the auditor shall understand the purpose and the intended users and determine acceptability of the framework under SA 210.
questions.explanation: SA 800 lists financial reporting provisions of a contract, such as a loan agreement or a project grant, as an example of a special purpose framework; a partnership deed prescribing the valuation and allocation basis on which retirement accounts are drawn up stands in the same position. The statements are prepared to meet the financial information needs of specific users, namely the continuing and the retiring partners, and the relative's casual request does not enlarge that group. The auditor must accordingly obtain an understanding of the purpose and the intended users and must determine acceptability of the framework under SA 210, so the alternative which treats the deed as making the framework automatically acceptable is the closest wrong answer. The two alternatives which deny that any special purpose framework exists wrongly exclude users who are also owners, and wrongly assert that a valuation formula in a deed prescribes nothing about reporting.

questions.question:
In planning and performing an audit of financial statements prepared in accordance with a special purpose framework, an auditor formulates the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The auditor should comply with all SAs relevant to the audit.
**Statement 2:** The auditor should comply with ethical requirements, including independence.
**Statement 3:** Application of some SAs may require special consideration, for example judgments under SA 320 being based on the financial information needs of intended users.
**Statement 4:** The SAs of the 100-700 series stand displaced to the extent the engagement relates to a special purpose framework.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 800 lists, as factors to be considered while planning and performing an audit of special purpose financial statements, compliance with all SAs relevant to the audit together with ethical requirements including independence, and the fact that the application of some SAs may require special consideration, the source's own illustration being that SA 320 judgments rest on the financial information needs of intended users. Statements 1, 2 and 3 reproduce those factors. Statement 4 is the trap: SA 800 deals with special considerations in the application of the 100-700 series SAs and therefore supplements them rather than displacing them, so the decisive word in Statement 4 is 'displaced'. Options containing Statement 4 (the second, third and fourth choices) are therefore wrong even though each of them also carries two correct statements.

questions.question:
Read the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) and select the correct option.
**Assertion (A):** In an audit of financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework, the auditor must comply with ethical requirements, including independence, in addition to complying with all SAs relevant to the audit.
**Reason (R):** Ethical requirements and the relevant SAs apply to such an audit only until the auditor decides to restrict the distribution of the auditor's report to the intended users, because a restricted report falls outside the scope of the SAs.
options: Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Assertion A states the requirement exactly as SA 800 frames it for planning and performing the audit: compliance with all SAs relevant to the audit and with ethical requirements including independence, with no conditional cut-off. Reason R is false. A restriction on the distribution or use of the report is a reporting device which limits who may use the report; it does not shrink the body of SAs the auditor must comply with, nor does it switch off independence. Since R is incorrect, the only tenable choice is that A is correct but R is incorrect. Candidates who equate 'restricted use' with 'reduced compliance' fall for the first two options, and the fourth option fails because A is plainly correct.

questions.question: CA Nivedita audits a cash basis statement of affairs prepared under the financial reporting provisions of a project grant, the intended users being the granting agency and the funding bank. For planning she fixes overall materiality at 0.5% of total expenditure shown in the entity's audited general purpose financial statements, explaining that this is the benchmark her firm uses for statutory audits of similar entities. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE observation on her approach?
options: It is acceptable, because SA 320 works through percentage benchmarks applied to a stable reported figure, and she has applied one consistently across similar engagements.
It is acceptable, because in a special purpose engagement materiality is what the auditor and the intended users mutually agree.
It is objectionable, because a special purpose financial statement must always carry materiality lower than that used for the general purpose financial statements.
It is objectionable, because under SA 800 the SA 320 judgments are to be based on the financial information needs of the intended users of the special purpose statement.
questions.explanation: SA 800 specifically warns that the application of some SAs requires special consideration in this setting and gives SA 320 as the example, the judgments being based on the financial information needs of intended users. The decisive fact is that the intended users here are the granting agency and the funding bank and the statement is a cash basis one, so anchoring the benchmark to the general purpose financial statements uses the wrong population. The first option mistakes mechanical consistency for the required user-based judgment; the second confuses an agreed no-correction threshold with the auditor's own determination of materiality; the third imports a rule of general comparative materiality which SA 800 does not state at this point, and 'always' makes it unacceptable in any event.

questions.question:
CASE: Vindhya Hi-Tech Limited prepares each year, under the financial reporting provisions of a loan agreement, a special purpose financial statement titled 'Contracted Cash Statement', presented on a prescribed cash basis, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with a debt-service coverage covenant. Northbridge Bank Limited, the sole lender, is the only intended user. CA Karthik Raman is the auditor of the Contracted Cash Statement. The following facts emerge during planning: (a) Management and Northbridge Bank have agreed in writing that misstatements identified in the Contracted Cash Statement below Rs. 7,00,000 will not be corrected, and management has asked CA Karthik to adopt that figure as the materiality for the audit. (b) Vindhya's Audit Committee, which oversees the preparation of the general purpose financial statements, has been discharged from this engagement, and a two-member 'Covenant Reporting Committee' of the Board oversees the preparation of the Contracted Cash Statement. (c) Management represents that, since a single cash basis statement is audited, SAs other than SA 700 are not relevant and no independence documentation need be obtained. (d) CA Karthik intends to state that his report is intended solely for Northbridge Bank and to restrict its distribution to that bank. (e) The engagement team includes a trainee who holds a small number of Vindhya's listed debentures, and the matter is referred to the firm's ethics partner.
With reference to fact (a) alone, which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion regarding materiality for this audit?
options: Materiality need not be determined at all, because management and the intended user have already fixed the amount below which misstatements will not be corrected.
The agreed threshold does not relieve CA Karthik of the requirement to determine materiality as per SA 320, which remains his own judgment.
Materiality should be adopted as Rs. 7,00,000, because an agreement between management and the intended user governs the reporting package.
Materiality should be determined under SA 320 by reference to the general purpose financial statements, because the agreed threshold concerns correction only.
questions.explanation: SA 800 states that where management may agree with intended users on a threshold below which identified misstatements will not be corrected, this does not relieve the auditor from the requirement to determine materiality as per SA 320. The decisive fact is that Rs. 7,00,000 is a correction threshold agreed between management and Northbridge Bank, whereas materiality is the auditor's own judgment, based on the financial information needs of the intended users. The first option treats the threshold as a substitute for materiality and so reverses the rule; the third treats a private commercial agreement as overriding professional judgment; the fourth accepts the requirement but anchors it to the wrong users, since the relevant needs are those of the users of the special purpose statement, not of the general purpose financial statements.

questions.question:
CASE: Vindhya Hi-Tech Limited prepares each year, under the financial reporting provisions of a loan agreement, a special purpose financial statement titled 'Contracted Cash Statement', presented on a prescribed cash basis, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with a debt-service coverage covenant. Northbridge Bank Limited, the sole lender, is the only intended user. CA Karthik Raman is the auditor of the Contracted Cash Statement. The following facts emerge during planning: (a) Management and Northbridge Bank have agreed in writing that misstatements identified in the Contracted Cash Statement below Rs. 7,00,000 will not be corrected, and management has asked CA Karthik to adopt that figure as the materiality for the audit. (b) Vindhya's Audit Committee, which oversees the preparation of the general purpose financial statements, has been discharged from this engagement, and a two-member 'Covenant Reporting Committee' of the Board oversees the preparation of the Contracted Cash Statement. (c) Management represents that, since a single cash basis statement is audited, SAs other than SA 700 are not relevant and no independence documentation need be obtained. (d) CA Karthik intends to state that his report is intended solely for Northbridge Bank and to restrict its distribution to that bank. (e) The engagement team includes a trainee who holds a small number of Vindhya's listed debentures, and the matter is referred to the firm's ethics partner.
Consider the statements framed on fact (b):
**Statement 1:** SA 260 requires communication with those charged with governance, and for the Contracted Cash Statement that oversight rests with the Covenant Reporting Committee, which need not be the body that oversees the general purpose financial statements.
**Statement 2:** Because the Contracted Cash Statement is prepared under a loan agreement, Northbridge Bank as the intended user replaces those charged with governance and receives the SA 260 communications.
**Statement 3:** A two-member committee cannot constitute governance, so no SA 260 communication is required in this engagement.
Which of these statements are correct?
options: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
questions.explanation: SA 260 requires the auditor to communicate with those charged with governance, and SA 800 adds that those responsible for oversight of the preparation of special purpose financial statements may not be the same as those responsible for the general purpose financial statements. The decisive fact is that the Board's Covenant Reporting Committee, not the discharged Audit Committee, oversees the Contracted Cash Statement, so it is the appropriate recipient. Statement 2 fails because an external intended user does not become those charged with governance merely because the framework flows from a contract; Statement 3 fails because SA 800 draws no distinction by the number of members of the oversight body, and the absence of the usual Audit Committee shifts the identity of the recipients rather than removing the duty.

questions.question:
CASE: Vindhya Hi-Tech Limited prepares each year, under the financial reporting provisions of a loan agreement, a special purpose financial statement titled 'Contracted Cash Statement', presented on a prescribed cash basis, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with a debt-service coverage covenant. Northbridge Bank Limited, the sole lender, is the only intended user. CA Karthik Raman is the auditor of the Contracted Cash Statement. The following facts emerge during planning: (a) Management and Northbridge Bank have agreed in writing that misstatements identified in the Contracted Cash Statement below Rs. 7,00,000 will not be corrected, and management has asked CA Karthik to adopt that figure as the materiality for the audit. (b) Vindhya's Audit Committee, which oversees the preparation of the general purpose financial statements, has been discharged from this engagement, and a two-member 'Covenant Reporting Committee' of the Board oversees the preparation of the Contracted Cash Statement. (c) Management represents that, since a single cash basis statement is audited, SAs other than SA 700 are not relevant and no independence documentation need be obtained. (d) CA Karthik intends to state that his report is intended solely for Northbridge Bank and to restrict its distribution to that bank. (e) The engagement team includes a trainee who holds a small number of Vindhya's listed debentures, and the matter is referred to the firm's ethics partner.
With reference to facts (c) and (e), which of the following actions should CA Karthik take?
**1:** Reject management's representation and comply with all SAs relevant to the audit of the Contracted Cash Statement, and not merely with SA 700.
**2:** Comply with ethical requirements including independence, and assess the trainee's debenture holding on that footing.
**3:** Set independence aside, because the only intended user, Northbridge Bank, is fully informed of the composition of the engagement team.
**4:** Apply only those SAs which the firm chooses to designate, since SA 800 lists these matters merely as factors to be considered.
options: 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 2 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The factors SA 800 requires the auditor to consider in planning and performing such an audit are compliance with all SAs relevant to the audit and with ethical requirements including independence; neither is qualified by the number of statements audited or by the identity of the users. The decisive facts are management's assertion in (c) that only SA 700 matters, which must be rejected because relevance of each SA is assessed on the engagement's circumstances and not by agreement with the client, and the debenture holding in (e), which must be evaluated under the ethical requirements that apply to this audit. Action 3 wrongly makes disclosure to the intended user a cure for an independence matter, and action 4 converts an objective relevance test into a firm preference.

questions.category: SA 800 – Restriction on Distribution or Use
questions.question:
CASE: Vindhya Hi-Tech Limited prepares each year, under the financial reporting provisions of a loan agreement, a special purpose financial statement titled 'Contracted Cash Statement', presented on a prescribed cash basis, for the purpose of demonstrating compliance with a debt-service coverage covenant. Northbridge Bank Limited, the sole lender, is the only intended user. CA Karthik Raman is the auditor of the Contracted Cash Statement. The following facts emerge during planning: (a) Management and Northbridge Bank have agreed in writing that misstatements identified in the Contracted Cash Statement below Rs. 7,00,000 will not be corrected, and management has asked CA Karthik to adopt that figure as the materiality for the audit. (b) Vindhya's Audit Committee, which oversees the preparation of the general purpose financial statements, has been discharged from this engagement, and a two-member 'Covenant Reporting Committee' of the Board oversees the preparation of the Contracted Cash Statement. (c) Management represents that, since a single cash basis statement is audited, SAs other than SA 700 are not relevant and no independence documentation need be obtained. (d) CA Karthik intends to state that his report is intended solely for Northbridge Bank and to restrict its distribution to that bank. (e) The engagement team includes a trainee who holds a small number of Vindhya's listed debentures, and the matter is referred to the firm's ethics partner.
CA Karthik now settles the wording of his report having regard to fact (d). Which of the following are appropriate actions?
**1:** Include a paragraph alerting users of the report that the Contracted Cash Statement is prepared in accordance with a special purpose framework and may not be suitable for another purpose, in an emphasis of matter paragraph.
**2:** Indicate that the report is intended only for Northbridge Bank, achieved by restricting the distribution or use of the report.
**3:** Expand the paragraph alerting readers to include the restriction on distribution or use, and modify its heading accordingly.
**4:** Omit the alerting paragraph, because distribution is already restricted to the single intended user named in the report.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: SA 800 treats alerting readers as mandatory, because special purpose financial statements may be used for other purposes, and treats a restriction on distribution or use as an option the auditor may exercise. Where the restriction is exercised, the source permits the paragraph alerting readers to be expanded to include those other matters and the heading to be modified accordingly, which is exactly what actions 1, 2 and 3 do. The decisive fact is that a restriction limits who may use the report but does not answer the question whether a reader who does obtain it understands the basis of preparation, so action 4 wrongly treats a permissive step as displacing a mandatory one.

questions.question:
CASE: Meridian Capital Services Limited is regulated by a sectoral regulator whose financial reporting provisions require such entities to prepare a 'Regulatory Capital Adequacy Statement' on a prescribed special purpose basis and to place that statement, together with the auditor's report, on public record. The regulator is the intended user; the statement is not prepared to meet the needs of shareholders or of the general public, though members of the public may read it because it is publicly filed. CA Farida Mulla audits the statement. Her draft report describes the purpose for which the statement is prepared, names the regulator as the intended user, records her evaluation that the statement adequately describes the applicable financial reporting framework, and expresses an unmodified opinion. She deliberately excludes any paragraph alerting readers to the special purpose basis, reasoning that the regulator itself mandated that basis and that naming the intended user is sufficient. Separately, Ashwin Holdings Limited files an identical statement with the regulator alone, and its auditor alerts readers in an emphasis of matter paragraph and adds to that same paragraph an indication that the report is intended solely for the regulator, with the heading of the paragraph modified to reflect that addition.
With reference to CA Farida's draft report, which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE criticism?
options: No criticism is warranted, because naming the regulator as the intended user in the report itself tells every reader the use for which the statement was prepared.
She should restrict distribution of the report to the regulator, after which the alerting paragraph becomes unnecessary.
Alerting readers is mandatory; she must state in an emphasis of matter paragraph that the statement is prepared under a special purpose framework and may not be suitable for another purpose.
She should describe the purpose for which the statement is prepared and the intended users instead of adding an emphasis of matter paragraph, the two requirements being alternatives to each other.
questions.explanation: The alerting-readers requirement is stated as mandatory precisely because special purpose financial statements may be used for other purposes, and the source's own illustration is a regulator requiring certain entities to place special purpose financial statements on public record, which is the present fact pattern. The decisive fact is that the general public may read a statement filed on public record although the regulator alone is the intended user, so the alert against unsuitable use must appear in an emphasis of matter paragraph. The first and fourth options substitute the separate SA 700 requirement of describing the purpose and intended users for the alert, which is not an alternative to it; the second is unavailable because a public record filing cannot be reconciled with restricting distribution, and a restriction would in any event not remove the mandatory alert.

questions.question:
CASE: Meridian Capital Services Limited is regulated by a sectoral regulator whose financial reporting provisions require such entities to prepare a 'Regulatory Capital Adequacy Statement' on a prescribed special purpose basis and to place that statement, together with the auditor's report, on public record. The regulator is the intended user; the statement is not prepared to meet the needs of shareholders or of the general public, though members of the public may read it because it is publicly filed. CA Farida Mulla audits the statement. Her draft report describes the purpose for which the statement is prepared, names the regulator as the intended user, records her evaluation that the statement adequately describes the applicable financial reporting framework, and expresses an unmodified opinion. She deliberately excludes any paragraph alerting readers to the special purpose basis, reasoning that the regulator itself mandated that basis and that naming the intended user is sufficient. Separately, Ashwin Holdings Limited files an identical statement with the regulator alone, and its auditor alerts readers in an emphasis of matter paragraph and adds to that same paragraph an indication that the report is intended solely for the regulator, with the heading of the paragraph modified to reflect that addition.
Consider the statements drawn from the case:
**Statement 1:** In forming an opinion and reporting on the Regulatory Capital Adequacy Statement, CA Farida shall apply the requirements in SA 700.
**Statement 2:** SA 700 requires her to evaluate whether the statement adequately describes the applicable financial reporting framework.
**Statement 3:** The auditor's report shall also describe the purpose for which the statement is prepared and the intended users.
**Statement 4:** Because the framework is a special purpose one, the description of purpose and intended users in her draft report is an optional courtesy rather than a requirement.
Which of these statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 800 requires the auditor forming an opinion on and reporting special purpose financial statements to apply the requirements of SA 700, and it identifies two specific consequences: the SA 700 evaluation of whether the financial statements adequately describe the applicable financial reporting framework, and the requirement that the auditor's report also describe the purpose for which the statements are prepared and the intended users. Statements 1, 2 and 3 correspond to those requirements and are what CA Farida's draft report correctly does. Statement 4 is wrong: the description of purpose and intended users is mandatory in this setting, and it is the alerting-readers emphasis of matter paragraph, not this description, that she has omitted. Any option carrying Statement 4 must therefore be rejected.

questions.question:
CASE: Meridian Capital Services Limited is regulated by a sectoral regulator whose financial reporting provisions require such entities to prepare a 'Regulatory Capital Adequacy Statement' on a prescribed special purpose basis and to place that statement, together with the auditor's report, on public record. The regulator is the intended user; the statement is not prepared to meet the needs of shareholders or of the general public, though members of the public may read it because it is publicly filed. CA Farida Mulla audits the statement. Her draft report describes the purpose for which the statement is prepared, names the regulator as the intended user, records her evaluation that the statement adequately describes the applicable financial reporting framework, and expresses an unmodified opinion. She deliberately excludes any paragraph alerting readers to the special purpose basis, reasoning that the regulator itself mandated that basis and that naming the intended user is sufficient. Separately, Ashwin Holdings Limited files an identical statement with the regulator alone, and its auditor alerts readers in an emphasis of matter paragraph and adds to that same paragraph an indication that the report is intended solely for the regulator, with the heading of the paragraph modified to reflect that addition.
Take CA Farida's facts as the base and change one fact: assume the regulator requires no public filing, so that Ashwin Holdings files its statement with the regulator alone and its auditor restricts distribution and use of the report to the regulator. Compared with CA Farida's position, what changes for that auditor?
options: The obligation to alert readers continues, but that paragraph may be expanded to include the restriction on distribution or use, and its heading modified accordingly.
The obligation to alert readers ceases, because no person other than the intended user can obtain the report.
The alerting paragraph becomes discretionary and, if included, must retain its original heading.
Nothing changes at all, because a restriction on the distribution or use of the report is dealt with wholly separately from the paragraph alerting readers to the special purpose framework.
questions.explanation: The two cells must be read together. Alerting readers is mandatory, because special purpose financial statements may be used for other purposes, and that obligation is not switched off by the auditor's decision to restrict distribution; restricting distribution is the permissive step, by which the auditor may indicate that the report is intended only for specific users. The change brought by that permissive step is one of content and presentation: the paragraph alerting readers may be expanded to include these other matters and the heading modified accordingly, which is what Ashwin's auditor did. The decisive fact is the mandatory permissive asymmetry, so the second and third options wrongly downgrade a mandatory requirement, and the fourth wrongly denies any effect on the alerting paragraph or its heading.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements on the SA 800 requirements relating to alerting readers of the auditor's report on special purpose financial statements and to restricting the distribution or use of that report:
**Statement 1:** Alerting readers is mandatory, whereas indicating that the report is intended only for specific users is left to the auditor's option.
**Statement 2:** The illustration given for the need to alert readers is a regulator requiring certain entities to place special purpose financial statements on public record.
**Statement 3:** Where the auditor restricts distribution or use, the paragraph alerting readers must be deleted and replaced by a new paragraph placed under the opinion heading.
**Statement 4:** A restriction on distribution or use by itself discharges the requirement to alert readers, because no other person can obtain the report.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the source heads alerting readers as mandatory while the restriction on distribution or use is expressed as something the auditor may indicate, and the public record illustration is exactly the one stated. Statement 3 is not correct, because restriction does not delete the alert; the paragraph alerting readers may be expanded to include those other matters and the heading modified accordingly. Statement 4 is not correct, because a restriction limits the class of users and cannot cure the risk that a statement prepared under a special purpose framework is used for a purpose for which it may not be suitable. The last option is incomplete because it exempts Statement 3, which is equally wrong, and the first option lists the two correct statements.

questions.question:
Match each situation in Column I with the consequence in Column II that follows under SA 800.
**Column I**
A. A regulator requires an entity to place its special purpose financial statements on public record.
B. The auditor decides to indicate that the report is intended only for specified users and to restrict its distribution.
C. Management agrees with the intended users that misstatements below a stated amount will not be corrected.
D. The persons responsible for oversight of the preparation of the special purpose financial statements differ from those responsible for the general purpose financial statements.
**Column II**
1. The paragraph alerting readers may be expanded to include those matters and its heading modified accordingly.
2. The auditor shall alert users, in an emphasis of matter paragraph, that the statements are prepared under a special purpose framework and may not be suitable for another purpose.
3. SA 260 communications are directed to the persons responsible for oversight of the special purpose financial statements.
4. The auditor is not relieved of the requirement to determine materiality as per SA 320.
questions.explanation: A public record filing is the source's illustration of the risk that special purpose financial statements are used for another purpose, which triggers the mandatory emphasis of matter alert, so A pairs with 2. B is the permissive restriction, whose stated effect is that the alerting paragraph may be expanded and its heading modified, so B pairs with 1. An agreed no-correction threshold does not relieve the auditor of determining materiality under SA 320, so C pairs with 4. Because SA 260 communication is with those charged with governance and that oversight may rest with different persons for special purpose statements, D pairs with 3. The distractors mainly interchange A with B, which is the common error of treating the mandatory alert as the flexible item and the restriction as the fixed one.

questions.category: SA 800 – Restriction on Distribution or Use
questions.question: Rathi Spinning Mills Limited prepares a 'Working Capital Funds Statement' in the form required by the financial reporting provisions of its term loan with a consortium of four banks. At the consortium's request, the auditor states that the report is intended solely for the consortium members and restricts its distribution to them. His report also describes the purpose for which the statement is prepared and identifies the consortium as the intended users, and it contains a paragraph, headed to reflect both matters, stating that the statement is prepared in accordance with a special purpose framework and may not be suitable for another purpose and that distribution of the report is restricted to the consortium. Which of the following is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion on his report?
options: It is defective, because the paragraph alerting readers may deal with no matter other than the special purpose framework, and the restriction must find its place elsewhere in the report.
It is defective, because a restriction on distribution can be conveyed only in the opinion paragraph.
It is appropriate only if the description of purpose and intended users is dropped, since that description cannot coexist with a restriction.

It is appropriate, because alerting readers is mandatory and, where distribution or use is restricted, the alerting paragraph may be expanded to include those matters with the heading modified accordingly.
questions.explanation: Two requirements operate together here: the mandatory alert that the statement is prepared under a special purpose framework and may not be suitable for another purpose, and the permissive indication that the report is intended only for specified users, achieved by restricting distribution or use. The source expressly allows, in the restricted case, the paragraph alerting readers to be expanded to include those other matters and the heading to be modified accordingly, which is what the auditor has done while retaining the mandatory alert and the description of purpose and intended users. The decisive fact is that the alert survives the restriction rather than being replaced by it. The first two options invent prohibitions the standard does not contain, and the third wrongly treats a mandatory reporting element as inconsistent with a restriction.

questions.question:
CASE: Samarth Infra Limited prepares a special purpose statement under the financial reporting provisions of a project grant, the intended users being the granting state agency and the bank financing the project. CA Iyer audits the statement and issues a report which describes the purpose of the statement, identifies those two intended users and includes the mandatory paragraph alerting readers that the statement is prepared under a special purpose framework and may not be suitable for another purpose. Six months later, without informing CA Iyer, management circulates the audited statement to prospective equity investors as part of an investor presentation. When CA Iyer objects, management asks him to withdraw the alerting paragraph, arguing that it depresses investor interest and that the intended users were named in the report in any event.
Which of the following actions should CA Iyer take?
**1:** Decline to withdraw the paragraph, because alerting readers is mandatory and special purpose financial statements may be used for other purposes.
**2:** Explain that the alert exists precisely to avoid misunderstandings where such statements may not be suitable for another purpose, and that naming the intended users does not achieve this.
**3:** Accept a written representation from management that equity investors will correctly understand the basis of preparation, in substitution for the paragraph.
**4:** Consider indicating that the report is intended only for specified users and restricting its distribution or use, in which case the alerting paragraph may be expanded and its heading modified accordingly.
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The circulation to prospective equity investors is exactly the contingency the alert addresses, since the source states that special purpose financial statements may be used for other purposes and requires the auditor to alert users in an emphasis of matter paragraph that the statements may not be suitable for another purpose. The decisive fact is that the statements have in fact moved into the hands of users who are neither of the named intended users, so the alert must remain and Action 3's representation cannot substitute for a reporting requirement. Action 2 correctly rejects the argument that naming intended users is sufficient, because that is a separate SA 700 requirement. Action 4 is available to him as a permissive step and would let him expand the paragraph and modify its heading, but it does not remove the mandatory alert.

questions.question:
Read the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) and select the correct option.
**Assertion (A):** While forming an opinion on and reporting financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework, the auditor shall apply the requirements of SA 700.
**Reason (R):** SA 700 requires the auditor to evaluate whether the financial statements adequately describe the applicable financial reporting framework.
options: Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct as the source frames them: SA 800 requires the auditor forming an opinion and reporting on special purpose financial statements to apply the requirements of SA 700, and it identifies the SA 700 evaluation of whether the financial statements adequately describe the applicable financial reporting framework as one of the matters so imported. R does not, however, explain A. R is one content requirement within SA 700, whereas A is the direction that SA 700 governs the opinion and reporting phase; a requirement found inside SA 700 cannot be the reason for applying SA 700. This is the classic assertion-reason trap in which two true statements are offered with a causal link asserted that is not present, so the first option must be resisted.

questions.question:
Case: Kolhapur Tool Room Ltd asks its statutory auditor, Ritesh Jain & Co., to also express an opinion, for the sanctioning authority of a project grant, on a schedule of tangible assets purchased under that grant. The schedule has been compiled on the cash-disbursement basis prescribed in the grant sanction and not on the accrual basis used in the company's general purpose financial statements. The same firm is separately asked to express an opinion on the company's statement of cash flows for the year, prepared under the general purpose framework.
Ritesh Jain records in his planning note: 'SA 805 concerns special considerations in applying the SAs of the 100-700 series to such engagements, and the framework on which the subject matter is prepared makes no difference to the standards that apply.'
Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** SA 805 deals with special considerations in applying the SAs in the 100-700 series to the audit of a single financial statement or of a specific element, account or item of a financial statement.
**Statement 2:** Such a single financial statement or element may be prepared under a general purpose or a special purpose framework, and where it is prepared under a special purpose framework, SA B00 also applies.
**Statement 3:** The statement of cash flows is a single financial statement, which SA 805 treats as different from a complete set of financial statements.
**Statement 4:** Ritesh Jain is right that the framework applied has no bearing on the standards applicable to such an engagement.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1 and 2 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
All of the above
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: SA 805 prescribes special considerations in applying the SAs of the 100-700 series to an audit of a single financial statement or of a specific element, account or item of a financial statement, so Statement 1 is right. Statements 2 and 3 follow from the same source: the subject matter may be prepared under either a general or a special purpose framework, and where a special purpose framework is used SA B00 also applies; the source also illustrates the cash flow statement as a single financial statement which is different from a complete set of financial statements. Statement 4 is therefore wrong, because the decisive fact in the case is that the grant schedule is compiled on a cash-disbursement (special purpose) basis, which brings SA B00 into play, while the general purpose statement of cash flows is not. The framework is thus relevant to which additional SA applies, but not to whether SA 805 applies at all.

questions.category: SA 805 – Single FS vs Special Purpose Framework
questions.question:
Case: Two banks approach CA Ananya Rao in the same week. Bank A asks her to audit and report on the statement of cash flows of Kaveri Agro Products Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X4, that statement being prepared under the company's general purpose framework but a separate opinion being sought on it alone. Bank B asks her to audit and report on cash flow information of the same company, prepared on the cash basis of accounting specially for its creditors. Ananya's articles clerk notes in the acceptance file: 'Both requests are the same thing under different labels - cash in and cash out - so both are single financial statements.'
Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** Bank A's request concerns a single financial statement.
**Statement 2:** Bank B's request concerns information prepared under a special purpose framework, so SA B00 also applies.
**Statement 3:** The articles clerk is right that the two requests are the same in substance.
**Statement 4:** The cash and bank balances of Kaveri Agro would, if reported on separately, be a specific element, account or item rather than a single financial statement.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: SA 805 gives the cash flow statement as its example of a single financial statement, so a separate opinion on the general purpose statement of cash flows sought by Bank A is an engagement on a single financial statement and Statement 1 is right. Bank B's subject matter is cash flow information drawn up on the cash basis for creditors, which is a special purpose framework; SA 805 states that where a single financial statement or a specific element is prepared under a special purpose framework, SA B00 also applies, so Statement 2 is right. The two requests differ in kind and not merely in label: one concerns a statement that would form part of a complete set, the other concerns information prepared for specific users on a framework designed to meet their needs, which is why Statement 3 is wrong. Statement 4 is also correct, because cash and bank balances are listed by the source as a specific element, account or item of a financial statement and not as a single financial statement.

questions.question:
Match the following engagement subject matters (Column I) with their correct classification under SA 805 (Column II).
**Column I:**
(A) Statement of cash flows of a company on which a separate opinion is sought
(B) Cash and bank balances of the same company
(C) Schedule of tangible assets of the same company
(D) The balance sheet, statement of profit and loss, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows and notes forming part thereof, taken together
**Column II:**
(1) A single financial statement
(2) A specific element, account or item of a financial statement
(3) A complete set of financial statements, and therefore neither a single financial statement nor a specific element
questions.explanation: SA 805 draws a line between a single financial statement and a specific element, account or item, and states that a single financial statement is different from a complete set of financial statements. The source's own example of a single financial statement is the cash flow statement, so (A) pairs with (1), while (D), which takes the statements and the notes forming part thereof together, is a complete set and pairs with (3). Cash and bank balances and a schedule of tangible assets are both listed in the source as examples of specific elements, accounts or items, so (B) and (C) pair with (2). The tempting errors are to reason from the word 'cash' that cash and bank balances are themselves a single financial statement, or from the word 'schedule' that a schedule of tangible assets is a statement; the classification turns on whether the subject matter is an entire statement or a component of one.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding specific elements, accounts or items of financial statements on which an audit opinion may be expressed under SA 805:
**Statement 1:** The recorded value of identified intangible assets is an example of a specific element, account or item of a financial statement.
**Statement 2:** Allowance for doubtful debts is an example of a specific element, account or item of a financial statement.
**Statement 3:** A schedule of externally managed assets and income of a private pension plan is an example of a specific element, account or item of a financial statement.
**Statement 4:** A schedule of disbursements in relation to a lease property can be reported on only where the arrangement is a finance lease in the books of the lessor.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: The source lists the recorded value of identified intangible assets, allowance for doubtful debts, trade receivable, cash and bank balances and inventory as examples of specific elements, accounts or items, and separately lists a schedule of externally managed assets and income of a private pension plan and a schedule of tangible assets, so Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Statement 4 imports a condition the source does not state: the schedule of disbursements in relation to a lease property is given as an example without any classification of the lease, and the accounting character of the lease does not decide whether the subject matter is a specific element of a financial statement. Candidates who discard the pension plan schedule or the lease property schedule because they sit outside an ordinary company balance sheet miss precisely the two illustrations the source is concerned to give.

questions.question:
Case: CA Nikhil Shah is approached in the same month by three parties. The trustees of a private pension plan of a manufacturing group want an opinion on the schedule of externally managed assets and income of that plan. An entity that has given a warehouse on lease wants an opinion on the schedule of disbursements made in relation to that lease property. An asset-holding company wants an opinion on a schedule of its tangible assets. A colleague objects: 'SA 805 covers only trade receivables, cash and bank balances, allowance for doubtful debts, inventory and intangible assets. These three schedules are not financial statements or elements of financial statements, so no SA 805 engagement is possible.'
Which of the following is the most appropriate response to the colleague?
options: The colleague is right, because the illustrations under SA 805 are confined to items appearing as a caption in a balance sheet or in a statement of profit and loss.

The colleague is wrong: the source itself lists the pension plan schedule of externally managed assets and income, the schedule of tangible assets and the lease property disbursement schedule as specific elements, accounts or items.
The colleague is wrong, but only the pension plan schedule qualifies, since the other two are single financial statements.
The colleague is right that these three fall outside SA 805, but each of them is instead a single financial statement.
questions.explanation: The illustrations of specific elements, accounts or items under SA 805 go well beyond line items of a balance sheet: the source lists a schedule of externally managed assets and income of a private pension plan, a schedule of tangible assets and a schedule of disbursements in relation to a lease property alongside trade receivables, cash and bank balances, allowance for doubtful debts, inventory and the recorded value of identified intangible assets. The decisive point is that the subject matter is a specific element, account or item of a financial statement, not whether it appears as a caption in a primary statement of a general purpose set. Option 3 misclassifies two of the schedules as single financial statements; a single financial statement is an entire statement such as the cash flow statement, which is a different category. Option 4 compounds both errors, and option 1 restates the colleague's unduly narrow reading.

questions.category: SA 805 – Compliance with All Relevant SAs
questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Where a firm audits the complete set of financial statements of a company and is also engaged to express an opinion on a schedule of its inventory, the firm may rely on the compliance achieved in the complete-set audit and need not separately comply with the SAs relevant to the inventory engagement.
**Reason (R):** In an engagement covered by SA 805, the auditor shall comply with all SAs relevant to the audit even if the auditor is also engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The assertion states the opposite of the source requirement, while the reason reproduces it: in such an engagement the auditor shall comply with all SAs relevant to the audit even if the auditor is also engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements. The engagement on the inventory schedule therefore carries its own compliance obligation and options 1 and 2 fail because A is not correct. Option 3 fails because R is precisely the requirement stated by the source. The decisive point is the 'even if' clause: being the complete-set auditor removes the practicability determination that SA 805 requires of an auditor who is not engaged for the complete set, but it does not dilute the obligation to comply with all relevant SAs.

questions.category: SA 805 – Compliance with All Relevant SAs
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about an engagement to report on a single financial statement or on a specific element, account or item of a financial statement:
**Statement 1:** The auditor shall comply with all SAs relevant to the audit whether or not the auditor is also engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements.
**Statement 2:** The requirement to determine whether the engagement, performed as per the SAs, is practicable applies even where the auditor is also engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements.
**Statement 3:** Where the same firm audits the complete set, the practicability determination contemplated by SA 805 is not triggered for the engagement on the single financial statement or element.
**Statement 4:** An auditor who is not engaged to audit the complete set may accept a single financial statement engagement without judging whether an audit as per the SAs is practicable.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
Statements 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct, since compliance with all relevant SAs is required even if the auditor also audits the complete set. Statements 2 and 4 misstate the conditional trigger: the source requires the auditor to determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable where the auditor is not engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements, which makes Statement 3 correct and Statements 2 and 4 not correct. The decisive distinction is between two different obligations - an unconditional obligation to comply with all relevant SAs, and a practicability determination arising only in the single-statement-only or element-only situation. Since the question asks for the statements that are not correct, the answer is Statements 2 and 4 only, and options that include Statements 1 or 3 cannot be right.

questions.question:
Case: CA Raghav Batra, partner of Raghav Batra & Co., is approached by Nandan Retail Ltd to express an audit opinion on the company's trade receivables as at 31 March 20X4, aggregating Rs. 148 crore out of total assets of Rs. 640 crore. The statutory audit of the complete set of financial statements for 20X3-24 has been accepted by CA Suresh Menon & Associates, and Nandan Retail confirms that Raghav Batra & Co. will not be engaged for that audit. The receivables schedule is prepared on the same recognition and measurement basis that the company applies in its general purpose financial statements.
