The opinion is needed principally to satisfy a lending consortium that has sanctioned a Rs. 200 crore working capital facility. Raghav Batra has no previous connection with the company, has not studied its business, its accounting systems or its internal control, and has not seen the workings of the allowance for doubtful debts. The finance director tells him: 'Verify only our aged-debtor listing and the balance confirmations we already hold; you are looking at one line, so this is a small job needing no planning.'
Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** Raghav Batra shall determine whether the engagement, performed as per the SAs, is practicable, because he is not engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements.
**Statement 2:** Since the finance director has offered the aged-debtor listing and confirmations, Raghav Batra may limit his compliance to those procedures.
**Statement 3:** If Raghav Batra concludes that the engagement may not be practicable, he may discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable.
**Statement 4:** Because the receivables schedule is prepared under a general purpose framework, the acceptance considerations of SA 805 do not apply.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Raghav Batra is expressly not engaged for the complete set, so the source requires him to determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable, and it permits him to discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable if he concludes that it may not be; Statements 1 and 3 are therefore correct. Statement 2 fails because in such an engagement the auditor shall comply with all SAs relevant to the audit, and management's offer of a listing and some confirmations cannot narrow that obligation or excuse planning. Statement 4 confuses two ideas: the framework decides whether SA B00 also applies, not whether SA 805's acceptance considerations apply, and this schedule is on the general purpose basis in any event. The Rs. 148 crore size of the balance and the lending consortium's purpose are relevant background but neither creates nor removes the practicability determination.

questions.question:
Case: CA Raghav Batra, partner of Raghav Batra & Co., is approached by Nandan Retail Ltd to express an audit opinion on the company's trade receivables as at 31 March 20X4, aggregating Rs. 148 crore out of total assets of Rs. 640 crore. The statutory audit of the complete set of financial statements for 20X3-24 has been accepted by CA Suresh Menon & Associates, and Nandan Retail confirms that Raghav Batra & Co. will not be engaged for that audit. The receivables schedule is prepared on the same recognition and measurement basis that the company applies in its general purpose financial statements. The opinion is needed principally to satisfy a lending consortium that has sanctioned a Rs. 200 crore working capital facility. Raghav Batra has no previous connection with the company, has not studied its business, its accounting systems or its internal control, and has not seen the workings of the allowance for doubtful debts. The finance director tells him: 'Verify only our aged-debtor listing and the balance confirmations we already hold; you are looking at one line, so this is a small job needing no planning.'
Which of the following actions should Raghav Batra take in deciding whether to accept this engagement?
**Action 1:** Consider whether he has the same understanding of the entity and its environment, including its internal control, as an auditor who also audits the complete set of financial statements.
**Action 2:** Consider whether he may need further evidence to corroborate the audit evidence acquired from the accounting records.
**Action 3:** Treat the appointment of CA Suresh Menon & Associates for the complete set as removing any need to judge whether his own engagement is practicable.
**Action 4:** If he concludes that the engagement may not be practicable, explore with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable.
options: Actions 1, 3 and 4 only
Actions 2 and 3 only
Actions 1, 2 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: The source identifies two reasons why such an engagement may not be practicable: the auditor often does not have the same understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, as an auditor who also audits the complete set, and the auditor may need further evidence to corroborate audit evidence acquired from the accounting records. Actions 1 and 2 apply those two reasons to Raghav Batra, who has never studied Nandan Retail's business, systems, controls or the workings of the allowance for doubtful debts, so that what he has are balances taken straight out of the records. Action 4 is the permitted consequence of a conclusion that the engagement may not be practicable. Action 3 is wrong because the practicability determination arises precisely because he is not the complete-set auditor; the other firm's appointment triggers the judgment instead of excusing it.

questions.question:
Case: CA Raghav Batra, partner of Raghav Batra & Co., is approached by Nandan Retail Ltd to express an audit opinion on the company's trade receivables as at 31 March 20X4, aggregating Rs. 148 crore out of total assets of Rs. 640 crore. The statutory audit of the complete set of financial statements for 20X3-24 has been accepted by CA Suresh Menon & Associates, and Nandan Retail confirms that Raghav Batra & Co. will not be engaged for that audit. The receivables schedule is prepared on the same recognition and measurement basis that the company applies in its general purpose financial statements. The opinion is needed principally to satisfy a lending consortium that has sanctioned a Rs. 200 crore working capital facility. Raghav Batra has no previous connection with the company, has not studied its business, its accounting systems or its internal control, and has not seen the workings of the allowance for doubtful debts. The finance director tells him: 'Verify only our aged-debtor listing and the balance confirmations we already hold; you are looking at one line, so this is a small job needing no planning.'
Assume now that Nandan Retail withdraws the other appointment and engages Raghav Batra & Co. to audit the complete set of financial statements for 20X3-24 as well as to express an opinion on the trade receivables. Which of the following most appropriately describes the change in Raghav Batra's position under SA 805?
options: He must still comply with all SAs relevant to the receivables engagement, but the practicability determination, which arises only where the auditor is not engaged to audit the complete set, is no longer triggered.
He need no longer comply with the SAs on the receivables engagement, because the complete-set audit already covers the same accounting records.
He must still determine whether the receivables engagement is practicable, because the receivables schedule is prepared under a general purpose framework.
He may restrict the receivables engagement to the aged-debtor listing, because the understanding of internal control obtained for the complete set is the only SA relevant to an element.
questions.explanation: The single fact that changes is that the firm is now also engaged to audit the complete set. The source requires compliance with all SAs relevant to the audit even where the auditor is also engaged to audit the complete set, so that obligation is untouched by the change. The practicability determination, by contrast, is expressed as a requirement applying where the auditor is not engaged to audit the complete set, so it ceases to be triggered, and the reason is apparent on these facts - the firm will now possess the understanding of the entity, its environment and its internal control that was earlier missing. Options 2 and 4 ignore the 'even if' obligation, and option 3 wrongly ties the determination to the reporting framework rather than to whether the complete set is being audited.

questions.question:
Case: KHV & Co. is asked by Veerappa Spinning Mills Ltd to express an audit opinion, as at 31 March 20X4, on (a) the company's cash and bank balances of Rs. 42 crore and (b) its inventory of Rs. 96 crore. The complete set of financial statements is audited by another firm and KHV & Co. is not, and will not be, engaged for that audit. KHV & Co. has never audited the company and has no understanding of its environment, its information technology systems or its internal control, including its physical verification of inventory and its controls over bank reconciliations. The books show 31 bank accounts across 14 centres and inventory held at 9 warehouses. The firm's audit manager writes in the acceptance note: 'The books of account will give us the balances, and a bank confirmation plus a signed stock statement will corroborate them, so the absence of any understanding of internal control is immaterial in an element-level engagement.'
Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The absence of the same understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, as an auditor who also audits the complete set is a reason identified by SA 805 why such an engagement may not be practicable.
**Statement 2:** KHV & Co. is required to comply with all SAs relevant to the audit of these two elements only if it is also engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements.
**Statement 3:** KHV & Co. may need further evidence to corroborate the audit evidence acquired from the accounting records.
**Statement 4:** If KHV & Co. concludes that the engagement may not be practicable, it may discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 restate the two reasons the source gives for such an engagement often not being practicable: the missing understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, and the possible need for further evidence to corroborate audit evidence acquired from the accounting records. Statement 4 is correct because the source permits the auditor, on concluding that the engagement may not be practicable, to discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable. Statement 2 is wrong: compliance with all relevant SAs is required in such an engagement irrespective of whether the auditor also audits the complete set, the 'even if' clause widening rather than narrowing the obligation. The manager's note is therefore incomplete - confirmations bear on corroboration but say nothing about the control understanding over inventory at 9 warehouses and 31 bank accounts across 14 centres.

questions.question:
Case: KHV & Co. is asked by Veerappa Spinning Mills Ltd to express an audit opinion, as at 31 March 20X4, on (a) the company's cash and bank balances of Rs. 42 crore and (b) its inventory of Rs. 96 crore. The complete set of financial statements is audited by another firm and KHV & Co. is not, and will not be, engaged for that audit. KHV & Co. has never audited the company and has no understanding of its environment, its information technology systems or its internal control, including its physical verification of inventory and its controls over bank reconciliations. The books show 31 bank accounts across 14 centres and inventory held at 9 warehouses. The firm's audit manager writes in the acceptance note: 'The books of account will give us the balances, and a bank confirmation plus a signed stock statement will corroborate them, so the absence of any understanding of internal control is immaterial in an element-level engagement.'
Which one of the following is the most appropriate evaluation of the audit manager's acceptance note?
options: The note is correct, because third-party corroboration of recorded balances is all that an element-level engagement requires.
The note is correct in substance, because the practicability determination applies only where the element is prepared under a special purpose framework.

The note overlooks that, not being engaged for the complete set, the firm shall determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable, and the missing understanding of internal control is a stated reason why it may not be.
The note overlooks that the firm must first discuss with management whether another type of engagement would be more practicable, before judging practicability.
questions.explanation: Because KHV & Co. is not and will not be engaged to audit the complete set, the source requires it to determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable, and it identifies the absence of the same understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, as a reason why it may not be. The manager's note speaks only to corroboration of balances recorded in the books and treats the internal control gap as immaterial, which is exactly the consideration the source says must inform the determination over inventory at 9 warehouses and 31 bank accounts across 14 centres. Options 1 and 2 wrongly accept the note, and option 2 also invents a framework condition that the source does not attach to the determination. Option 4 reverses the sequence, since the discussion with management about another type of engagement is what the auditor may do after concluding that the engagement may not be practicable.

questions.question:
Case: CA Shalini Kulkarni receives a letter asking her to express an audit opinion on the inventory of a company whose complete set of financial statements will be audited by another firm; she is not in contention for that audit.
Arrange the following steps in the order in which SA 805 contemplates them.
**P.** Discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable.
**Q.** Determine whether the engagement, performed as per the SAs, is practicable.
**R.** Consider whether she has the same understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, as an auditor who also audits the complete set, and whether further evidence may be needed to corroborate audit evidence acquired from the accounting records.
**S.** Record that she is not engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements.
options: S, Q, P, R
S, R, Q, P
Q, S, P, R
R, S, P, Q
questions.explanation: The chain begins with the condition that starts the analysis, namely that the auditor is not engaged to audit the complete set of financial statements. The source then supplies the content of that judgment - whether the auditor has the same understanding of the entity and its environment, including internal control, as an auditor who also audits the complete set, and whether further evidence may be needed to corroborate evidence acquired from the accounting records - and these must be weighed before a determination on practicability can be reached. The discussion with management about another type of engagement is expressly conditional on the auditor concluding that the engagement may not be practicable, so it follows the determination and cannot precede it. Sequences which place P before Q or before R reverse this conditional order, and a sequence which places S last cannot be right because the absent complete-set engagement is the trigger.

questions.question:
Case: CA Imtiaz Sohoni & Co. receives four invitation letters in July 20X4. Letter 1, from the trustees of a private pension plan of a client, seeks an opinion on the schedule of externally managed assets and income of the plan. Letter 2, from an aircraft lessor, seeks an opinion on the schedule of disbursements in relation to a lease property. Letter 3, from an e-commerce company, seeks an opinion on its allowance for doubtful debts of Rs. 214 crore; the audit of the complete set is with another firm and Imtiaz Sohoni & Co. is not engaged for it. Letter 4, from a software exporter, seeks an opinion on its statement of cash flows; Imtiaz Sohoni & Co. is also the statutory auditor of the complete set of that company. Letters 1 and 3 happen to be signed by the same individual, a coincidence the partner notices but which has no bearing on either engagement.
Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** Letters 1, 2 and 3 relate to specific elements, accounts or items of financial statements, while Letter 4 relates to a single financial statement.
**Statement 2:** For Letter 3 the firm shall determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable.
**Statement 3:** For Letter 4 the firm need not comply with the SAs relevant to the statement of cash flows engagement because it already audits the complete set.
**Statement 4:** Where the subject matter of such an engagement is prepared under a special purpose framework, SA B00 also applies.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: Statements 1, 2 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1, 2, 3 and 4
questions.explanation: The pension plan schedule of externally managed assets and income, the lease property disbursement schedule and the allowance for doubtful debts are all illustrations the source gives of specific elements, accounts or items, whereas the statement of cash flows is its illustration of a single financial statement, so Statement 1 is correct and the common signatory is deliberately irrelevant. Statement 2 follows from the conditional requirement to determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable where the auditor is not engaged to audit the complete set, which is true of Letter 3 on these facts. Statement 3 is wrong because the auditor shall comply with all SAs relevant to the audit even if also engaged to audit the complete set, so the software exporter engagement carries its own compliance obligation. Statement 4 is correct: the subject matter may be prepared under a general or a special purpose framework, and SA B00 applies additionally when it is special.

questions.question:
Consider the following four separate engagements of CA Praveen Iyer and match each situation in Column I with the correct requirement in Column II.
**Column I:**
(A) Praveen is engaged to report on the inventory of a company and is also engaged to audit the complete set of its financial statements.
(B) Praveen is engaged to report on the recorded value of identified intangible assets of a company and is not engaged to audit the complete set.
(C) The subject matter of one of Praveen's engagements is prepared under a special purpose framework rather than a general purpose framework.
(D) Praveen concludes that the engagement on a schedule of tangible assets of a lessor may not be practicable.
**Column II:**
(1) Praveen may discuss with management whether another type of engagement might be more practicable.
(2) SA B00 also applies to that engagement, along with the special considerations of SA 805.
(3) Praveen shall comply with all SAs relevant to that engagement notwithstanding the complete-set audit.
(4) Praveen shall determine whether the engagement, performed as per the SAs, is practicable.
questions.explanation: Situation A is the 'even if' case, where compliance with all relevant SAs is required although the complete set is also being audited, so A pairs with (3). Situation B is the converse trigger, since where the auditor is not engaged to audit the complete set the auditor shall determine whether the engagement as per the SAs is practicable, so B pairs with (4). Situation C engages the framework condition: a single financial statement or a specific element may be prepared under a general or a special purpose framework, and in the latter case SA B00 also applies, so C pairs with (2). Situation D pairs with (1), because the conversation with management about another type of engagement is what the auditor may do once he concludes the engagement may not be practicable. The options that swap (3) and (4) confuse the two different triggers.

questions.category: SA 805 – Adapting SAs to Element Audits
questions.question:
In the context of an audit of a specific element, account or item of a financial statement under SA 805, consider the following statements:

**Statement 1:** The auditor shall adapt all SAs as necessary to the particular engagement.
**Statement 2:** Because the engagement covers only trade receivables, SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 stand excluded from application.
**Statement 3:** SAs such as SA 240 (fraud), SA 550 (related parties) and SA 570 (going concern) remain relevant even when the subject matter is a specific element of the FS.
**Statement 4:** Where the element is audited alongside the complete set of FS, the audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS may be used.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is the only incorrect one. SA 805 requires the auditor to adapt all SAs as necessary in the engagement; adaptation, and not exclusion, is the response to a narrower subject matter. The standard specifically names SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 as remaining relevant even where only a specific element is audited, because fraud can reside in fictitious receivables, the counterparties can be related parties, and realisation of the element depends on the entity continuing as a going concern. Statement 4 is separately supported, since SA 805 permits use of audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS. The decisive distinction is between a smaller scope of subject matter and a smaller set of applicable standards - only the former exists.

questions.category: SA 805 – Use of Evidence from Complete Set Audit
questions.question: CA Mihir Trivedi is the statutory auditor of Vasvi Steels Ltd for FY 2025-26 and is also engaged to report on the specific element 'carrying value of investment property' of ₹96 crore as at 31.03.2026. In his planning note he records: 'The complete-set audit already covered external confirmations, valuation inputs and title verification for the identical population at the identical date. Fresh procedures would be duplication; the element file will therefore contain only a cross-reference to the complete-set working papers, and I will not separately evaluate whether that evidence is sufficient and appropriate for the element.' Advise him. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: SA 805 permits the auditor to use audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS, but he must still adapt the SAs to the element engagement and satisfy himself that the evidence so used supports the opinion on the element.

The approach is acceptable in full, because SA 805 expressly permits use of audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS, so cross-referencing alone disposes of the requirement and nothing further is expected of the auditor.
The approach is unacceptable in full, because evidence obtained in the complete-set audit cannot be used in a separate element engagement and the element must be audited afresh.
The evidence may be reused only where the element engagement is performed by an audit team different from the one that performed the complete-set audit.
questions.explanation: SA 805 states that when auditing a single FS or a specific element the auditor may use audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS; an identical population, date and valuation source make reuse efficient here. That permission does not displace the separate requirement that the auditor adapt all SAs as necessary in the engagement - the reuse decision is itself a judgment that must be made and documented. The defect in the note is therefore the blanket refusal to evaluate, not the reuse itself. Option 1 overstates the permission into a complete answer, option 2 denies reuse altogether, and option 3 invents a different-team condition the standard does not lay down.

questions.question:
Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R):

**Assertion (A):** While auditing the schedule of tangible assets of an infrastructure investment trust, the engagement partner fixes materiality for the schedule at a level significantly below the materiality fixed for the complete set of FS of the trust.
**Reason (R):** SA 805 states that materiality determined for a single FS or specific element may be lower than the materiality determined for the complete set of FS, and that this will affect the nature, timing and extent of audit procedures.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The assertion describes a permissible and typical outcome, because an element is a smaller and more focussed universe and an amount trivial against the complete set can be significant to the element. Reason R reproduces the SA 805 position accurately, and it is precisely that rule which makes the partner's course of action in A correct - the link is direct, not coincidental, so the second option fails. Nothing in the assertion is wrong, which rules out the third and fourth options. The decisive point is the words 'may be lower' combined with the consequence for nature, timing and extent: a lower element figure is a judgment, but once made it necessarily changes the work done.

questions.question: Kaveri Agro Exports Ltd prepares, in addition to its statutory FS, a 'schedule of disbursements in relation to lease property' on which CA Nilesh Desai is engaged to report for FY 2025-26. The statutory FS are overseen by a five-member Audit Committee. The disbursement schedule is compiled and approved by a two-member Property Committee consisting of the Whole-time Director (Finance) and the Company Secretary, neither of whom sits on the Audit Committee. The engagement team proposes to confine all SA 260 communications on the schedule to the Audit Committee, on the ground that this committee handles the annual audit. State with reasons whether the proposal is correct.
options: Correct, because SA 260 communications arising from any audit engagement of the entity must always be routed to the body that oversees the complete set of FS.
Correct, because the Property Committee merely compiles internal records and has no governance status for audit purposes, so nothing reportable can be communicated to it.

Incorrect, because SA 260 requires communication with those charged with governance, and the TCWG responsible for oversight of preparation of a single FS or specific element may not be the same as for the complete set of FS.

Incorrect, because where a body other than the Audit Committee approves a single FS or element, SA 260 requires those communications to be escalated instead to the TCWG of the ultimate parent entity of the group, which alone has the standing to receive them.
questions.explanation: SA 805 records that while SA 260 requires the auditor to communicate with those charged with governance, the TCWG responsible for oversight of the preparation of a single FS or specific element may not be the same as for the complete set of FS. Here the body that actually compiles and approves the disbursement schedule is the two-member Property Committee, so the decisive fact is who has oversight of the element, not who oversees the annual FS. Confining communications to the Audit Committee would leave the element's real oversight body uninformed. Options 0 and 1 invert the rule, and option 3 imports a parent-entity idea that the standard does not state.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements drawn from SA 800 and SA 805:

**Statement 1:** SA 800 observes that the TCWG responsible for oversight of preparation of special purpose FS may not be the same as those responsible for general purpose FS.
**Statement 2:** SA 805 observes that the TCWG responsible for oversight of preparation of a single FS or specific element may not be the same as those responsible for the complete set of FS.
**Statement 3:** The two standards are laying down the same comparator, namely general purpose FS versus special purpose FS, and the texts are therefore merely duplicated.
**Statement 4:** In each standard the operative point is the same - the identity of the appropriate recipients of SA 260 communications must be established by reference to the particular engagement actually accepted and cannot be assumed from another engagement.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 each reproduce the wording of the respective standard, and statement 4 captures the shared principle that SA 260 recipients are identified engagement by engagement rather than by the identity of the client. Statement 3 fails because the comparators are different: SA 800 contrasts special purpose FS with general purpose FS, whereas SA 805 contrasts a single FS or specific element with the complete set of FS. The distinction is substantive, because a single FS or element can itself form part of a general purpose FS, so the SA 805 contrast is not a framework contrast at all. Option 2 is incomplete as it drops statement 1, which is a correct reproduction of SA 800.

questions.question:
An auditor accepts two separate engagements from the same client for FY 2025-26: (i) audit of special purpose FS prepared on the accrual basis solely for a term-loan lender, and (ii) audit of the specific element 'inventory' appearing in the client's general purpose FS. In the special purpose engagement, management and the lender have agreed that misstatements identified below ₹40 lakh will not be corrected. In the element engagement, the auditor notes that an error of ₹2 crore in inventory provisioning would be immaterial to the complete set of FS, for which materiality is ₹25 crore.

Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The ₹40 lakh agreed threshold in the special purpose engagement relieves the auditor of the requirement to determine materiality under SA 320 for that engagement.
**Statement 2:** The agreed threshold does not relieve the auditor of the requirement to determine materiality as per SA 320, and judgments under SA 320 continue to rest on the financial information needs of the intended users.
**Statement 3:** For the inventory element, materiality may be lower than that determined for the complete set of FS and any such reduction will affect the nature, timing and extent of procedures on inventory.
**Statement 4:** Since ₹2 crore is clearly immaterial against complete-set materiality of ₹25 crore, the element engagement must adopt the same ₹25 crore figure.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: SA 800 is explicit that where management agrees with intended users a threshold below which identified misstatements will not be corrected, the arrangement does not relieve the auditor of the requirement to determine materiality as per SA 320, whose judgments are based on the financial information needs of intended users; statement 1 is therefore wrong and statement 2 right. SA 805 operates on a different axis: materiality for a single FS or specific element may be lower than that for the complete set of FS, and this affects the nature, timing and extent of procedures, which makes statement 3 right and statement 4 wrong. The decisive contrast is that the SA 800 issue is whether an externally agreed floor displaces SA 320, while the SA 805 issue is whether a smaller subject matter demands a tighter scale. A complete-set figure of ₹25 crore cannot simply be lifted into the element engagement.

questions.question: M/s Deven & Associates audit the complete set of FS of Shalimar Hotels Ltd for the year ended 31.03.2026 and, under a second appointment in the same firm and for the same reporting period, also report on the specific element 'recorded value of identified intangible assets' of ₹412 crore. Management requests a single combined report containing one opinion paragraph covering both the FS and the intangible-asset element, arguing that the scope, dates, client, framework and audit team are all identical. Which of the following is the correct position under SA 805?
options: A combined report is permissible, because the entity, the reporting date, the audit team and the applicable framework are identical across the two engagements and no user could be misled.
The auditor shall express a separate opinion for each engagement, since the engagement to report on a specific element is undertaken alongwith the engagement to audit the complete set of FS.

A separate opinion is required only if the two engagements are signed by different engagement partners, cover different reporting periods, apply different financial reporting frameworks, or relate to different components of the group.
The auditor may issue one combined opinion provided the intangible assets are separately disclosed in the notes to the complete set of FS.
questions.explanation: SA 805 addresses this situation directly: where the auditor undertakes an engagement to report on a single FS or specific element alongwith the engagement to audit the complete set of FS, the auditor shall express a separate opinion for each engagement. The obligation is triggered by the existence of the two engagements, not by differences in period, personnel or team, so the identical scope and dates urged by management are irrelevant facts. Combining the opinions would also make the modification status of each subject matter indistinguishable to a reader. Option 0 treats the identity of scope and dates as decisive when the standard looks only to the existence of two engagements, option 2 attaches conditions the standard does not impose, and option 3 confuses disclosure in the notes with the structure of the audit report.

questions.question: An auditor has reported on the trade receivables of Orbito Distribution Ltd as a specific element for the year ended 31.03.2026 and has also audited the complete set of FS of the company. The company proposes to print the audited trade-receivables schedule inside the annual report immediately after the balance sheet, using the same type-face, the same ruled format, a similar heading 'Statement of Receivables', and with no indication on the face of the schedule that it is the subject of a separate element engagement. Which one of the following statements about this proposal is LEAST appropriate?
options: An audited single FS or specific element may be published together with the audited complete set of FS, so the proposal is not barred merely because the two appear in one document.
The permission to publish together is conditional on the presentation of the single FS or element differentiating it sufficiently from the complete set of FS, which this layout fails to do.
The auditor should require the schedule to be visually and descriptively distinguished from the FS, failing which he should not permit the proposed presentation.
Because the element report is printed in the same document as the FS, the auditor must replace the separate opinion on the element with a single combined opinion.
questions.explanation: SA 805 permits an audited single FS or specific element to be published together with the audited complete set of FS, but conditions the permission on the presentation of the element differentiating it sufficiently from the complete set of FS. The first three statements are consistent with that two-part position: publication is allowed in principle, the allowance is conditional, and the auditor's response is to insist on differentiation. The fourth statement is the least appropriate because joint publication is governed by presentation and not by the number of opinions; the separate-opinion requirement operates independently and would be breached rather than cured by combining opinions. The decisive facts are the identical format, similar heading and the absence of any differentiating indication.

questions.category: SA 805 – Separate Opinion vs Publication Together
questions.question:
Consider the following statements on the interplay, under SA 805, between the requirement to express a separate opinion and the permission to publish an element report together with the complete set of FS:

**Statement 1:** Where the auditor undertakes an engagement to report on a single FS or specific element alongwith the engagement to audit the complete set of FS, expressing a separate opinion for each engagement is an unqualified requirement.
**Statement 2:** Publishing the audited single FS or element together with the audited complete set of FS is permitted only if the presentation of the single FS or element differentiates it sufficiently from the complete set of FS.
**Statement 3:** The auditor may collapse the two opinions into one whenever management consents, because the mandatory character described in Statement 1 is in reality conditional.
**Statement 4:** The conditional element in Statement 2 is a condition about presentation and therefore operates independently of the separate-opinion requirement in Statement 1.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The two rules differ in character, and that asymmetry is the point being tested. Reporting separately for each engagement is mandatory - SA 805 says the auditor shall express a separate opinion for each engagement where the element engagement is undertaken alongwith the complete-set audit - and management's consent cannot displace it, so statement 3 is incorrect. Joint publication is by contrast a permission subject to a single presentation condition, namely sufficient differentiation of the element from the complete set of FS. Because one rule governs opinions and the other governs layout, satisfying or failing the publication condition has no effect on the duty to report separately, which is what statement 4 captures. This mandatory/conditional asymmetry is distinct from the separate restriction that bars an unmodified element opinion where the complete-set report carries an adverse opinion or a disclaimer.

questions.category: SA 805 – Adapting SAs to Element Audits
questions.question:
CASE: M/s Kothari & Mehta are the statutory auditors of Suraksha Pharmaceuticals Ltd for the year ended 31.03.2026, and materiality for the complete set of FS is ₹30 crore. In the same year the firm accepts a second engagement to report on the specific element 'inventory of active pharmaceutical ingredients' (API inventory) of the same company, carrying value ₹268 crore at 31.03.2026. During planning and performance the following facts emerge:
(a) A junior member records in the element audit plan that SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 need not be considered for this engagement because it is confined to one line item, noting that 'fraud, related parties and going concern are complete-FS concepts'.
(b) The complete-set audit had already covered full physical verification of API inventory at the same warehouses at the same date, price testing and an obsolete-stock review; the manager proposes to use this audit evidence in the element engagement.
(c) Materiality for the element is fixed at ₹2.20 crore against complete-set materiality of ₹30 crore, and in response the team increases sample items at the year-end count, moves confirmation of third-party warehouse stocks to an interim date with roll-forward procedures, and obtains a specialist's report on shelf-life provisioning.
(d) The API inventory schedule is compiled and approved by a 'Stock Statement Committee' of two functional directors who are not members of the Audit Committee that oversees the complete set of FS; the team proposes to address all SA 260 communications on the element to the Audit Committee.
(e) The company wishes to bind the audited API inventory schedule into its annual report immediately after the balance sheet, in identical format and type-face with nothing on the face of the schedule indicating a separate element engagement, and asks for one combined opinion covering both the FS and the schedule.

With reference to facts (a) and (b), consider the following possible actions:
**Action 1:** Apply SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 to the element engagement so far as they are relevant, adapting all SAs as necessary rather than excluding them.
**Action 2:** Exclude those three SAs from the element plan, since the engagement is limited to one line item of the FS.
**Action 3:** Use the audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS for the element engagement, the population, date and locations being identical.
**Action 4:** Set aside the complete-set evidence and perform all element procedures afresh, because a separate opinion will be expressed on the element.

Which actions should the auditor take?
options: Actions 1 and 2 only
Actions 2 and 4 only
Actions 1 and 3 only
Actions 1, 3 and 4 only
Actions 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 805 requires the auditor to adapt all SAs as necessary in the engagement and names SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 as relevant even when a specific element of the FS is audited; fictitious purchases, related-party warehouse arrangements and an inability to continue as a going concern are all capable of affecting the carrying value of API inventory, so Action 2 is wrong. The standard separately permits the auditor to use audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS, and identical population, date and locations make reuse appropriate here, so Action 4's demand for a fresh audit is not required and is indeed wasteful. Actions 1 and 3 are therefore the correct combination, and any option including Action 2 or Action 4 fails. The decisive fact is that the element engagement is narrower in subject matter, not narrower in the standards that apply to it.

CASE: M/s Kothari & Mehta are the statutory auditors of Suraksha Pharmaceuticals Ltd for the year ended 31.03.2026, and materiality for the complete set of FS is ₹30 crore. In the same year the firm accepts a second engagement to report on the specific element 'inventory of active pharmaceutical ingredients' (API inventory) of the same company, carrying value ₹268 crore at 31.03.2026. During planning and performance the following facts emerge:
(a) A junior member records in the element audit plan that SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 need not be considered for this engagement because it is confined to one line item, noting that 'fraud, related parties and going concern are complete-FS concepts'.
(b) The complete-set audit had already covered full physical verification of API inventory at the same warehouses at the same date, price testing and an obsolete-stock review; the manager proposes to use this audit evidence in the element engagement.
(c) Materiality for the element is fixed at ₹2.20 crore against complete-set materiality of ₹30 crore, and in response the team increases sample items at the year-end count, moves confirmation of third-party warehouse stocks to an interim date with roll-forward procedures, and obtains a specialist's report on shelf-life provisioning.
(d) The API inventory schedule is compiled and approved by a 'Stock Statement Committee' of two functional directors who are not members of the Audit Committee that oversees the complete set of FS; the team proposes to address all SA 260 communications on the element to the Audit Committee.
(e) The company wishes to bind the audited API inventory schedule into its annual report immediately after the balance sheet, in identical format and type-face with nothing on the face of the schedule indicating a separate element engagement, and asks for one combined opinion covering both the FS and the schedule.

With reference to fact (c), consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** Materiality determined for a specific element may be lower than the materiality determined for the complete set of FS.
**Statement 2:** The lower element-level materiality will affect the nature, timing and extent of audit procedures on the element.
**Statement 3:** Because ₹2.20 crore is a fraction of ₹30 crore, the element materiality must be raised to align with the complete-set figure once a separate opinion is to be expressed on the element.
**Statement 4:** The additional count samples, the interim confirmations with roll-forward and the specialist's work are consistent with the response SA 805 contemplates when element materiality is set lower.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 805 states that materiality determined for a single FS or specific element may be lower than the materiality determined for the complete set of FS and that this will affect the nature, timing and extent of audit procedures. A ₹268 crore element measured against ₹2.20 crore is a much tighter scale than the ₹30 crore complete-set figure, and the team's response - larger count samples, confirmations moved earlier with roll-forward, and expert input on shelf-life provisioning - is exactly the extension of work the standard anticipates. Statement 3 is wrong because nothing requires the element figure to be aligned with the complete-set figure; a separate opinion in fact presupposes a separate materiality judgment. The decisive fact is that the element's scale is set by reference to the element itself, not by reference to the FS of which it forms part.

questions.category: SA 805 – Separate Opinion vs Publication Together
questions.question:
CASE: M/s Kothari & Mehta are the statutory auditors of Suraksha Pharmaceuticals Ltd for the year ended 31.03.2026, and materiality for the complete set of FS is ₹30 crore. In the same year the firm accepts a second engagement to report on the specific element 'inventory of active pharmaceutical ingredients' (API inventory) of the same company, carrying value ₹268 crore at 31.03.2026. During planning and performance the following facts emerge:
(a) A junior member records in the element audit plan that SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 need not be considered for this engagement because it is confined to one line item, noting that 'fraud, related parties and going concern are complete-FS concepts'.
(b) The complete-set audit had already covered full physical verification of API inventory at the same warehouses at the same date, price testing and an obsolete-stock review; the manager proposes to use this audit evidence in the element engagement.
(c) Materiality for the element is fixed at ₹2.20 crore against complete-set materiality of ₹30 crore, and in response the team increases sample items at the year-end count, moves confirmation of third-party warehouse stocks to an interim date with roll-forward procedures, and obtains a specialist's report on shelf-life provisioning.
(d) The API inventory schedule is compiled and approved by a 'Stock Statement Committee' of two functional directors who are not members of the Audit Committee that oversees the complete set of FS; the team proposes to address all SA 260 communications on the element to the Audit Committee.
(e) The company wishes to bind the audited API inventory schedule into its annual report immediately after the balance sheet, in identical format and type-face with nothing on the face of the schedule indicating a separate element engagement, and asks for one combined opinion covering both the FS and the schedule.

With reference to fact (e), which of the following is the MOST appropriate advice to the firm?
options: The schedule may be published with the FS in the proposed presentation, provided a separate opinion is expressed for each engagement and the element report is signed by a different partner.
The schedule may not be published with the FS at all, because an audited specific element and an audited complete set of FS can never appear in the same document.
The firm may issue one combined opinion, and once it does so the schedule may be printed in whatever presentation the company prefers.

The firm must express a separate opinion for each engagement; the schedule may be published together with the complete set of FS only if its presentation differentiates it sufficiently from the complete set of FS, which the proposed layout does not.
questions.explanation: Two distinct requirements operate on fact (e). Where an engagement to report on a specific element is undertaken alongwith the engagement to audit the complete set of FS, the auditor shall express a separate opinion for each engagement, and management's preference for a single combined opinion cannot override that mandatory rule. Joint publication is separately permitted, but only if the presentation of the element differentiates it sufficiently from the complete set of FS; identical format, identical type-face and nothing indicating a separate element engagement fail that condition. Option 0 wrongly treats presentation as unconstrained once opinions are separate, option 1 wrongly bars all joint publication, and option 2 reverses both rules by buying freedom of layout with a single combined opinion. The decisive facts are the request for one combined opinion and the non-differentiated layout.

questions.category: SA 805 – Adapting SAs to Element Audits
questions.question:
CASE: CA Arundhati Rao of M/s Rao & Bhatt is engaged to report on a single financial statement - the statement of cash flows of Mangalam Infra Ltd for the year ended 31.03.2026 - and her firm also audits the complete set of FS of the company for the same year. Materiality for the single statement is initially planned at the same amount used for the complete set of FS. The statement of cash flows is drawn up by the Head of Treasury and reviewed by a Compliance Officer who reports to the CFO, while the complete set of FS is overseen by the Audit Committee. During fieldwork the following occur:
(i) the team removes all fraud-related enquiries and related-party procedures from the plan on the ground that a cash flow statement contains no accrual judgments;
(ii) the team plans to reuse the bank balance confirmations and cash-count evidence already obtained in the audit of the complete set of FS;
(iii) the company asks that the audited statement of cash flows be printed in its annual report immediately following the balance sheet, with the same column headings and no separate title or footnote identifying it as the subject of a distinct engagement;
(iv) the company asks for a single report covering both the complete set of FS and the separately engaged statement of cash flows.

Match the following:
**Column I**
A. Position on application of SAs to this engagement
B. Position on audit evidence for the single FS
C. Position on materiality for the single FS
D. Position on reporting where both engagements exist

**Column II**
1. The auditor may use audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS.
2. All SAs shall be adapted as necessary, and SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 remain relevant.
3. The auditor shall express a separate opinion for each engagement.
4. Materiality for the single FS may be lower than that for the complete set of FS, and this affects the nature, timing and extent of procedures.
questions.explanation: Fact (i) misstates the standard: SA 805 requires the auditor to adapt all SAs as necessary in the engagement and expressly preserves the relevance of SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 even for a single FS or element, and the absence of accrual judgments does not remove the risk of manipulated cash receipts or undisclosed related-party fund flows, so A matches 2. Reuse of the confirmations and cash-count evidence from the complete-set audit is expressly permitted, so B matches 1. Planning single-statement materiality at the complete-set figure ignores that element materiality may be lower with consequences for nature, timing and extent, so C matches 4. Because the cash flow statement engagement is undertaken alongwith the complete-set audit, a separate opinion is required for each engagement notwithstanding the company's request in fact (iv), so D matches 3.

options: No change arises, because SA 260 communications arising from an audit of the entity must always be routed to its Audit Committee.

The change is decisive for identifying the recipients, because the TCWG responsible for oversight of preparation of a single FS may not be the same as for the complete set of FS, so the Sub-Committee becomes the appropriate recipient for the single statement engagement.
The change removes the need for any SA 260 communication on this engagement, because a sub-committee constituted by the Board has no status as those charged with governance for audit purposes.
The change compels the auditor to express a separate opinion on the single financial statement, which would not otherwise have been required given that the same firm audits the complete set of FS.
questions.explanation: SA 805 records that although SA 260 requires communication with those charged with governance, the TCWG responsible for oversight of the preparation of a single FS or specific element may not be the same as for the complete set of FS. A Board sub-committee expressly charged with oversight of the statement of cash flows therefore changes the identity of the appropriate recipients for that engagement, while the Audit Committee remains the body for the complete set of FS. The assumption that one committee covers every engagement is precisely what the standard warns against. Option 3 confuses a governance fact with the reporting rule, since the separate-opinion requirement flows from undertaking both engagements and not from the composition of the Board's committees, and option 2 wrongly denies sub-committee governance status.

questions.category: SA 805 – Adapting SAs to Element Audits
questions.question: CASE: Tanvi Spinners Ltd is audited for FY 2025-26 by M/s Iyer Nair & Co. The company is negotiating a debt recapitalisation, two lenders have declined to roll over ₹340 crore of working-capital limits, and the complete-set audit file records a material uncertainty relating to going concern. Separately, and in the same firm, the auditor reports on the specific element 'inventory of cotton and yarn' of the same company as at 31.03.2026. The engagement assistant deletes all SA 570-related considerations from the element plan, recording that 'going concern is dealt with in the report on the complete set of FS and cannot be raised again in a single-element engagement'. He separately proposes to rely on the inventory evidence already obtained in the complete-set audit. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: The assistant is correct, because SA 570 is a complete-set concept and is excluded from an engagement confined to a specific element of the FS.
The assistant is correct, because the element engagement covers a smaller population and the SAs apply in full only to audits of the complete set of FS.
The assistant is wrong, because all SAs must be adapted as necessary and SA 570 is expressly relevant even for a specific element; his proposal to use complete-set evidence is however permissible.

The assistant is wrong only in form and not in substance, because the element plan need not separately mention SA 570 provided the complete-set audit file demonstrates that going concern was duly considered and dealt with there.
questions.explanation: SA 805 requires the auditor to adapt all SAs as necessary in the engagement and states expressly that SAs such as SA 240, SA 550 and SA 570 are relevant even when a specific element of the FS is audited. On these facts the point is not academic: an entity whose working-capital limits are not being renewed may be unable to hold or dispose of cotton and yarn in the ordinary course, which bears directly on the carrying value of the element. The assistant's second proposal is sound, since SA 805 permits the auditor to use audit evidence obtained as part of the audit of the complete set of FS, and option 2 captures both halves correctly. Options 0 and 1 treat narrower subject matter as producing a narrower set of standards, and option 3 substitutes the complete-set file for the element-level judgment that the standard demands.

questions.category: SA 805 – Unmodified Opinion on Element after Adverse/Disclaimer
questions.question:
CASE: R. Kulkarni & Co. is the statutory auditor of Meridian Steel Ltd (MSL) and has also been appointed to report on a schedule of trade receivables as at 31 March 2024, which MSL's term-lender requires. The complete set of financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2024 is prepared under Ind AS. Inventory, representing 34% of total assets and affecting cost of goods sold, trade payables, working capital and related disclosures, is so materially misstated that the firm concludes the effects are both material and pervasive, and it signs an adverse opinion on the complete set dated 27 May 2024. The schedule of trade receivables is prepared on the same Ind AS basis, deals with the same date, constitutes about 9% of total assets, has been audited in full by the firm, and the firm is satisfied that the inventory misstatement has no effect on the receivables balance. Neither law nor regulation prohibits reporting on the schedule. Because the lender insists on a clean report, management asks the firm to express an unmodified opinion on the schedule and to print that report in the same annual report immediately after the adverse opinion report, under a distinctly headed section.

With reference to management's request that both reports appear in the same printed annual report, which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: The unmodified opinion may be expressed as requested, since the schedule has been fully audited, is unaffected by the inventory misstatement and amounts to only about 9% of total assets, the inventory problem being irrelevant to receivables.

The unmodified opinion may not be expressed in the form requested, because the opinion on the element would be contained in an auditor's report published together with the report containing the adverse opinion.
No opinion at all may be expressed on the schedule, because an adverse opinion on the complete set of financial statements precludes any separate engagement on a specific element.
The unmodified opinion may be expressed as requested because neither law nor regulation prohibits reporting on the schedule, that being the only condition capable of applying on these facts.
questions.explanation: Where an adverse or disclaimer of opinion has been expressed on the complete set of financial statements, an unmodified opinion on a specific element is available only if all three conditions hold: not prohibited by law or regulation, the opinion is expressed in a report not published together with the report containing the adverse or disclaimer opinion, and the element does not constitute a major portion of the complete set. The three conditions are cumulative, so satisfying two of them is not enough. Here the decisive fact is the manner of publication: printing the report on the schedule in the same annual report immediately after the adverse opinion report is publication together, and the distinctly headed section does not convert one document into two. The first option ignores that condition; the third over-reads the rule, since reporting on the element remains possible if the reports are separated; the fourth wrongly treats the legal bar as the only relevant condition.

questions.category: SA 805 – Unmodified Opinion on Element after Adverse/Disclaimer
questions.question:
CASE: R. Kulkarni & Co. is the statutory auditor of Meridian Steel Ltd (MSL) and has also been appointed to report on a schedule of trade receivables as at 31 March 2024, which MSL's term-lender requires. The complete set of financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2024 is prepared under Ind AS. Inventory, representing 34% of total assets and affecting cost of goods sold, trade payables, working capital and related disclosures, is so materially misstated that the firm concludes the effects are both material and pervasive, and it signs an adverse opinion on the complete set dated 27 May 2024. The schedule of trade receivables is prepared on the same Ind AS basis, deals with the same date, constitutes about 9% of total assets, has been audited in full by the firm, and the firm is satisfied that the inventory misstatement has no effect on the receivables balance. Neither law nor regulation prohibits reporting on the schedule. Because the lender insists on a clean report, management asks the firm to express an unmodified opinion on the schedule and to print that report in the same annual report immediately after the adverse opinion report, under a distinctly headed section.

Assume that, instead of binding the two reports in the annual report, MSL agrees that the auditor's report on the schedule of trade receivables will be issued as a standalone document addressed to the term-lender only and will not be published together with the report containing the adverse opinion. All other facts remain unchanged. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: The unmodified opinion remains prohibited, because a schedule of trade receivables is a single financial statement and is therefore deemed to constitute a major portion of the complete set.
The unmodified opinion remains prohibited unless and until the adverse opinion on the complete set is withdrawn, the exception being available only where the complete-set report is unmodified.

The unmodified opinion becomes capable of being expressed, because with the reports no longer published together each of the three conditions, including the assessment that an element of about 9% of total assets is not a major portion, can be satisfied.
The unmodified opinion becomes permitted without anything further needing consideration, because separating the documents is by itself a complete answer.
questions.explanation: The bar created by publication together is only one of the three cumulative conditions, so removing it re-opens the exception provided the remaining conditions are also met. On the changed facts there is no legal prohibition, the schedule is a specific element rather than a single financial statement, and about 9% of total assets is a figure on which the auditor can conclude the element is not a major portion of the complete set. The decisive change is therefore the manner of issue, not the audit findings, which were already complete. The first option mislabels a schedule of trade receivables as a single financial statement, the deeming rule being confined to a single financial statement; the second wrongly imports a requirement that the complete-set opinion be unmodified; the fourth ignores that the other two conditions still have to be satisfied.

questions.question:
CASE: R. Kulkarni & Co. is the statutory auditor of Meridian Steel Ltd (MSL) and has also been appointed to report on a schedule of trade receivables as at 31 March 2024, which MSL's term-lender requires. The complete set of financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2024 is prepared under Ind AS. Inventory, representing 34% of total assets and affecting cost of goods sold, trade payables, working capital and related disclosures, is so materially misstated that the firm concludes the effects are both material and pervasive, and it signs an adverse opinion on the complete set dated 27 May 2024. The schedule of trade receivables is prepared on the same Ind AS basis, deals with the same date, constitutes about 9% of total assets, has been audited in full by the firm, and the firm is satisfied that the inventory misstatement has no effect on the receivables balance. Neither law nor regulation prohibits reporting on the schedule. Because the lender insists on a clean report, management asks the firm to express an unmodified opinion on the schedule and to print that report in the same annual report immediately after the adverse opinion report, under a distinctly headed section.

Assume that the term-lender instead requires an audited statement of cash flows of MSL for the year ended 31 March 2024, that the firm will issue its report on that statement as a standalone document not published together with the annual report, and that no law or regulation prohibits such reporting. All other facts, including the adverse opinion on the complete set, remain unchanged. Which of the following is the correct outcome?
options: The auditor shall not express an unmodified opinion on the statement of cash flows, because a single financial statement is deemed to constitute a major portion of the complete set of financial statements.
The auditor may express an unmodified opinion, because the statement of cash flows is capable of being audited without reference to the misstated inventory.
The auditor may express an unmodified opinion provided the presentation of the statement of cash flows sufficiently differentiates it from the complete set of financial statements.
The auditor shall determine the effect of the adverse opinion on the statement of cash flows and may report on it without modification if no effect is identified.
questions.explanation: The exception permitting an unmodified opinion after an adverse or disclaimer opinion on the complete set is available for a specific element and requires, among other conditions, that the element not constitute a major portion of the complete set. For a single financial statement the position is different: a single financial statement is deemed to constitute a major portion, so that condition can never be satisfied and the auditor shall not express an unmodified opinion on it. The decisive fact is the identity of the subject matter, a statement of cash flows being a single financial statement, which also explains why the standalone issue of the report and the absence of any legal bar do not rescue the arrangement. The second option substitutes the auditor's satisfaction about inventory for the deeming rule; the third borrows a consideration that has nothing to do with this prohibition; the fourth applies the qualified-opinion rule to an adverse opinion.

questions.category: SA 805 – Unmodified Opinion on Element after Adverse/Disclaimer
questions.question:
CASE: R. Kulkarni & Co. is the statutory auditor of Meridian Steel Ltd (MSL) and has also been appointed to report on a schedule of trade receivables as at 31 March 2024, which MSL's term-lender requires. The complete set of financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2024 is prepared under Ind AS. Inventory, representing 34% of total assets and affecting cost of goods sold, trade payables, working capital and related disclosures, is so materially misstated that the firm concludes the effects are both material and pervasive, and it signs an adverse opinion on the complete set dated 27 May 2024. The schedule of trade receivables is prepared on the same Ind AS basis, deals with the same date, constitutes about 9% of total assets, has been audited in full by the firm, and the firm is satisfied that the inventory misstatement has no effect on the receivables balance. Neither law nor regulation prohibits reporting on the schedule. Because the lender insists on a clean report, management asks the firm to express an unmodified opinion on the schedule and to print that report in the same annual report immediately after the adverse opinion report, under a distinctly headed section.

Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The modified opinion carried by the report on the complete set of financial statements is itself one of the matters for which the auditor must consider the implications for the engagement to report on the schedule of trade receivables.
**Statement 2:** Had the opinion on the complete set been qualified instead of adverse, the auditor would in all events have been required to qualify the opinion on the schedule.
**Statement 3:** Placing the report on the schedule in a distinctly headed section of the same printed annual report would satisfy the condition that the opinion not be expressed in a report published together with the report containing the adverse opinion.
**Statement 4:** The auditor must satisfy himself that the specific element does not constitute a major portion of the complete set of financial statements, along with the other two conditions.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only.
2 and 3 only.
1 and 4 only.
1, 2 and 4 only.
questions.explanation: A modified opinion is expressly one of the matters, alongside going concern, key audit matter, emphasis of matter/other matter paragraphs and other information, whose relevance to the single financial statement or element engagement the auditor shall consider, so Statement 1 is correct. Where the complete set carries a qualified opinion the requirement is to determine the effect on the report on the single financial statement or element and to qualify only if deemed appropriate, which makes Statement 2 too absolute. Statement 3 fails because a distinctly headed section within the same printed annual report is still publication together with the report containing the adverse opinion, and the condition looks to the identity of the report document rather than to headings. Statement 4 states one of the three cumulative conditions accurately, the major portion test being an actual assessment for a specific element rather than a deemed one.

questions.category: SA 805 – Relevance of Matters in Complete-Set Report
questions.question:
CASE: The complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Aster Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2023 carried an auditor's report signed by D. Mehta & Associates on 29 May 2023. That report contained (a) a 'Material Uncertainty related to Going Concern' section arising from the refinancing of a term loan during FY 2022-23, (b) a Key Audit Matter on recognition of milestone revenue under regulatory-approved technology transfer contracts, (c) an Emphasis of Matter paragraph drawing attention to a note on a related party transaction, and (d) an 'Other Information' section. In November 2024 the same firm is appointed to report on a schedule of the externally managed assets and income of the company's employee pension trust for the year ended 31 March 2024. That schedule is prepared on the contribution and distribution basis prescribed by the pension trust deed, a special purpose framework, and the going concern uncertainty, the milestone revenue KAM and the related party note concern the company as a whole rather than the pension arrangement.

Consider the following statements on the auditor's evaluation of the relevance of the matters in the FY 2022-23 report:
**Statement 1:** The nature of the going concern matter and the extent to which it relates to the pension schedule are relevant considerations.
**Statement 2:** The pervasiveness of the matter described in the report on the complete set of financial statements is a relevant consideration.
**Statement 3:** Because those matters stood concluded when the report was signed on 29 May 2023, the time elapsed since that date is not a relevant consideration.
**Statement 4:** The nature and extent of the difference between the applicable financial reporting frameworks is relevant in judging whether the milestone revenue KAM bears on the schedule.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 3 only.
1 and 2 only.
2 and 4 only.
3 and 4 only.
questions.explanation: The auditor shall consider the implications of a matter included in the report on the complete set of financial statements for the engagement to report on a single financial statement or specific element, and the listed factors include the nature of the matter and the extent to which it relates to that statement or element, its pervasiveness, the nature and extent of difference between applicable financial reporting frameworks, the extent of difference between the periods covered, and the time elapsed since the date of the report on the complete set. Statements 1, 2 and 4 each restate one of those factors, and the framework factor in Statement 4 is squarely engaged because the schedule follows a trust-deed basis while the complete set follows Ind AS. Statement 3 is the only incorrect one, since roughly 18 months have elapsed between 29 May 2023 and November 2024 and lapse of time is expressly a relevant factor. The conclusion that these matters concern the company as a whole rather than the pension arrangement is itself reached by applying factors 1 and 2, not by declining to consider them.

questions.category: SA 805 – Relevance of Matters in Complete-Set Report
questions.question:
CASE: The complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Aster Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2023 carried an auditor's report signed by D. Mehta & Associates on 29 May 2023. That report contained (a) a 'Material Uncertainty related to Going Concern' section arising from the refinancing of a term loan during FY 2022-23, (b) a Key Audit Matter on recognition of milestone revenue under regulatory-approved technology transfer contracts, (c) an Emphasis of Matter paragraph drawing attention to a note on a related party transaction, and (d) an 'Other Information' section. In November 2024 the same firm is appointed to report on a schedule of the externally managed assets and income of the company's employee pension trust for the year ended 31 March 2024. That schedule is prepared on the contribution and distribution basis prescribed by the pension trust deed, a special purpose framework, and the going concern uncertainty, the milestone revenue KAM and the related party note concern the company as a whole rather than the pension arrangement.

Match each factor in Column I with the feature of this engagement to which that factor most directly directs the auditor's attention in Column II.
Column I:
1. Nature of the matter described in the report on the complete set of financial statements and the extent to which it relates to the single financial statement or specific element
2. Pervasiveness of the matter described in the report on the complete set of financial statements
3. Nature and extent of difference between applicable financial reporting frameworks
4. Extent of difference between the period covered by the complete set of financial statements and the period of the specific element
5. Time elapsed since the date of the auditor's report on the complete set of financial statements
Column II:
A. Whether the milestone revenue Key Audit Matter touches any caption presented in the pension schedule
B. Whether the going concern uncertainty affects the entity as a whole rather than only the pension arrangement
C. Whether the contribution and distribution basis of the trust deed diverges materially from Ind AS
D. Whether FY 2023-24, the period of the schedule, coincides with the year covered by the earlier report
E. The gap of roughly 18 months between 29 May 2023 and the November 2024 appointment
questions.explanation: Factor 1 asks how far the described matter reaches into the subject matter of the element engagement, so it directs attention to whether the milestone revenue KAM touches any caption of the pension schedule. Factor 2 concerns how far the matter spreads, which is exactly the question whether the going concern uncertainty is entity-wide rather than confined to the pension arrangement. Factor 3 addresses the comparison of the Ind AS framework with the trust deed's contribution and distribution basis, and factor 4 addresses the comparison of the year ended 31 March 2023 with the year ended 31 March 2024. Factor 5 is the only one measuring the passage of time since the earlier report date, which is the 18 month gap; the other matchings swap these distinctly different comparisons, in particular confusing the framework difference with the period difference.

questions.category: SA 805 – Relevance of Matters in Complete-Set Report
questions.question:
CASE: The complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Aster Pharma Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2023 carried an auditor's report signed by D. Mehta & Associates on 29 May 2023. That report contained (a) a 'Material Uncertainty related to Going Concern' section arising from the refinancing of a term loan during FY 2022-23, (b) a Key Audit Matter on recognition of milestone revenue under regulatory-approved technology transfer contracts, (c) an Emphasis of Matter paragraph drawing attention to a note on a related party transaction, and (d) an 'Other Information' section. In November 2024 the same firm is appointed to report on a schedule of the externally managed assets and income of the company's employee pension trust for the year ended 31 March 2024. That schedule is prepared on the contribution and distribution basis prescribed by the pension trust deed, a special purpose framework, and the going concern uncertainty, the milestone revenue KAM and the related party note concern the company as a whole rather than the pension arrangement.

Which of the following actions should D. Mehta & Associates take in dealing with the relevance of matters included in its report on the complete set of financial statements?
1. Consider whether the going concern material uncertainty, the Key Audit Matter and the Other Information section are relevant to the engagement to report on the pension schedule.
2. Consider the implications of the Emphasis of Matter paragraph, and of any modified opinion, for this engagement.
3. Consider the relevance of the matters in the earlier report only if that report contained a modified opinion.
4. Consider the difference between the periods covered and the time elapsed since 29 May 2023 in evaluating those implications.
options: 1, 3 and 4 only.
2 and 3 only.
1, 2 and 4 only.
questions.explanation: The auditor shall consider the implications of whether a matter included in the report on the complete set of financial statements is relevant for the engagement to report on a single financial statement or specific element, and the matters expressly enumerated are going concern, key audit matter, modified opinion, emphasis of matter/other matter and other information. Actions 1 and 2 between them cover that entire list, and action 4 applies the listed factors of difference in the period covered and time elapsed since the date of the earlier report, both of which are live here since FY 2023-24 differs from FY 2022-23 and 18 months have passed. Action 3 is wrong because the duty to consider relevance is not conditioned on the earlier report having been modified; an unmodified report carrying a key audit matter, an emphasis of matter paragraph or an other information section still requires that consideration. Any option including action 3 is therefore incomplete or incorrect.

questions.category: SA 805 – Qualified Opinion on Complete Set
questions.question:
