CASE: CA Prakash Iyer is engaged both to audit the complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Sunfield Textiles Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2024 and to report on a schedule of tangible assets as at 31 March 2024 required by an asset-financing lender. The schedule presents only the original cost of acquisition of specified plant and machinery and, under the special purpose basis prescribed in the lender's agreement, excludes accumulated depreciation and carrying amounts. In his report on the complete set dated 30 June 2024 the auditor qualified the opinion solely because depreciation on plant acquired on 1 February 2024 had not been provided, the effect being confined to carrying value of plant, accumulated depreciation, the statement of profit and loss and related disclosures. The plant concerned is included in the schedule at cost. The lender asks that the opinion on the schedule also be qualified for consistency, while the company's finance director insists that no qualification on the schedule is permissible in any circumstances.

Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion on the auditor's reporting obligation for the schedule?
options: The auditor shall qualify the opinion on the schedule as the lender demands, because a qualified opinion on the complete set of financial statements necessarily involves every specific element drawn from those statements.
The auditor need not take the qualification into account at all, because the schedule is prepared on a special purpose basis that differs from Ind AS.
The auditor shall disclaim an opinion on the schedule, because the report on the complete set of financial statements carries a modified opinion.
The auditor shall determine the effect of the qualification on the report on the schedule and shall qualify the opinion on the schedule only if, having done so, the auditor deems it appropriate.
questions.explanation: Where the auditor has expressed a qualified opinion on the complete set of financial statements, the requirement is to determine the effect of that qualification on the report on the single financial statement or specific element and then, if deemed appropriate, to modify (qualify) the opinion on that statement or element. The obligation is therefore to perform the determination, not to reproduce the qualification automatically, and the outcome turns on whether the qualified matter reaches the subject matter of the schedule. Here the omitted depreciation affects carrying amounts and profit or loss, while the schedule presents original cost only, so a properly reasoned unmodified opinion on the schedule is available. The lender's consistency argument in option 1 states the very assumption the rule rejects; the finance director's absolute in option 2 is equally wrong because the effect must still be determined; option 3 imports a consequence the source attaches to no modified opinion.

questions.category: SA 805 – Qualified Opinion on Complete Set
questions.question:
CASE: CA Prakash Iyer is engaged both to audit the complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Sunfield Textiles Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2024 and to report on a schedule of tangible assets as at 31 March 2024 required by an asset-financing lender. The schedule presents only the original cost of acquisition of specified plant and machinery and, under the special purpose basis prescribed in the lender's agreement, excludes accumulated depreciation and carrying amounts. In his report on the complete set dated 30 June 2024 the auditor qualified the opinion solely because depreciation on plant acquired on 1 February 2024 had not been provided, the effect being confined to carrying value of plant, accumulated depreciation, the statement of profit and loss and related disclosures. The plant concerned is included in the schedule at cost. The lender asks that the opinion on the schedule also be qualified for consistency, while the company's finance director insists that no qualification on the schedule is permissible in any circumstances.

Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The three conditions which permit an unmodified opinion after an adverse or disclaimer of opinion on the complete set apply equally where the complete set carries only a qualified opinion.
**Statement 2:** In judging the relevance of the qualified matter to the schedule, the auditor may have regard to the pervasiveness of that matter and to the nature and extent of the difference between the applicable financial reporting frameworks.
**Statement 3:** If the auditor concludes that the qualified matter also affects the schedule, the auditor shall modify (qualify) the opinion expressed on the schedule.
**Statement 4:** Because accumulated depreciation is not presented in the schedule, the auditor is precluded from ever expressing an unmodified opinion on it.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only.
2 and 3 only.
1, 2 and 3 only.
2, 3 and 4 only.
questions.explanation: The three cumulative conditions, namely no legal prohibition, no publication together with the report containing the adverse or disclaimer opinion, and the element not constituting a major portion, are attached by the source only to an adverse or disclaimer of opinion on the complete set, so Statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 correctly applies the relevance factors, both pervasiveness of the matter described and difference between applicable financial reporting frameworks being listed factors, and both are engaged because the schedule follows the lender's special purpose basis. Statement 3 states the second limb of the qualified opinion rule, the auditor qualifying the opinion on the element where the determination of effect shows that it is appropriate. Statement 4 inverts the rule, since a matter confined to a presentation element absent from the schedule is precisely the case in which an unmodified opinion on the schedule may be appropriate once the effect has been determined.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Where the auditor has disclaimed an opinion on the complete set of financial statements of an entity, the auditor may nevertheless express an unmodified opinion on that entity's statement of profit and loss for the same period, provided no law or regulation prohibits such reporting and the report on the statement is issued in a document separate from the report containing the disclaimer.
**Reason (R):** For the purposes of this exception, a single financial statement is deemed to constitute a major portion of the complete set of financial statements.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The statement of profit and loss is a single financial statement, not a specific element, and the source expressly provides that where an adverse or disclaimer of opinion has been expressed on the complete set the auditor shall not express an unmodified opinion on a single financial statement. Reason R states the underlying rationale correctly, namely that a single financial statement is deemed to constitute a major portion, which is why the third condition of the element exception can never be met for a single financial statement. Since R is correct and A is wrong, the correct pairing is the last option. The attractive error in A is to treat the satisfaction of the legal prohibition and publication conditions as sufficient, when the major portion condition operates automatically and adversely against any single financial statement.

questions.category: SA 805 – Relevance of Matters in Complete-Set Report
questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** In considering whether a key audit matter described in the auditor's report on the complete set of financial statements is relevant to an engagement to report on a specific element of those financial statements, the auditor shall have regard to the extent to which that matter relates to the specific element.
**Reason (R):** An auditor who has expressed an adverse opinion on the complete set of financial statements shall not express an unmodified opinion on a single financial statement of that entity.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is correct: among the factors relevant in considering the implications of a matter included in the report on the complete set is the nature of the matter described and the extent to which it relates to the single financial statement or specific element. Reason R is also a correct statement of the source, a single financial statement being deemed to constitute a major portion so that the exception for specific elements is unavailable. However R says nothing about how the relevance of a key audit matter is evaluated, and it addresses a single financial statement whereas A addresses a specific element, so R cannot explain A. The trap in this question is the temptation to treat two rules drawn from the same table row as logically connected when they operate on different subject matter and for different purposes.

questions.category: SA 805 – Unmodified Opinion on Element after Adverse/Disclaimer
questions.question:
Match each situation in Column I with the reporting consequence in Column II. In every situation the auditor has also been appointed to report on the item mentioned.
Column I:
A. Disclaimer of opinion on the complete set of financial statements; unmodified opinion sought on a schedule of disbursements in relation to lease property constituting about 2% of total assets; no legal prohibition; the report on the schedule is issued as a standalone document.
B. Adverse opinion on the complete set of financial statements; unmodified opinion sought on the balance sheet; no legal prohibition; the report on the balance sheet is issued as a standalone document.
C. Qualified opinion on the complete set of financial statements on a matter which the auditor, on determining the effect, concludes also affects the specific element on which he is reporting.
D. Adverse opinion on the complete set of financial statements; unmodified opinion sought on a schedule of bank balances constituting about 1% of total assets in a standalone report; however the statute governing the entity prohibits the issue of an unmodified report on any element while the complete set carries an adverse opinion.
Column II:
1. Permitted, all three conditions of the exception being satisfied.
2. Not permitted, the deeming rule applicable to a single financial statement defeating the major portion condition.
3. The auditor shall modify (qualify) the opinion expressed on the specific element.
4. Not permitted, the first condition of the exception not being satisfied.
questions.explanation: Situation A is the paradigm case for the exception: a specific element that is plainly not a major portion, no legal bar and no publication together, so consequence 1 applies. In situation B the balance sheet is a single financial statement, which is deemed to constitute a major portion, so consequence 2 follows however small the auditor might regard it. Situation C is governed by the separate qualified opinion rule, under which the auditor determines the effect and, having concluded the matter affects the element, qualifies the opinion on it, that being consequence 3. Situation D fails the very first condition because the statute prohibits the reporting, and the absence of the other two obstacles is irrelevant since the conditions are cumulative.

questions.question:
Nirmal & Co. audited the complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Kalyani Granites Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2024 and issued an adverse opinion because mineral exploration expenditure of Rs. 228 crore had been charged to profit or loss instead of being capitalised, an error the auditor regards as material and pervasive. The firm is also engaged to report on a schedule of tangible assets as at 31 March 2024 prepared for a debenture trustee on the same Ind AS basis. That schedule carries a gross block of Rs. 305 crore, out of total assets of Rs. 410 crore in the complete set, and Rs. 228 crore of the block is the disputed mineral exploration asset. The report on the schedule will be issued as a separate document, and no law or regulation prohibits reporting on the schedule. Management argues that since the other two conditions are met the auditor is free to give a clean opinion on the schedule.

Which of the following is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: An unmodified opinion may be expressed, because for a specific element the major portion question is deemed to be answered in the auditor's favour.
An unmodified opinion may be expressed, because conditions (i) and (ii) having been satisfied the element may be reported upon.
An unmodified opinion shall not be expressed, because the specific element constitutes a major portion of the complete set of financial statements.
No opinion at all shall be expressed on the schedule, because an adverse opinion on the complete set of financial statements always precludes reporting on a specific element.
questions.explanation: For a specific element the third condition requires an actual assessment of whether the element constitutes a major portion of the complete set, and the deeming rule operates only for a single financial statement and only against the auditor. On these facts the schedule covers a gross block of Rs. 305 crore out of total assets of Rs. 410 crore, and the very asset that produced the adverse opinion is inside it, so the element is plainly a major portion and condition (iii) is not satisfied. Because the three conditions are cumulative, the absence of any legal prohibition and the separate issue of the report cannot cure that failure, which disposes of option 2. Option 1 misstates the deeming rule, which exists for single financial statements only; option 4 is too wide, since the exception is available for elements that genuinely are not a major portion.

questions.category: SA 805 – Unmodified Opinion on Element after Adverse/Disclaimer
questions.question: In which one of the following situations may the auditor express an unmodified opinion on the subject matter indicated, given that the auditor's report on the complete set of financial statements of the entity contains a disclaimer of opinion?
options: The auditor reports unmodified on the statement of cash flows of the same year for which the complete set was disclaimed, the report being issued as a separate document and there being no legal prohibition.

The auditor reports unmodified on a schedule of externally managed assets and income of a welfare fund representing about 4% of total assets, the report being circulated only to the fund's trustees, not published together with the disclaimer report, and no law or regulation prohibiting such reporting.
The auditor reports unmodified on a schedule of tangible assets representing about 6% of total assets, both reports being printed as annexures to the same annual report of the entity.

The auditor reports unmodified on a schedule of rental income of a specified building representing about 3% of total assets, the report being a separate document, save that the entity's governing statute requires that no unmodified report be issued on any element while the complete set carries a modified opinion.
questions.explanation: An unmodified opinion after a disclaimer on the complete set requires all three conditions together, namely no legal or regulatory prohibition, an auditor's report not published together with the report containing the disclaimer, and a specific element that does not constitute a major portion. Only the second situation satisfies each of them: the schedule is a specific element of small relative size, it goes only to the trustees, and nothing in law stands in the way. The first situation fails because a statement of cash flows is a single financial statement, which is deemed to be a major portion, so the third condition cannot be met. The third situation fails on publication together, an annexure of the same annual report being the same document, and the fourth fails because the statute prohibits the reporting.

questions.category: SA 805 – Relevance of Matters in Complete-Set Report
questions.question:
Zed & Co. reported on the complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Bramble Foods Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2024, signing the report on 30 May 2024. That report included a Key Audit Matter on the recognition of export incentive receivables arising from shipments made during FY 2023-24, and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on a pending income tax appeal relating to FY 2020-21. In August 2024 the firm is appointed to report on a schedule of export incentive claims arising on shipments made during the quarter ended 30 June 2024, that is, a period falling wholly after the year end covered by the complete set, and prepared on the same Ind AS basis. The firm regards the matters in its earlier report as of doubtful relevance to this engagement.

Which factor listed in the source most directly supports that view?
options: The extent of difference between the period covered by the complete set of financial statements and the period of the specific element.
The time elapsed since the date of the auditor's report on the complete set of financial statements.
The pervasiveness of the matter described in the auditor's report on the complete set of financial statements.
The nature and extent of the difference between the applicable financial reporting frameworks governing the complete set and this schedule.
questions.explanation: Among the factors relevant in considering whether a matter in the report on the complete set bears on an element engagement is the extent of difference between the period covered by the complete set and the period of the single financial statement or element. Here the Key Audit Matter is tied to shipments made during FY 2023-24 while the schedule covers shipments in the quarter ended 30 June 2024, a period falling wholly outside the earlier report, which is what makes that matter doubtful in relevance. Lapse of time is a weak support because barely two months have passed since 30 May 2024, so option 2 does not distinguish the two engagements. Option 4 is inapplicable because both the complete set and the schedule follow Ind AS, and option 3 addresses how far a matter spreads rather than when it arose.

questions.category: SA 805 – Qualified Opinion on Complete Set
questions.question:
CASE: Beneil & Co. audited the complete set of Ind AS financial statements of Kalpvriksh Agro Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2024 and qualified the opinion because a capital subsidy of Rs. 17 crore had been credited to the statement of profit and loss instead of being treated as deferred income, the effects being material but not pervasive. The firm is separately engaged to report on the company's statement of cash flows for the same year, prepared on the same Ind AS basis, and its report on that statement will be issued as a standalone document. The firm has determined that the classification of the subsidy does not affect any amount reported in the statement of cash flows, since the subsidy was received in cash and appears in investing activities whichever head is credited.

Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The auditor shall determine the effect of the qualification on the complete set of financial statements on the report on the statement of cash flows.
**Statement 2:** Because a single financial statement is deemed to constitute a major portion of the complete set of financial statements, the auditor cannot express an unmodified opinion on the statement of cash flows.
**Statement 3:** Since the auditor has determined the effect of the qualification and considers it appropriate, the auditor may express an unmodified opinion on the statement of cash flows.
**Statement 4:** Where the opinion on the complete set of financial statements is qualified, the opinion on any single financial statement must also be qualified.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only.
2 and 4 only.
1 and 3 only.
1, 3 and 4 only.
questions.explanation: The qualified opinion rule requires the auditor to determine the effect of the qualification on the report on the single financial statement or specific element and to modify that opinion only if deemed appropriate, which makes Statements 1 and 3 correct and Statement 4 wrong in its absolutism. The deeming rule in Statement 2 is a real rule but it operates within the different exception that governs an adverse or disclaimer of opinion on the complete set, where a single financial statement is deemed a major portion and an unmodified opinion is therefore unavailable. That exception is not triggered by a qualification which is not pervasive, so the statement of cash flows is not barred from a clean opinion merely because it is a single financial statement. The decisive fact is the degree of the modification on the complete set together with the auditor's determination that the subsidy's classification does not affect reported cash flows.

questions.category: SA 805 – Unmodified Opinion on Element after Adverse/Disclaimer
questions.question:
Sahil Gandhi & Co. has expressed a disclaimer of opinion on the complete set of financial statements of Ornate Ceramics Ltd for the year ended 31 March 2024 because accounting records of three manufacturing units were destroyed by fire and sufficient appropriate audit evidence could not be obtained. The firm is also engaged to report on a schedule of the company's bank balances as at 31 March 2024 for a joint-venture partner, the schedule representing about 2% of total assets, the balances having been confirmed and audited in full, and no law or regulation prohibiting such reporting.

In which one of the following manners of issuing the report on the schedule would the condition that the opinion not be expressed in a report published together with the report containing the disclaimer NOT be defeated?
options: The report on the schedule is printed on the page immediately following the report on the complete set in the company's annual report.
The report on the schedule is issued as a separate document to the joint-venture partner, while the report on the complete set appears in the company's annual report.
The report on the schedule is bound within the annual report but is preceded by a divider and carries its own distinct heading.
The report on the schedule is appended to the complete set of financial statements as Annexure III of the same booklet.
questions.explanation: The condition is directed at whether the two opinions are contained in auditor's reports that are published together, so the test concerns the identity and circulation of the document rather than the internal presentation of its pages. Issuing the report on the schedule as a separate document to the joint-venture partner leaves the disclaimer report in the annual report and satisfies that condition, the other two conditions being met on these facts since the schedule is a small specific element and nothing in law prohibits the reporting. Options 0, 2 and 3 all keep the report on the schedule inside the annual report, so the two reports remain published together; a divider, a distinct heading or numbering as an annexure differentiates the presentation of the schedule but does not separate the reports. This is the point at which the general treatment of publishing an element alongside the complete set stops helping the auditor, because the disclaimer exception refuses that arrangement altogether.

questions.question:
Devanahalli Pharma Ltd has prepared a one-page 'Summary of Financial Results' for FY 2025-26 showing only revenue, total income, profit before depreciation and tax, profit after tax and earnings per share, whereas the audited financial statements for the same year run to 118 pages. The summary adopts the same order of items and the same major headings as the audited financial statements and states that it is derived from the audited financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026, on which M/s Kulkarni & Co, the statutory auditors, have reported.
**Statement 1:** The summary may contain less detail than the audited financial statements and still be summary financial statements to which SA 810 applies.
**Statement 2:** Because the summary omits notes, depreciation and fixed asset details, it ceases to be a structured representation consistent with that provided by the audited financial statements and therefore falls outside SA 810.
**Statement 3:** SA 810 deals with the auditor's responsibilities when undertaking an engagement to report on summary financial statements derived from financial statements audited as per the Standards on Auditing, ordinarily by the same auditor.
**Statement 4:** The mere reference in the summary to the audited financial statements and to the report of M/s Kulkarni & Co is by itself sufficient to establish that the summary financial statements are not misleading.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 810 covers an engagement to report on summary financial statements derived from financial statements audited as per the SAs, ordinarily by the same auditor, and summary financial statements by definition contain less detail than the financial statements while providing a structured representation consistent with that provided by the financial statements. Statement 1 and Statement 3 state these two limbs correctly. Statement 2 fails because reduction of detail is exactly what a summary is expected to show; what must be preserved is consistency of structured representation, which the identical order of items and major headings supplies. Statement 4 is wrong because whether the applied criteria will result in summary financial statements that are not misleading is a separate factor in judging acceptability of the criteria, and a cross-reference to the audited statements is not the test of it.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** While reporting on summary financial statements, the auditor must be satisfied that the summary gives a structured representation consistent with that provided by the audited financial statements, and not merely that each figure appearing in the summary is drawn from the audited financial statements.
**Reason (R):** Summary financial statements are permitted to contain less detail than the audited financial statements, and therefore SA 810 dispenses with any requirement that the presentation of the summary be consistent with the presentation of the audited financial statements.
In the context of SA 810, which of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is incorrect
A is incorrect but R is correct
questions.explanation: The source definition has two limbs joined by 'but': summary financial statements contain less detail than the financial statements yet provide a structured representation consistent with that provided by the financial statements. The Assertion captures the second limb correctly, so it is correct. The Reason states the first limb truly but draws the opposite conclusion from it, and that conclusion is wrong; reduced detail is a permitted compression of content, not a licence to rearrange or re-present the structure. Reading only 'less detail' and ignoring 'consistent structured representation' is the classic incomplete reading the Reason illustrates, so A is correct and R is incorrect.

questions.question: M/s Advait & Associates audited the financial statements of Ramanathapuram Cotton Mills Ltd for FY 2024-25. For FY 2025-26 the shareholders entrusted the audit to a different firm, M/s Sheshadri & Co. In January 2027 the board approaches M/s Advait & Associates and asks them to report on the summary financial statements for FY 2025-26, which have been prepared from the financial statements audited by M/s Sheshadri & Co. M/s Advait & Associates have adequate staff, are willing to charge the fee quoted by the board, and have no independence objection of any kind. What is the MOST APPROPRIATE conclusion?
options: They may accept, because capacity, staff availability and the fee arrangements are the matters that govern acceptance of an engagement to report on summary financial statements, and all three are in order here.

They may accept, because SA 810 applies to summary financial statements derived from financial statements audited as per the SAs, and the source financial statements for FY 2025-26 were audited as per the SAs by a duly appointed firm.

They must accept, because the summary financial statements are for FY 2025-26 and they audited the immediately preceding year, which establishes the continuity of involvement that the standard expects.
Ordinarily they should not accept, because SA 810 contemplates acceptance of such an engagement only when the auditor has himself been engaged to audit the source financial statements.
questions.explanation: SA 810 pairs two qualified expressions: the auditor shall 'ordinarily' accept an engagement to report on summary financial statements 'only when' he has been engaged to conduct the audit of the financial statements from which the summary is derived. Here the FY 2025-26 audit was performed by another firm, so the condition attaching to acceptance is absent and, ordinarily, the engagement should not be accepted. Availability of staff and fee (option 1) and the mere fact that the source statements were audited as per the SAs (option 2) address the scope of the standard, not the identity condition in the acceptance requirement. Auditing the previous year (option 3) is not the audit of the source financial statements and therefore does not satisfy the condition.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements made by an audit principal while planning the acceptance of an engagement to report on summary financial statements:
**Statement 1:** 'Applied criteria' means the criteria applied by management in the preparation of the summary financial statements.
**Statement 2:** Where the criteria have been established by a recognised organisation, the auditor is bound to treat them as acceptable and need not consider the nature of the entity.
**Statement 3:** Nature of the entity, purpose of the summary financial statements, information needs of the intended users of the summary financial statements, and whether the applied criteria will result in summary financial statements that are not misleading, are factors affecting the determination of acceptability of the applied criteria.
**Statement 4:** Criteria may also be established by law or regulation, and in such a case the auditor may presume that such criteria are acceptable.
Which of the statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The requirement before accepting is to determine whether the applied criteria are acceptable, applied criteria being those applied by management in preparing the summary financial statements, so Statement 1 is a correct definition. The four listed factors are exactly the factors the source identifies, so Statement 3 is correct. The presumption available where criteria are established by a recognised organisation or by law or regulation is expressed as 'may presume', i.e. permissive, which Statement 4 states correctly and Statement 2 misstates by converting it into a binding rule that displaces the nature-of-entity factor. The trap in Statement 2 is twofold: it upgrades a permission into a duty and treats the presumption as obliterating one of the four acceptability factors.

questions.question:
Match the fact situations in Column I with the factor affecting the acceptability of the applied criteria under SA 810 that each most directly engages in Column II.
Column I
A. The summarisation format keeps a single captive power generation segment line for a company that owns a generation business, an equipment leasing arm and a construction joint venture.
B. The summary financial statements are to be circulated as the financial annexure to a notice seeking shareholder approval for a merger, not as a general annual communication.
C. The summary is being sent to the holders of privately placed bonds whose representatives have stated that they need liquidity and covenant data.
D. The format nets deferred tax assets against deferred tax liabilities and drops every disclosure of a pending environmental prosecution which dominates the company's public correspondence.
Column II
1. Purpose of the summary financial statements
2. Information needs of the intended users of the summary financial statements
3. Nature of the entity
4. Whether the applied criteria will result in summary financial statements that are not misleading
Choose the correct matching:
questions.explanation: The four acceptability factors are distinct questions and each situation keys to one of them. A places a single aggregated segment line against a generation, leasing and construction joint-venture group, which is a mismatch with the nature of the entity. B identifies the specific reason for issuing the summary, that is its purpose as a financial annexure to a merger notice. C turns on what a defined class of users needs to know, that is the information needs of the intended users of the summary financial statements. D concerns distortion produced by the criteria themselves, that is whether the applied criteria will result in summary financial statements that are not misleading, which is a separate factor and not merely a restatement of information needs; option 4 misassigns D to information needs and B to the not-misleading factor.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the agreement the auditor obtains from management before accepting an engagement to report on summary financial statements:
**Statement 1:** Management must acknowledge its responsibility for preparation of the summary financial statements as per the applied criteria.
**Statement 2:** Management must acknowledge its responsibility to make the audited financial statements available to the intended users of the summary financial statements without difficulty.
**Statement 3:** Management may acknowledge a responsibility to make the audited financial statements available to the auditor on request within thirty days of the date of the auditor's report.
**Statement 4:** Management must acknowledge its responsibility to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in the annual report alone.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
3 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The three responsibilities on which agreement must be obtained are preparation of the summary financial statements as per the applied criteria, making the audited financial statements available to intended users of the summary without difficulty, and including the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing the summary financial statements. Statements 1 and 2 reproduce the first two accurately, so they are correct statements. Statement 3 distorts the second: the duty runs to the intended users of the summary and is to be discharged without difficulty, not to the auditor within a thirty-day window, and the source prescribes no such period. Statement 4 narrows the third duty to the annual report, whereas the requirement covers any document containing the summary financial statements; therefore 3 and 4 are the statements that are not correct.

questions.question: Cholanagudem Sugars Ltd is not obliged by any statute to publish summary financial statements. Its chief financial officer has prepared the summary financial statements for FY 2025-26 on a proforma drafted by the company's own financial consultant, which nets deferred tax assets against deferred tax liabilities and drops the segment reporting note. The company's bank consortium uses the summary to monitor covenant compliance, and the summary will also be posted on the company website for retail investors. The auditor is considering acceptance of the engagement to report on this summary. Which of the following is the correct position?
options: The auditor may presume the applied criteria to be acceptable, since they were drawn up by a professional financial consultant engaged by the company himself, and a consultant of that standing must be treated as a recognised organisation for this purpose.

The presumption of acceptability is unavailable here, because the criteria were neither established by a recognised organisation nor by law or regulation, so the auditor must positively determine acceptability himself.

No examination of the criteria is needed at the acceptance stage, because the auditor's only concern before accepting is whether he has been engaged to audit the source financial statements, which he has.
The auditor may presume the criteria acceptable because the bank consortium, being the principal intended user of the summary, has approved the format in advance of circulation.
questions.explanation: SA 810 permits the auditor to presume criteria acceptable only where they have been established by a recognised organisation or by law or regulation. A proforma drafted by management's own consultant on management's instructions is a set of applied criteria applied by management in preparing the summary and attracts no presumption, so the auditor must positively determine acceptability by reference to the nature of the entity, the purpose of the summary financial statements, the information needs of the intended users and whether the criteria will result in a summary that is not misleading; dropping the segment note may suit neither a diversified sugar and cogeneration entity nor the covenant-monitoring purpose of the bank users. Options 1 and 4 wrongly extend the presumption to a self-interested adviser's format and to advance user approval, neither of which is a recognised body or a legal source, and option 3 omits the acceptance-stage requirement altogether.

questions.question:
Base facts: The proposed criteria for preparing the summary financial statements of Bettiah Ceramics Ltd for FY 2025-26 are those issued by a recognised industry organisation, and the auditor relies on the resulting position regarding their acceptability. Management gives the required acknowledgements and the auditor accepts the engagement.
Changed fact: The recognised organisation withdraws its format and management substitutes a set of criteria drafted by its own accounts department, which excludes all disclosure of related party borrowings.
Assuming nothing else changes, what is the consequence of the changed fact for the auditor's acceptance decision?
options: None, because the auditor's determination of acceptability of criteria is not made at the acceptance stage at all.
None, because criteria prepared by management are automatically the applied criteria and are therefore acceptable by definition.
The auditor must decline the engagement outright, because SA 810 does not permit management to apply its own criteria to summary financial statements and no such engagement may be accepted.

He loses the ability to presume the criteria acceptable and must determine acceptability himself, keeping in view the nature of the entity, the purpose of the summary, the information needs of intended users and whether the criteria will yield a summary that is not misleading.
questions.explanation: The presumption that criteria are acceptable is available only where they are established by a recognised organisation or by law or regulation, and it is expressed permissively as 'may presume'. When the recognised format is replaced by criteria drafted by management's own accounts department, the source of the presumption disappears and the auditor must carry out the affirmative determination of acceptability by reference to the four factors; the exclusion of related party borrowings will be tested chiefly through the not-misleading factor. Options 1 and 2 misstate the rule: determination of acceptability is expressly a pre-acceptance step and management's own criteria are not acceptable by definition. Option 3 overcorrects, since management-drafted criteria remain permissible and simply forfeit the presumption.

questions.question:
Match the practice adopted by a company in Column I with the factor affecting the auditor's evaluation of whether the audited financial statements are available to intended users of the summary financial statements without undue difficulty, in Column II.
Column I
A. The audited financial statements are placed on a publicly accessible filing portal maintained under law and can be downloaded by anyone for a nominal fee.
B. The summary carries the sentence: 'The full audited financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2026 may be obtained from the Company Secretary at the registered office during business hours.'
C. The board has approved a written procedure naming the Company Secretary as the officer responsible, with a published undertaking to dispatch a copy of the audited financial statements within three days to any person who received the summary and asks for one.
D. The summary states in bold that it contains less detail than the audited financial statements.
Column II
1. Summary financial statements describe clearly from whom or where the audited financial statements are available
2. Audited financial statements are on public record
3. Management has established a process by which intended users can obtain ready access to the audited financial statements
4. Not a factor affecting the evaluation of availability of the audited financial statements
Choose the correct matching:
questions.explanation: The source lists precisely three factors affecting the evaluation of availability without undue difficulty: the summary describing clearly from whom or where the audited financial statements are available, the audited financial statements being on public record, and management having established a process for ready access by intended users. A is public record, B identifies both the person and the place and so is the first factor, and C is an established process with a named responsible officer and a turnaround. D describes the summarised nature of the document, which is a characteristic of summary financial statements rather than one of the three availability factors, so it matches 4; option 3 tests whether the candidate can keep the availability factors separate from other content of the summary.

questions.question: Before accepting an engagement to report on the summary financial statements of Hosur Bearings Ltd, the auditor finds that the summarisation format used by management is prescribed by an insurance regulator through a circular binding on the company. He is also unable, after repeated requests, to obtain agreement from management that its report on the summary financial statements will be included in the company's quarterly investor newsletter, which reprints the summary. Which of the following conclusions is the LEAST APPROPRIATE?
options: The auditor may accept the engagement, because the presumption that criteria established by law or regulation are acceptable extends to management's responsibilities as well.
The auditor shall not accept the engagement, because he has been unable to obtain the required agreement from management.
The auditor shall not accept, since inability to obtain management's acknowledgement is a ground standing on its own, independent of the state of the applied criteria.
The auditor should inform the board that on the present terms the engagement to report on the summary financial statements cannot be accepted.
questions.explanation: The presumption arising from criteria established by a recognised organisation or by law or regulation is confined to the acceptability of the applied criteria; it says nothing about management's responsibilities, which require a separate agreement. That agreement must cover preparation as per the applied criteria, availability of the audited financial statements to intended users without difficulty, and inclusion of the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing the summary, which includes the newsletter reprinting it. The final row of the acceptance table gives two independent grounds for not accepting: unacceptable criteria, or inability to obtain management's agreement; the second, third and fourth conclusions correctly reflect that structure and its consequence, while the first option improperly transfers the criteria presumption into the agreement requirement, making it the least appropriate conclusion.

questions.question:
M/s Nandi & Associates are the statutory auditors of Kudremukh Iron Ore Ltd for FY 2025-26. The company proposes to publish summary financial statements for FY 2025-26 in a glossy 'Annual Digest' to be posted to about 42,000 small shareholders along with the notice of the annual general meeting. The summary financial statements will be prepared by applying the summarisation format issued by a recognised industry organisation. The digest will carry only the line that the full audited financial statements 'are available on the company's website'; the website in fact hosts just the last two quarters' results, the audited financial statements for FY 2025-26 are to be uploaded only after the annual general meeting, and no process has been decided for supplying copies to shareholders who ask for them. The finance head tells the auditors that the auditor's report will be printed in the statutory annual report but that the digest, being a marketing document, will not carry it. Nothing in the numbers is disputed and the applied criteria do not produce a summary that is misleading.
**Statement 1:** M/s Nandi & Associates may ordinarily accept the engagement, since they have been engaged to audit the financial statements from which the summary financial statements are derived.
**Statement 2:** Because the format applied is that of a recognised industry organisation, the auditors may presume the applied criteria to be acceptable.
**Statement 3:** The finance head's position about the digest is consistent with the acknowledgement the auditor must obtain from management.
**Statement 4:** The absence of any decided process for supplying copies of the audited financial statements bears on the auditor's evaluation of whether those statements will be available to the intended users of the digest without undue difficulty.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is right because the same firm audits the source financial statements for FY 2025-26, satisfying the condition on which the auditor ordinarily accepts. Statement 2 is right because criteria established by a recognised organisation attract a permissive presumption of acceptability, and the facts add that nothing in the summary is misleading. Statement 3 is wrong: management must acknowledge responsibility to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing the summary, and the digest is such a document, so excluding the report from it is inconsistent with that acknowledgement. Statement 4 is right, since one of the three availability factors is whether management has established a process by which intended users can obtain ready access to the audited financial statements, and here no process exists.

questions.question:
M/s Nandi & Associates are the statutory auditors of Kudremukh Iron Ore Ltd for FY 2025-26. The company proposes to publish summary financial statements for FY 2025-26 in a glossy 'Annual Digest' to be posted to about 42,000 small shareholders along with the notice of the annual general meeting. The summary financial statements will be prepared by applying the summarisation format issued by a recognised industry organisation. The digest will carry only the line that the full audited financial statements 'are available on the company's website'; the website in fact hosts just the last two quarters' results, the audited financial statements for FY 2025-26 are to be uploaded only after the annual general meeting, and no process has been decided for supplying copies to shareholders who ask for them. The finance head tells the auditors that the auditor's report will be printed in the statutory annual report but that the digest, being a marketing document, will not carry it. Nothing in the numbers is disputed and the applied criteria do not produce a summary that is misleading.
Which actions should M/s Nandi & Associates take before accepting the engagement to report on the summary financial statements?
**1.** Determine whether the applied criteria are acceptable, keeping in view the nature of the entity, the purpose of the summary financial statements, the information needs of the 42,000 intended users and whether the criteria will result in a summary that is not misleading.
**2.** Obtain management's agreement that it acknowledges its responsibility to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing them, the Annual Digest included.
**3.** Accept the engagement on the strength of the presumed acceptability of the criteria and leave availability of the audited financial statements and the printing of his report to be dealt with after the report is signed.
**4.** Evaluate whether the audited financial statements will be available to the intended users of the digest without difficulty, having regard to whether the summary describes from whom or where they are available, whether they are on public record and whether management has established a process for ready access.
Choose the correct set of actions:
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Before accepting, the auditor has two positive requirements: determine whether the applied criteria are acceptable, and obtain management's agreement to its three responsibilities, of which the availability of the audited financial statements to intended users without difficulty and inclusion of his report in any document containing the summary are directly engaged by these facts. Actions 1, 2 and 4 therefore belong to the acceptance stage, and action 4 uses exactly the three evaluation factors the source lists. Action 3 is wrong in two ways: the presumption that criteria of a recognised organisation are acceptable is permissive and does not displace the determination, and inability to obtain management's agreement is itself a ground for not accepting, so neither the availability question nor the printing of the report can be deferred until after the report is signed.

M/s Nandi & Associates are the statutory auditors of Kudremukh Iron Ore Ltd for FY 2025-26. The company proposes to publish summary financial statements for FY 2025-26 in a glossy 'Annual Digest' to be posted to about 42,000 small shareholders along with the notice of the annual general meeting. The summary financial statements will be prepared by applying the summarisation format issued by a recognised industry organisation. The digest will carry only the line that the full audited financial statements 'are available on the company's website'; the website in fact hosts just the last two quarters' results, the audited financial statements for FY 2025-26 are to be uploaded only after the annual general meeting, and no process has been decided for supplying copies to shareholders who ask for them. The finance head tells the auditors that the auditor's report will be printed in the statutory annual report but that the digest, being a marketing document, will not carry it. Nothing in the numbers is disputed and the applied criteria do not produce a summary that is misleading.
On the question of availability of the audited financial statements to the intended users of the digest, which of the following statements are correct?
**Statement 1:** The line that the audited financial statements 'are available on the company's website' does not, on these facts, describe clearly from whom or where the audited financial statements are available to a shareholder holding only the digest.
**Statement 2:** Because the digest is posted directly to shareholders, availability without difficulty stands established whatever the state of the website.
**Statement 3:** Management has not established a process by which intended users of the summary can obtain ready access to the audited financial statements.
**Statement 4:** The audited financial statements for FY 2025-26 are, on these facts, demonstrably on public record at the date of the digest.
options: 1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The auditor's evaluation of availability without undue difficulty is affected by three factors, and this case fails on two of them. Statement 1 is correct because the reference is to a website location that will not carry the FY 2025-26 audited financial statements until after the annual general meeting, so it does not clearly tell a digest reader from whom or where they are available; Statement 3 is correct because no process for ready access has been decided at all. Statement 2 is wrong because distribution of the summary is not distribution of the audited financial statements, and the acknowledgement required of management is an availability duty running to the intended users of the summary. Statement 4 is unsupported: nothing in the facts places the FY 2025-26 audited financial statements on public record at the date of the digest.

questions.question:
M/s Nandi & Associates are the statutory auditors of Kudremukh Iron Ore Ltd for FY 2025-26. The company proposes to publish summary financial statements for FY 2025-26 in a glossy 'Annual Digest' to be posted to about 42,000 small shareholders along with the notice of the annual general meeting. The summary financial statements will be prepared by applying the summarisation format issued by a recognised industry organisation. The digest will carry only the line that the full audited financial statements 'are available on the company's website'; the website in fact hosts just the last two quarters' results, the audited financial statements for FY 2025-26 are to be uploaded only after the annual general meeting, and no process has been decided for supplying copies to shareholders who ask for them. The finance head tells the auditors that the auditor's report will be printed in the statutory annual report but that the digest, being a marketing document, will not carry it. Nothing in the numbers is disputed and the applied criteria do not produce a summary that is misleading.
What is the correct conclusion on acceptance of the engagement in its present state?
options: Accept, because the applied criteria are those issued by a recognised industry organisation, may therefore be presumed acceptable, and the facts record no dispute about the numbers.
Decline the engagement outright, because a summary posted to 42,000 small shareholders without the audited financial statements attached must mislead them.
Accept on the present terms and ask the company to publish the digest without the summary financial statements, so that only the statutory annual report carries them.

Do not accept while matters stand, since management has not acknowledged that his report will appear in any document containing the summary and the availability position for the digest's readers is unresolved.
questions.explanation: Two pre-acceptance requirements remain unmet. Management must acknowledge responsibility to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing them, and the finance head expressly denies this for the digest; and the auditor cannot evaluate availability of the audited financial statements to the 42,000 intended users favourably when the website does not yet carry those statements and no process for ready access has been decided. The concluding row of the acceptance table directs that where he is unable to obtain management's agreement the auditor shall not accept, which is option 4. Option 1 is wrong because a presumption of acceptability of the criteria does not substitute for that agreement; option 2 misstates the reason for refusal, since the facts record that the applied criteria do not produce a misleading summary; and option 3 substitutes a suggestion about the company's publishing plan for the requirement the standard actually imposes.

questions.question: M/s Pillai & Raman are approached to report on the summary financial statements of Viraj Aluminium Ltd for FY 2025-26, which they have also been engaged to audit. Two features emerge during acceptance planning. First, the criteria applied by management in preparing the summary exclude all related party transactions and all contingent liabilities, although the company faces an environmental claim its lawyers estimate at Rs 78 crore, and the auditors are unable to conclude that these criteria will result in a summary that is not misleading. Second, management declines to acknowledge any responsibility for preparation of the summary financial statements in accordance with the applied criteria, saying that this is the auditors' concern and not theirs. No criteria have been established by any recognised organisation, law or regulation. What conclusion should the auditors reach?
options: They may accept, because neither ground taken by itself would justify refusing the engagement.
They shall not accept the engagement, because each of the unacceptable applied criteria and the inability to obtain management's agreement is independently a sufficient ground for not accepting.
They shall not accept only if both grounds co-exist, since the acceptance table conditions refusal on the two failures occurring together.
They may accept provided the auditors' report on the summary financial statements describes the excluded items and the management's refusal.
questions.explanation: The concluding row of the acceptance table is disjunctive: if the auditor concludes that the applied criteria are unacceptable, or is unable to obtain agreement from management, he shall not accept such engagement. Here both limbs of the disjunction are satisfied, but only one is needed, and the criteria limb is engaged because the auditor cannot conclude that management-drafted criteria will yield a summary that is not misleading while no presumption of acceptability is available in the absence of a recognised organisation, law or regulation. Option 3 inverts the disjunction into a conjunction, which is the principal trap in this drafting. Option 4 confuses an acceptance-stage bar with a reporting-stage remedy, and no form of report can cure a refusal to acknowledge management's responsibility for preparation as per the applied criteria.

questions.question: Kalinga Textiles Mills Ltd will publish summary financial statements for FY 2025-26 together with the auditor's report in its printed annual report. The company also intends to reproduce the same summary financial statements, without the auditor's report, in a quarterly investor newsletter that carries commentary on order inflows, and its finance director argues that the report has been included once already so no further inclusion is needed. The applied criteria are those prescribed by the sectoral regulator, the audited financial statements are filed and available on a public portal, and the summary states that the audit was performed by the same firm that is asked to report on the summary. What is the correct position of the auditor at the acceptance stage?
options: The requirement is satisfied, because the annual report is the only document to which the responsibility for including the auditor's report on the summary financial statements attaches and the newsletter is a separate publication.
It is sufficient if the newsletter carries a prominent cross-reference to the annual report in which the auditor's report on the summary financial statements has been printed.
The responsibility arises only where the summary financial statements are accompanied by the audited financial statements, which the newsletter will not be.
Management must acknowledge responsibility to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing them, which the newsletter reprinting the summary is.
questions.explanation: The third responsibility on which agreement must be obtained from management is to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in any document containing the summary financial statements. A quarterly newsletter reprinting the summary is such a document, and the 'included once already' argument reads the words 'any document' out of the requirement, so option 4 states the correct position and option 1 does not. Option 2 substitutes a cross-reference for the report itself, which the responsibility does not contemplate; option 3 wrongly links the responsibility to the audited financial statements being supplied with the summary, which is a separate responsibility in the same list. The regulator-prescribed criteria may make options 1 and 2 superficially attractive, but a presumption of acceptability of criteria has no bearing on the agreement the auditor must obtain.

questions.question:
While framing its acceptance checklist for engagements to report on summary financial statements, a firm records the following four statements:
**Statement 1:** Where the criteria applied in preparing the summary financial statements have been established by law or regulation, the auditor may presume such criteria to be acceptable.
**Statement 2:** The presumption in Statement 1 also relieves the auditor of the need to obtain management's acknowledgement of its responsibilities.
**Statement 3:** If the auditor concludes that the applied criteria are unacceptable, he shall not accept the engagement.
**Statement 4:** 'Applied criteria' means the criteria applied by the auditor in evaluating whether the summary financial statements are consistent with the audited financial statements.
Which of the statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly states the permissive presumption attaching to criteria established by a recognised organisation or by law or regulation, and Statement 3 correctly states one of the two independent grounds on which the auditor shall not accept the engagement. Statement 2 fails because the presumption reaches only the acceptability of the applied criteria; the agreement from management on its three responsibilities is a separate and additional pre-acceptance requirement. Statement 2 is the more tempting error and Statement 4 the more fundamental one, since applied criteria are the criteria applied by management in preparation of the summary financial statements, not a yardstick constructed by the auditor during his evaluation, so the correct set is 1 and 3 only.

questions.question:
An auditor is approached by a company to report on its summary financial statements. The following steps are stated out of order:
**1.** Obtaining agreement from management that it acknowledges its responsibilities in respect of the summary financial statements.
**2.** Determining whether the applied criteria, that is the criteria applied by management in preparing the summary financial statements, are acceptable.
**3.** Forming the view that he has been engaged to conduct the audit of the financial statements from which the summary financial statements are derived.
**4.** Accepting the engagement to report on the summary financial statements, failing which, on unacceptable criteria or failure to obtain management's agreement, not accepting it.
Which of the following represents the correct order in which these steps are completed under SA 810?
questions.explanation: The identity condition comes first in logic and in the standard: the auditor ordinarily accepts an engagement to report on summary financial statements only when he has been engaged to audit the financial statements from which they are derived, so step 3 precedes the pre-acceptance requirements. Those requirements are then discharged in the order the acceptance table sets them out, namely determination of whether the applied criteria are acceptable, followed by obtaining management's agreement to its three responsibilities, after which the accept or not-accept conclusion is reached, so the sequence is 3, 2, 1, 4. Option 4 places the management agreement before the criteria determination, which would let the auditor seek acknowledgements against criteria he has not yet found acceptable, and options 2 and 3 fail to place the identity condition first, which is the condition to which the ordinary acceptance requirement is attached.

questions.category: SA 810 – Procedures: Availability Description When Not Accompanied
questions.question:
Case: Meera Fortifies Ltd. completed its audit for the year ended 31st March, 2025 and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was dated 25th July, 2025. The auditor was separately engaged to report on the company's summary financial statements and signed that report on 22nd August, 2025. The summary financial statements were issued to shareholders as a standalone four-page circular; the audited financial statements were not attached to or sent with it. The circular is titled 'Abridged Financial Statements derived from Audited Financial Statements for the year ended 31st March, 2025', reproduces in Note 1 the criteria applied by management in preparing them, and ends with a statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements. The circular nowhere states from whom or where the audited financial statements can be obtained, they are not on public record, and management has not set up any process by which shareholders can obtain them. On 5th August, 2025 one of the company's two warehouse blocks was destroyed by fire.

On these facts, which is the correct position regarding the auditor's procedures under SA 810?
options: Availability of the audited financial statements was already secured by the agreement obtained from management before the engagement was accepted, so nothing remains for the auditor to evaluate on this aspect while reporting.

The closing statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements itself informs the shareholder from whom or where the audited financial statements can be had.

The auditor's only remedy is to insist that the audited financial statements be placed on public record, that being the sole route to availability which the standard contemplates for a document of this kind.

Here the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements, so the auditor must evaluate whether they clearly describe from whom or where those statements are available, and they do not.

The evaluation of whether the summary financial statements describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available arises only where the two are issued together, so it is not engaged on these facts.
questions.explanation: SA 810 lists among the procedures forming the basis of the auditor's opinion the evaluation, when the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements, of whether they clearly describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available. The decisive fact is that the circular is a standalone four-page document with the audited financial statements neither attached nor sent with it, and it nowhere indicates a source. The statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements is a different disclosure and supplies no address or source, so the second option fails. The first option confuses the acceptance-stage management agreement with the reporting-stage procedure, and the fifth inverts the conditional trigger. Public record is only one of the factors affecting the auditor's availability evaluation, not the exclusive remedy, so the third option is wrong.

questions.question:
Case: Meera Fortifies Ltd. completed its audit for the year ended 31st March, 2025 and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was dated 25th July, 2025. The auditor was separately engaged to report on the company's summary financial statements and signed that report on 22nd August, 2025. The summary financial statements were issued to shareholders as a standalone four-page circular; the audited financial statements were not attached to or sent with it. The circular is titled 'Abridged Financial Statements derived from Audited Financial Statements for the year ended 31st March, 2025', reproduces in Note 1 the criteria applied by management in preparing them, and ends with a statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements. The circular nowhere states from whom or where the audited financial statements can be obtained, they are not on public record, and management has not set up any process by which shareholders can obtain them. On 5th August, 2025 one of the company's two warehouse blocks was destroyed by fire.

Assume now that, instead of a standalone circular, the four-page summary had been sent together with a printed copy of the audited financial statements. What change in the auditor's obligations follows from this single change in fact?
options: The auditor would cease to evaluate whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty, physical delivery being complete proof of availability.

The description evaluation would cease to be triggered, but the evaluation of whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty would still have to be made.
Both the evaluation of availability without difficulty and the evaluation of the description of the source would fall away, the user then holding the audited financial statements in hand.
The description evaluation would become mandatory in its own right and the evaluation of availability without difficulty would become a matter for the auditor's professional discretion.
Nothing would change, because describing from whom or where the audited financial statements are available is merely a second way of stating the evaluation of availability.
questions.explanation: The two procedures do different work: one asks whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty, and the other, expressed as a conditional, asks whether the summary financial statements clearly describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available where the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements. Attaching the audited financial statements removes the stated condition, so the description evaluation is no longer engaged, but it does not remove the separate standing evaluation of availability. The first option fails because availability remains an enumerated procedure irrespective of delivery; the third fails for the same reason as to the second procedure; the fifth collapses two distinct procedures into one; and the fourth reverses the trigger. The decisive fact is the shift from unaccompanied to accompanied issuance.

questions.question:
Case: Meera Fortifies Ltd. completed its audit for the year ended 31st March, 2025 and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was dated 25th July, 2025. The auditor was separately engaged to report on the company's summary financial statements and signed that report on 22nd August, 2025. The summary financial statements were issued to shareholders as a standalone four-page circular; the audited financial statements were not attached to or sent with it. The circular is titled 'Abridged Financial Statements derived from Audited Financial Statements for the year ended 31st March, 2025', reproduces in Note 1 the criteria applied by management in preparing them, and ends with a statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements. The circular nowhere states from whom or where the audited financial statements can be obtained, they are not on public record, and management has not set up any process by which shareholders can obtain them. On 5th August, 2025 one of the company's two warehouse blocks was destroyed by fire.

Which is the correct assessment of the circular's title by reference to the procedure concerning the summarised nature of the summary financial statements?
options: The title is sufficient for this procedure only because the closing statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements has been made, that statement doing the real work.
The title must additionally reproduce the criteria applied in preparation, because disclosing the summarised nature and disclosing the applied criteria are a single undivided requirement.
The title discloses the summarised nature of the document and identifies the audited financial statements from which it is derived, which is the manner SA 810's own illustration indicates.
The title is defective, since SA 810's illustration uses the word 'Summary' and a document headed 'Abridged' cannot satisfy the requirement.
The title must also carry the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, failing which the audited financial statements stand unidentified.
questions.explanation: The first enumerated procedure requires the auditor to evaluate whether the summary financial statements adequately disclose their summarised nature and identify the audited financial statements, and the source itself illustrates this with a title such as 'Summary/Abridged FS prepared/derived from Audited FS for year ended March 31, 20XX'. The Meera Fortifies title uses 'Abridged', the words 'derived from Audited Financial Statements' and the year reference, so all three illustrative elements are present. The second option merges that procedure with the separate requirement to evaluate whether the applied criteria are adequately disclosed; the fourth wrongly treats 'Abridged' as unavailable when the illustration offers it as an alternative to 'Summary'; and the fifth imports a requirement the source does not state. The first option substitutes a different disclosure for the title test, when the two are independent. The decisive fact is the wording of the heading itself.

Case: Meera Fortifies Ltd. completed its audit for the year ended 31st March, 2025 and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was dated 25th July, 2025. The auditor was separately engaged to report on the company's summary financial statements and signed that report on 22nd August, 2025. The summary financial statements were issued to shareholders as a standalone four-page circular; the audited financial statements were not attached to or sent with it. The circular nowhere states from whom or where the audited financial statements can be obtained, they are not on public record, and management has not set up any process by which shareholders can obtain them. On 5th August, 2025 one of the company's two warehouse blocks was destroyed by fire.

What is the correct position with respect to the destruction of the warehouse block on 5th August, 2025?
options: The auditor must report its effect in the report on the summary financial statements, because the fire occurred on a date earlier than that report and so falls within the period covered by it.
The auditor must determine whether the destruction of the warehouse requires adjustment or disclosure in the audited financial statements and, if it does, re-date the report on those statements.

No duty arises to report its effect, because the auditor reports on the summary financial statements after completion of the audit and the event occurred after the date of the report on the audited financial statements.
The auditor must report its effect only if the loss is material when measured against the summary financial statements taken as a whole, and not otherwise.

The position is the same as that governing events occurring between the balance sheet date and the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, the earlier report date being for this purpose irrelevant.
questions.explanation: Where the auditor reports on summary financial statements after completion of the audit of the financial statements, SA 810 provides that the auditor is not required to report on the effect of subsequent events which occurred after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, the stated reason being that the summary financial statements are derived from the audited financial statements. The reference date is therefore 25th July, 2025 and not 22nd August, 2025, and the fire of 5th August 2025 falls after it. The option resting the duty on the date of the report on the summary financial statements uses the wrong reference date, which is the most common error here; the option directing the auditor to revisit the audited financial statements revives a duty over statements already reported upon; the option conditioning the duty on materiality against the summary financial statements taken as a whole substitutes a screen the standard does not apply; and the option equating the position with the period up to the report on the audited financial statements treats the post-report-date period as if it were the subsequent-events window.

questions.category: SA 810 – Procedures: Applied Criteria vs Agreement
questions.question:
Case: Kanak Steel Girders Ltd prepared summary financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 2025 for circulation in its creditors' newsletter. The applied criteria, framed by the professional institute of which the company is a member and reproduced in Note 1 of the summary financial statements, require presentation of the summary balance sheet under five specified heads and disclosure of a minimum of seven line items in the summary profit and loss account.
