The auditor noticed three features: (1) the summary profit and loss account shows 'Profit for the year and total comprehensive income' of ₹ 214 crore, while the audited financial statements show ₹ 198 crore, management having lifted the figure from a draft circulated before the auditor's final numbers were settled; (2) the summary balance sheet presents only three heads, clubbing 'Financial Liabilities' with 'Other Liabilities', although every figure agrees with the audited financial statements, management contending that criteria drafted with its own involvement may be relaxed where the numbers tie; (3) the summary financial statements carry no reference to a customs demand of ₹ 12 crore disclosed as a contingency in the audited financial statements, management contending that a summary need not repeat every contingency.

Which of the following actions should the auditor take?
1. Treat feature (1) as a failure of the procedure of comparing the summary financial statements with the related information in the audited financial statements to determine whether they agree with it.
2. Treat feature (2) as a failure of the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria, notwithstanding that every figure agrees.
3. Treat feature (3) as going to the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements contain necessary information and are not misleading.
4. Accept management's contention on feature (2), on the view that the only test SA 810 applies to presentation is whether the figures agree.
options: 2 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: SA 810 enumerates preparation as per the applied criteria and comparison of the summary financial statements with the related information in the audited financial statements as two different procedures, so a defect can hit one without hitting the other. Feature (1) is an out-and-out disagreement of a figure with the audited financial statements, so the comparison procedure fails. Feature (2) is a departure from criteria which themselves require five heads, and agreement of the arithmetic cannot cure it, because conformity with criteria is a separate test. Feature (3) engages the requirement that the summary financial statements contain necessary information and not be misleading. Action 4 states the position the opposite way and is rejected, and with it every option containing it. The decisive facts are the ₹ 214 crore against ₹ 198 crore difference and the three-head presentation.

questions.category: SA 810 – Procedures: Necessary Information and Not Misleading
questions.question:
Case: Kanak Steel Girders Ltd prepared summary financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 2025 for circulation in its creditors' newsletter. The applied criteria, framed by the professional institute of which the company is a member and reproduced in Note 1 of the summary financial statements, require presentation of the summary balance sheet under five specified heads and disclosure of a minimum of seven line items in the summary profit and loss account. The auditor noticed three features: (1) the summary profit and loss account shows 'Profit for the year and total comprehensive income' of ₹ 214 crore, while the audited financial statements show ₹ 198 crore, management having lifted the figure from a draft circulated before the auditor's final numbers were settled; (2) the summary balance sheet presents only three heads, clubbing 'Financial Liabilities' with 'Other Liabilities', although every figure agrees with the audited financial statements, management contending that criteria drafted with its own involvement may be relaxed where the numbers tie; (3) the summary financial statements carry no reference to a customs demand of ₹ 12 crore disclosed as a contingency in the audited financial statements, management contending that a summary need not repeat every contingency.

Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: Feature (2) can be a defect under SA 810's procedures even though the summary figures agree item for item with the audited financial statements.
Statement 2: Feature (1) shows that the applied criteria are unacceptable, since a difference in a caption can arise only from bad criteria.
Statement 3: The evaluation of preparation as per the applied criteria and the comparison with the audited financial statements test the same thing, so performing one discharges the other.
Statement 4: Whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria is settled once and for all by management's responsibility acknowledged at the acceptance stage and is not re-tested as a procedure.
Which statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: a presentation which departs from criteria mandating five heads fails the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria even where every figure ties. Statement 2 is not, because a figure lifted from a superseded draft is a failure of the comparison procedure and says nothing about the acceptability of the criteria, which SA 810 deals with as an engagement acceptance matter. Statement 3 is not, because criteria conformity and arithmetical agreement with the related information in the audited financial statements are separately enumerated tests. Statement 4 is not, because preparation as per the applied criteria appears both in management's acknowledged responsibility and, independently, in the list of procedures performed as the basis for the auditor's opinion. The decisive point is that the two Kanak Steel defects engage two different procedures.

questions.question:
Case: Suratgarh Agro Products Ltd issued a booklet for the year ended 31st March, 2026 containing its summary financial statements headed simply 'Financial Statements for the year 2025-26'. The audited financial statements, together with the auditor's report on them dated 30th June, 2026, at which date the audit stood completed, were bound with the same booklet. The auditor, engaged to report on the summary financial statements, signed that report on 20th September, 2026. Before signing, the finance head sought two changes: (a) retention of the existing heading, since the booklet is meant for shareholders in rural areas who are unfamiliar with the word 'summary'; and (b) disclosure in the summary financial statements of a dividend declared by the board on 12th August, 2026, on the ground that the auditor must deal with every event up to the date of his own report.

Consider the following statements:
Statement 1: The heading fails to disclose the summarised nature of the statements and to identify the audited financial statements, so the first enumerated procedure is not satisfied.
Statement 2: Because the audited financial statements are bound with the booklet, the auditor is relieved of evaluating whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty.
Statement 3: The evaluation of whether the summary financial statements clearly describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available is not triggered on these facts.
Statement 4: The auditor must report the effect of the dividend declared on 12th August, 2026 because it preceded the date of his report on the summary financial statements.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Procedure (i) requires an evaluation of whether the summary financial statements adequately disclose their summarised nature and identify the audited financial statements, and a heading reading merely 'Financial Statements for the year 2025-26' does neither, however literate the readership. Procedure (iii), by its own terms, bites only when the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements; here they are bound together, so it is not triggered, which makes Statement 3 correct. Statement 2 is wrong because the evaluation of availability without difficulty is a standing procedure and is not switched off by the same fact that switches off procedure (iii); that is precisely the distinction between the two. Statement 4 is wrong because the relevant reference date is the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, namely 30th June, 2026, and the dividend of 12th August, 2026 falls after it.

questions.question:
Case: Suratgarh Agro Products Ltd issued a booklet for the year ended 31st March, 2026 containing its summary financial statements headed simply 'Financial Statements for the year 2025-26'. The audited financial statements, together with the auditor's report on them dated 30th June, 2026, at which date the audit stood completed, were bound with the same booklet. The auditor, engaged to report on the summary financial statements, signed that report on 20th September, 2026. Before signing, the finance head sought two changes: (a) retention of the existing heading, since the booklet is meant for shareholders in rural areas who are unfamiliar with the word 'summary'; and (b) disclosure in the summary financial statements of a dividend declared by the board on 12th August, 2026, on the ground that the auditor must deal with every event up to the date of his own report.

What is the MOST APPROPRIATE response to the finance head's request (b)?
options: Agree, because the auditor's report on the summary financial statements is dated 20th September, 2026, and a report is ordinarily required to deal with every event arising up to the date on which it is signed, the dividend being such an event.
Agree, because a dividend declared by the board after the balance sheet date is invariably required to be disclosed in the summary financial statements relating to that same year.
Refuse, but only on the ground that the dividend is a non-adjusting event which does not alter the profit reported in the audited financial statements for the year.
Refer the dividend to those charged with governance and apply to have the report on the audited financial statements re-dated, so that both reports deal with events up to the same date.

Refuse, because where the auditor reports on the summary financial statements after completion of the audit, the auditor is not required to report the effect of events occurring after the date of the report on the audited financial statements.
questions.explanation: SA 810 expressly provides that when the auditor reports on summary financial statements after completion of the audit of the financial statements, the auditor is not required to report on the effect of subsequent events which occurred after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, since the summary financial statements are derived from the audited financial statements. The date that fixes the cut-off is therefore 30th June, 2026 and not 20th September, 2026, and the dividend of 12th August, 2026 lies beyond it. The first option adopts the wrong reference date, which is the most common error here. The second asserts an invariable disclosure duty the source does not create; the third reaches refusal on an adjusting or non-adjusting analysis rather than on the date rule and so misstates the reason; and the fourth invents a re-dating remedy.

questions.category: SA 810 – Procedures: Summarised Nature vs Criteria vs Misleading
questions.question:
Consider the following statements on the procedures which form the basis of the auditor's opinion on summary financial statements:
Statement 1: Adequately disclosing the summarised nature of the summary financial statements and identifying the audited financial statements is an evaluation separate from adequately disclosing the criteria applied in their preparation.
Statement 2: Once the applied criteria are fully disclosed, the summary financial statements to that extent cannot be regarded as misleading.
Statement 3: The evaluation whether the summary financial statements contain necessary information and are not misleading is directed at content, and can fail even where the summarised nature and the applied criteria are both properly disclosed.
Statement 4: SA 810 illustrates the first evaluation with a title such as 'Summary/Abridged Financial Statements prepared/derived from Audited Financial Statements for the year ended 31st March, 20XX'.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The standard lists separately the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements adequately disclose their summarised nature and identify the audited financial statements, the evaluation of whether they adequately disclose the applied criteria, and the evaluation of whether they contain necessary information and are not misleading; these are three tests and not one. Statement 2 is the classic conflation: disclosure of criteria is a transparency requirement about the basis of preparation and tells the user nothing about whether the content selected is sufficient and non-misleading, so a document can disclose its criteria fully and still fail the third test. Statements 1, 3 and 4 are each supported by the text, Statement 4 being the source's own illustration of the first evaluation. The decisive point is that the misleading-content test looks at what has been included and emphasised, not at how the basis has been labelled.

questions.category: SA 810 – Procedures: Nature of Each Procedure
questions.question:
Match the following procedures, which the auditor performs as the basis for the opinion on summary financial statements, with the nature of the test each involves:
Column I
(A) Evaluate whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty
(B) Where the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements, evaluate whether they clearly describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available
(C) Evaluate whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria
(D) Compare the summary financial statements with the related information in the audited financial statements
Column II
(1) Applies only on a stated condition as to how the two documents are issued
(2) The comparison of the summary financial statements against the figures in the audited financial statements
(3) A standing evaluation of accessibility which does not depend on how the two documents are issued
(4) A test of conformity with the basis of preparation, not of arithmetical agreement
(5) A test discharged by the title given to the document
Which of the following matchings is correct?
questions.explanation: Availability of the audited financial statements is evaluated whenever the auditor reports, independently of the mode of issue, which matches A with 3; the description of the source of the audited financial statements carries an express condition about non-accompaniment, which matches B with 1. Preparation as per the applied criteria asks whether the basis management adopted in framing the summary financial statements has been followed, a qualitative test matched by 4, whereas comparing the summary financial statements with the related information in the audited financial statements asks whether the figures agree, matched by 2. The second option swaps C and D, the very confusion the standard's separate enumeration is meant to prevent. The third and fifth options attach the title test, Column II item 5, which belongs to the disclosure of summarised nature and is a distractor here.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Where the auditor reports on the summary financial statements after the audit of the financial statements is complete, the auditor is not required to report on the effect of subsequent events which occurred after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements.
Reason (R): The summary financial statements are derived from the audited financial statements.
In the light of the above, choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the explanation for A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the explanation for A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The source states the rule and its reason in a single sentence: the auditor is not required to report on the effect of subsequent events which occurred after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements since the summary financial statements are derived from the audited financial statements. The derivation is what logically closes the auditor's duty, because an event falling outside the audited financial statements can have no effect on a document which reproduces nothing beyond them. Both statements are therefore correct and the reason explains the assertion. A candidate who selects the second option would have to point to some independent basis for the exemption, which the standard does not supply; the third and fourth wrongly deny either the exemption or the derivation.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT correctly classified by reference to SA 810?
options: Obtaining management's agreement that it acknowledges responsibility to make the audited financial statements available to intended users of the summary financial statements without difficulty – matter to be settled before accepting the engagement.
Evaluating whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty – procedure performed as the basis for the auditor's opinion.
Determining whether the applied criteria are acceptable – procedure performed as the basis for the auditor's opinion on the summary financial statements.
Evaluating whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria – procedure performed as the basis for the auditor's opinion.

Evaluating whether the summary financial statements adequately disclose their summarised nature and identify the audited financial statements – procedure performed as the basis for the auditor's opinion.
questions.explanation: Acceptability of the applied criteria is determined by the auditor before accepting the engagement, together with the management responsibilities to be agreed; it is not one of the seven procedures enumerated as the basis for the opinion. What appears among those procedures instead is the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria and whether they adequately disclose those criteria, both of which assume the criteria have already been found acceptable. The third option therefore misclassifies an acceptance prerequisite as a reporting-stage procedure. The first two options illustrate the closely related but distinct pairing the standard makes at this point: management's agreement to make the audited financial statements available belongs to acceptance, while the auditor's own evaluation of availability belongs to the procedures, so neither is wrongly classified here.

questions.category: SA 810 – Procedures: Applied Criteria vs Agreement
questions.question: A company's summary balance sheet reproduces the audited figures without alteration but collapses the heads of the balance sheet in a manner the applied criteria do not permit. Separately, a figure in its summary profit and loss account agrees with the audited financial statements only because management altered the amount it had first entered. Which statement MOST APPROPRIATELY captures the distinction SA 810 draws between the evaluation of preparation as per the applied criteria and the comparison with the related information in the audited financial statements?
options: The first defect is a failure of the comparison procedure and the second a failure of the criteria evaluation, since agreement is tested against the criteria and conformity against the audited figures.
The first defect is a failure of the criteria evaluation and the second engages the comparison procedure, the two being different tests neither of which subsumes the other.
Both defects fall under the comparison procedure alone, because any departure from the audited financial statements must ultimately show up as a difference in figures.
Both defects fall under the criteria evaluation alone, the comparison procedure being confined to arithmetical casting within the summary financial statements.
The two requirements merge into a single test whenever the alteration is made by management rather than by the auditor.
Neither defect is reached by these two procedures, both being directed instead at the disclosure of the summarised nature.
questions.explanation: The evaluation of preparation as per the applied criteria asks whether the basis management adopted in framing the summary financial statements has been followed, so a permitted presentation not observed fails it even though the amounts agree. The comparison procedure asks whether the summary financial statements agree with the related information in the audited financial statements, so a figure reconciled by amending the amount engages that test and not the criteria test. SA 810 enumerates the two separately, and the first option simply inverts them. The third and fourth collapse one test into the other, which is the conflation the enumeration exists to prevent; the fifth introduces an irrelevant distinction by actor; and the sixth transfers both defects to the summarised nature procedure, which addresses neither.

questions.question:
Arrange the following procedures, performed by the auditor as the basis for the opinion on summary financial statements, in the order in which SA 810 enumerates them.
A – Evaluate whether the summary financial statements are prepared as per the applied criteria
B – Evaluate whether the audited financial statements are available to users of the summary financial statements without difficulty
C – Evaluate whether the summary financial statements adequately disclose their summarised nature and identify the audited financial statements
D – Compare the summary financial statements with the related information in the audited financial statements
E – Where the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements, evaluate whether they clearly describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available
F – Evaluate whether the summary financial statements contain necessary information and are not misleading
options: C – E – B – A – D – F
B – C – E – A – D – F
C – B – A – E – D – F
C – B – E – A – D – F
C – B – E – D – A – F
questions.explanation: The standard lists the procedures as disclosure of summarised nature and identification of the audited financial statements first, availability of the audited financial statements without difficulty second, the conditional description of the source third, preparation as per the applied criteria fourth, adequate disclosure of the applied criteria fifth, comparison with the related information sixth, and sufficiency and freedom from misleading content seventh. Item F, the last enumeration, closes every sequence offered, so the discriminating part is the order of the first five. The first option pushes the conditional source description ahead of the availability evaluation it presupposes; the third places the criteria evaluation before the conditional description; the second opens with availability rather than with the summarised nature disclosure; and the fifth reverses comparison and criteria compliance. The decisive point is the conditional placement of item E immediately after item B.

questions.question: Which of the following pairings of a situation with the SA 810 requirement it attracts is NOT correct?
options: The summary financial statements are issued together with the audited financial statements – the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements clearly describe from whom or where the audited financial statements are available is not attracted.

The report on the summary financial statements is signed after completion of the audit and after the date of the report on the audited financial statements – no duty arises to report the effect of events occurring after that earlier report date.
The applied criteria are established by a recognised body – the auditor must independently re-determine their acceptability before performing any of the enumerated procedures.

The summary financial statements reproduce the audited figures correctly but are silent on a material contingency disclosed in the audited financial statements – the evaluation whether the summary financial statements contain necessary information and are not misleading is attracted.

The document carries a title in the form illustrated in SA 810 – that is one way in which the evaluation of whether the summary financial statements adequately disclose their summarised nature and identify the audited financial statements may be satisfied.
questions.explanation: Acceptability of the applied criteria is settled at the engagement acceptance stage, and where the criteria are established by a recognised organisation or by law or regulation the auditor may presume them to be acceptable; nothing in SA 810 requires that presumption to be re-litigated before each procedure is performed, so the third pairing states the position backwards. The first is correct because the description of the source of the audited financial statements is expressly conditioned on the summary financial statements not being accompanied by the audited financial statements. The second follows from the exemption for events arising after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements. The fourth and fifth correctly attach a silent material contingency to the sufficiency and non-misleading evaluation, and an illustrative title to the summarised nature evaluation. The decisive fact is who established the criteria.

questions.question:
**Case:** Kansan Textiles Ltd prepared Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2025 under criteria prescribed by its industry association; the audited financial statements were placed on the company's website and are available to intended users without difficulty. The following facts emerged:
(1) The CFO wanted the opinion on the Summary FS to read that they 'present a true and fair view'. The engagement partner insisted that SA 810 permits only fixed forms of wording where an unmodified opinion is to be given.
(2) On comparison, the summarised balance sheet omitted a provision of Rs. 4.20 crore for a pending environmental claim which the audited FS had disclosed, although the applied criteria required every provision above Rs. 1 crore to be carried into the Summary FS. The auditor asked management to add it back; management declined on the ground that the summarised format had limited space.
(3) The auditor's report on the audited FS contained a qualified opinion (expected credit losses of Rs. 6.80 crore on loan investments not being recognised), a Key Audit Matters section and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on a pending merger.
(4) No law or regulation prescribed the wording of the opinion on the Summary FS.
You are the auditor reporting on the Summary FS under SA 810.

Is the engagement partner correct, and what wording may be used if an unmodified opinion is to be expressed on the Summary FS?
options: Incorrect; SA 810 prescribes no form of wording for the opinion on Summary FS, it being enough that the applied criteria are adequately disclosed in them and that the audited FS are identified.

Incorrect; since neither law nor regulation has prescribed the wording for this company's Summary FS and the applied criteria are adequately disclosed in them, the CFO may adopt the true and fair view formula.

Correct; the opinion may use either the 'consistent (in all material aspects) with the audited FS as per the applied criteria' phrase or the 'a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria' phrase.

Correct; only the 'fair summary' phrase is available where the applied criteria are framed by a recognised body, the 'consistent' phrase being reserved by SA 810 for criteria prescribed by law or regulation.
questions.explanation: SA 810 gives the auditor exactly two permitted forms of opinion where he concludes that an unmodified opinion on the Summary FS is appropriate: that the Summary FS are consistent (in all material aspects) with the audited FS as per the applied criteria, or that they are a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria. A true and fair view formula is neither of them, and the absence of statutory wording does not free the auditor to invent his own. The partner is right on the point of form, although on these facts the opinion would in the event be modified because of fact (2). Option 0 confuses disclosure of the applied criteria with the form of opinion; option 1 treats silence of the law as permission; option 3 invents a split between the two phrases according to who framed the criteria, which the standard does not make.

questions.category: SA 810 – Adverse Opinion on Summary FS
questions.question:
**Case:** Kansan Textiles Ltd prepared Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2025 under criteria prescribed by its industry association; the audited financial statements were placed on the company's website and are available to intended users without difficulty. The following facts emerged:
(1) The CFO wanted the opinion on the Summary FS to read that they 'present a true and fair view'. The engagement partner insisted that SA 810 permits only fixed forms of wording where an unmodified opinion is to be given.
(2) On comparison, the summarised balance sheet omitted a provision of Rs. 4.20 crore for a pending environmental claim which the audited FS had disclosed, although the applied criteria required every provision above Rs. 1 crore to be carried into the Summary FS. The auditor asked management to add it back; management declined on the ground that the summarised format had limited space.
(3) The auditor's report on the audited FS contained a qualified opinion (expected credit losses of Rs. 6.80 crore on loan investments not being recognised), a Key Audit Matters section and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on a pending merger.
(4) No law or regulation prescribed the wording of the opinion on the Summary FS.
You are the auditor reporting on the Summary FS under SA 810.

Which is the most appropriate conclusion on the opinion to be expressed on the Summary FS having regard to fact (2)?
options: An adverse opinion on the Summary FS, they not being consistent in all material aspects with the audited FS as per the applied criteria and management not making the necessary changes.
A qualified opinion, the omitted provision being material to the summarised balance sheet but confined to a single line item and therefore not pervasive.
A disclaimer of opinion on the Summary FS, the disagreement with management on the omitted provision remaining unresolved at the date of the auditor's report.

An unmodified opinion in the 'fair summary' form, the omission being one of presentation only, the figures actually shown agreeing with the audited FS and those audited FS remaining available on the company's website to all intended users without any difficulty.
questions.explanation: SA 810 requires an adverse opinion where the Summary FS are not consistent (in all material aspects) with, or are not a fair summary of, the audited FS as per the applied criteria and management does not make the necessary changes. Both triggers are present: the omitted Rs. 4.20 crore provision breaks the applied criteria, and management has refused to add it back. Availability of the audited FS to users is a separate procedural requirement and cannot cure an inconsistency, so option 3 fails. SA 810 offers neither a qualification nor a disclaimer for this situation, which rules out options 1 and 2. Note also that this adverse opinion springs from the Summary FS themselves; the qualification on the audited FS produces a different consequence under the table on references to matters included in the report on the audited FS.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference to Matters in Audited FS Report
questions.question:
**Case:** Kansan Textiles Ltd prepared Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2025 under criteria prescribed by its industry association; the audited financial statements were placed on the company's website and are available to intended users without difficulty. The following facts emerged:
(1) The CFO wanted the opinion on the Summary FS to read that they 'present a true and fair view'. The engagement partner insisted that SA 810 permits only fixed forms of wording where an unmodified opinion is to be given.
(2) On comparison, the summarised balance sheet omitted a provision of Rs. 4.20 crore for a pending environmental claim which the audited FS had disclosed, although the applied criteria required every provision above Rs. 1 crore to be carried into the Summary FS. The auditor asked management to add it back; management declined on the ground that the summarised format had limited space.
(3) The auditor's report on the audited FS contained a qualified opinion (expected credit losses of Rs. 6.80 crore on loan investments not being recognised), a Key Audit Matters section and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on a pending merger.
(4) No law or regulation prescribed the wording of the opinion on the Summary FS.
You are the auditor reporting on the Summary FS under SA 810.

With reference to fact (3), consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The report on the Summary FS must state that the report on the audited FS contains a qualified opinion, and must describe the basis for that qualified opinion together with the effect thereof on the Summary FS.
**Statement 2:** The report on the Summary FS must state that the report on the audited FS contains a Key Audit Matters section and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph, and must describe those matters and their effect on the Summary FS.
**Statement 3:** The report on the Summary FS must state that, owing to the qualified opinion on the audited FS, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS.
**Statement 4:** The description called for extends to the effect of the matters on the Summary FS and not merely to the existence of those matters.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: A qualified opinion in the report on the audited FS carries two requirements into the report on the Summary FS: a statement that the audited FS report contains a qualified opinion, and a description of the basis for it and of the effect thereof on the Summary FS - that is Statement 1. The Key Audit Matters section and the Emphasis of Matter paragraph fall in the first cell of the same table, which likewise calls for a statement that the audited FS report contains them and a description of the matter and its effect on the Summary FS - Statements 2 and 4. Statement 3 borrows the third limb belonging only to the adverse/disclaimer cell; a qualified opinion on the audited FS does not make it inappropriate to opine on the Summary FS, so every combination containing Statement 3 is wrong.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference to Matters in Audited FS Report
questions.question:
**Case:** Kansan Textiles Ltd prepared Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2025 under criteria prescribed by its industry association; the audited financial statements were placed on the company's website and are available to intended users without difficulty. The following facts emerged:
(1) The CFO wanted the opinion on the Summary FS to read that they 'present a true and fair view'. The engagement partner insisted that SA 810 permits only fixed forms of wording where an unmodified opinion is to be given.
(2) On comparison, the summarised balance sheet omitted a provision of Rs. 4.20 crore for a pending environmental claim which the audited FS had disclosed, although the applied criteria required every provision above Rs. 1 crore to be carried into the Summary FS. The auditor asked management to add it back; management declined on the ground that the summarised format had limited space.
(3) The auditor's report on the audited FS contained a qualified opinion (expected credit losses of Rs. 6.80 crore on loan investments not being recognised), a Key Audit Matters section and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph on a pending merger.
(4) No law or regulation prescribed the wording of the opinion on the Summary FS.
You are the auditor reporting on the Summary FS under SA 810.

Which of the following actions should the auditor take in this engagement?
**Action 1:** State in the report on the Summary FS that the report on the audited FS contains a qualified opinion, a Key Audit Matters section and an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
**Action 2:** Agree with management the form of opinion to be expressed on the Summary FS before the report is finalised.
**Action 3:** Describe the basis for the qualified opinion on the audited FS and the effect thereof on the Summary FS.
**Action 4:** Express a disclaimer of opinion on the Summary FS so as to avoid a public disagreement with management over the omitted provision.
options: 1 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
questions.explanation: Actions 1 and 3 implement the table on matters included in the report on the audited FS: the qualified opinion cell calls for a statement that the audited FS report contains a qualified opinion and a description of its basis and of the effect thereof on the Summary FS, while the KAM section and the EOM paragraph call for a statement that they are present and a description of them and their effect. Action 2 implements Note (i), under which the auditor shall agree with management the form of opinion to be expressed on the Summary FS. Action 4 is wrong because SA 810 provides no disclaimer route for an unresolved disagreement about the Summary FS: where management does not make the necessary changes the modification specified is an adverse opinion.

questions.question:
**Case:** Under the rules framed under the State Co-operative Societies Act applicable to Narmada Dairy Union Ltd, the auditor's report on the summary financial statements is required to state that 'the abstract and balance sheet are in agreement with the audited financial statements'. The audited FS of the Union for 2024-25 received an unmodified opinion, the applied criteria are those prescribed in the same rules, and after carrying out the procedures required by SA 810 the auditor is satisfied that the Summary FS are a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria. On reading the draft report, however, the auditor concluded that members of the Union, who are the intended users, would read the prescribed phrase as a certification that each transaction in the books of account had been examined, which is not what a summary FS engagement covers. The rules do not prohibit the auditor from adding a paragraph to his report.

Which is the MOST APPROPRIATE course of action for the auditor?
options: Decline to use the statutory phrase and issue the opinion in one of the two SA 810 forms instead, on the view that a Standard on Auditing cannot be modified by rules framed under a State Act.
Apply the procedures necessary to express the prescribed opinion, evaluate whether users might misunderstand it and consider whether an additional explanation can mitigate that misunderstanding.

Reproduce the prescribed statutory wording and take the matter no further, the impression formed by the members of the Union being outside the auditor's control once the law has itself fixed the wording of the opinion.

Express an adverse opinion on the Summary FS, the statutory wording being neither of the two forms permitted by SA 810 and the partner treating the conflict as a limitation on the scope of the summary FS engagement.
questions.explanation: Note (ii) governs this situation: where law or regulation prescribes a different wording of the opinion on Summary FS, the auditor shall apply the necessary procedures to enable him to express the prescribed opinion, and shall evaluate whether users might misunderstand that opinion and, if so, whether an additional explanation in the report on the Summary FS can mitigate the misunderstanding. The facts supply both conditions, the misunderstanding being identified and nothing preventing an added paragraph, so only the option covering both limbs is complete. Option 0 denies the accommodation SA 810 itself makes for prescribed wording; option 2 omits the procedures limb and the evaluation; option 3 mistakes a wording mismatch for a scope limitation or a defect in the Summary FS.

questions.question:
**Case:** Under the rules framed under the State Co-operative Societies Act applicable to Narmada Dairy Union Ltd, the auditor's report on the summary financial statements is required to state that 'the abstract and balance sheet are in agreement with the audited financial statements'. The audited FS of the Union for 2024-25 received an unmodified opinion, the applied criteria are those prescribed in the same rules, and after carrying out the procedures required by SA 810 the auditor is satisfied that the Summary FS are a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria. On reading the draft report, however, the auditor concluded that members of the Union, who are the intended users, would read the prescribed phrase as a certification that each transaction in the books of account had been examined, which is not what a summary FS engagement covers. The rules do not prohibit the auditor from adding a paragraph to his report.

Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The auditor shall apply the procedures necessary to enable him to express the opinion wording prescribed by law or regulation.
**Statement 2:** The auditor shall evaluate whether users might misunderstand the opinion on the Summary FS and, if so, whether an additional explanation in that report can mitigate the misunderstanding.
**Statement 3:** Because the wording is fixed by the rules, the auditor must for that reason substitute one of the two SA 810 phrases after obtaining management's agreement to it.
**Statement 4:** The statutory origin of the wording displaces the need for any further procedures, the prescribed opinion being self-supporting.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are the two limbs of Note (ii) and both apply to the Union, because the rules prescribe their own form of words and the members are likely to misread them. Statement 3 inverts the rule: SA 810 does not require the prescribed wording to be replaced by one of the two phrases, it requires procedures to be applied and the risk of misunderstanding to be evaluated, and Note (i) on agreeing the form of opinion operates where the standard's own phrases are in play. Statement 4 is the opposite error, treating a statutory form of words as removing the need for procedures. The decisive fact is that a real risk of user misunderstanding has already been identified and an additional paragraph is permissible.

questions.question:
**Case:** Under the rules framed under the State Co-operative Societies Act applicable to Narmada Dairy Union Ltd, the auditor's report on the summary financial statements is required to state that 'the abstract and balance sheet are in agreement with the audited financial statements'. The audited FS of the Union for 2024-25 received an unmodified opinion, the applied criteria are those prescribed in the same rules, and after carrying out the procedures required by SA 810 the auditor is satisfied that the Summary FS are a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria. On reading the draft report, however, the auditor concluded that members of the Union, who are the intended users, would read the prescribed phrase as a certification that each transaction in the books of account had been examined, which is not what a summary FS engagement covers. The rules do not prohibit the auditor from adding a paragraph to his report.

**Assertion (A):** The auditor in this case cannot discharge his SA 810 responsibility merely by reproducing the statutory phrase in the report on the Summary FS.
**Reason (R):** Where law or regulation prescribes a wording of the opinion on summary financial statements that differs from the SA 810 phrases, the auditor shall apply the necessary procedures to enable him to express the prescribed opinion and shall evaluate whether users might misunderstand that opinion.

Which option is correct?
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.explanation: Note (ii) imposes two affirmative duties whenever the law prescribes its own form of opinion, and those duties are precisely why mechanical reproduction of the statutory phrase is insufficient. The Reason therefore explains the Assertion directly: the auditor must do work to be able to express the prescribed opinion, and must consider whether users might misunderstand it and whether an additional explanation in the report on the Summary FS can mitigate that. The two statements are not merely parallel requirements, which rules out the second option, and neither misstates the standard, which rules out the third and fourth. The likelihood of misunderstanding among the members is the decisive fact.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference to Matters in Audited FS Report
questions.question:
**Case:** Palani Engineering Ltd circulated Summary Financial Statements for 2024-25 with its annual report. The auditor's report on the audited FS contained (a) a 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section pointing to a Rs. 210 crore term loan repayment falling due within twelve months against sanctioned limits that remained unconfirmed, (b) a Key Audit Matters section dealing with revenue recognition on long-duration contracts, (c) an 'Other Matter' paragraph recording that the auditor's report on the immediately preceding year was modified, and (d) a statement of an uncorrected material misstatement in the other information which management refused to correct. The Summary FS, prepared under criteria framed by a recognised body, reproduce the summarised figures but say nothing about the going concern uncertainty, and the applied criteria do not require the narrative accompanying the audited FS to be reproduced.

What should the auditor's report on the Summary FS contain in this regard?
options: Nothing further is required in the report on the Summary FS, the applied criteria framed by the recognised body not requiring the narrative accompanying the audited FS to be reproduced along with the summarised figures.

Only a statement that the report on the audited FS contains a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section and a Key Audit Matters section, the Other Matter paragraph and the other information statement being matters outside the Summary FS altogether.

A statement that the report on the audited FS contains a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section, a Key Audit Matter section, an Other Matter paragraph and a statement of uncorrected material misstatement of other information, and a description of those matters and their effect on the Summary FS.

A description of the going concern uncertainty and the effect thereof on the Summary FS, the Key Audit Matters, the Other Matter paragraph and the other information statement being narrative in character and calling for no reference in that report.
questions.explanation: Where the report on the audited FS contains going concern, Key Audit Matter, EOM/OM or other information matters, SA 810 requires two things of the report on the Summary FS: a statement that the audited FS report contains a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section, a Key Audit Matter section, an EOM/OM paragraph and a statement of uncorrected material misstatement of other information; and a description of the matter referred above and the effect thereof on the Summary FS. All four matters are present here, so options 1 and 3 each give an incomplete set. Option 0 confuses the content of the Summary FS, which the applied criteria govern, with the auditor's reporting obligation, which is triggered by what the report on the audited FS contains.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference to Matters in Audited FS Report
questions.question:
**Case:** Palani Engineering Ltd circulated Summary Financial Statements for 2024-25 with its annual report. The auditor's report on the audited FS contained (a) a 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section pointing to a Rs. 210 crore term loan repayment falling due within twelve months against sanctioned limits that remained unconfirmed, (b) a Key Audit Matters section dealing with revenue recognition on long-duration contracts, (c) an 'Other Matter' paragraph recording that the auditor's report on the immediately preceding year was modified, and (d) a statement of an uncorrected material misstatement in the other information which management refused to correct. The Summary FS, prepared under criteria framed by a recognised body, reproduce the summarised figures but say nothing about the going concern uncertainty, and the applied criteria do not require the narrative accompanying the audited FS to be reproduced.

Consider the following statements:
**Statement 1:** The report on the Summary FS must state that the report on the audited FS contains a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section and a Key Audit Matter section.
**Statement 2:** The report on the Summary FS must state that the report on the audited FS contains an Other Matter paragraph and a statement of uncorrected material misstatement of other information.
**Statement 3:** The report on the Summary FS must describe the matters referred to above and the effect thereof on the Summary FS.
**Statement 4:** The report on the Summary FS must state that, by reason of the going concern uncertainty, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS.
Which of the above are required by SA 810?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 together make up the first limb of the going concern/KAM/EOM/OM/other information cell, which requires the report on the Summary FS to state that the report on the audited FS contains each of those four items. Statement 3 is the second limb of the same cell, calling for a description of the matter referred above and the effect thereof on the Summary FS. Statement 4 is not required: the words 'due to such opinion it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS' appear only in the adverse/disclaimer cell, and a material uncertainty related to going concern falls in the first cell, not the third. Which cell the matter sits in, and not how serious the uncertainty is, decides the answer.

questions.category: SA 810 – Adverse Opinion on Summary FS
questions.question:
Match the situations in Column I with the reporting consequences in Column II under SA 810.
**Column I**
(A) The Summary FS are not consistent in all material aspects with the audited FS as per the applied criteria, but management makes the necessary changes before the report is issued.
(B) The Summary FS are not a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria and management declines to make the necessary changes.
(C) The auditor's report on the audited FS contains an adverse opinion.
(D) Law or regulation prescribes a wording of the opinion on the Summary FS different from the SA 810 phrases.
**Column II**
(1) Adverse opinion on the Summary FS.
(2) Unmodified opinion in one of the two permitted phrases, the second trigger of the modified opinion rule being absent.
(3) A statement that the audited FS report contains an adverse opinion, a description of its basis and a statement that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS.
(4) The necessary procedures are applied to enable the prescribed opinion to be expressed, and the possibility of user misunderstanding is evaluated.
Which matching is correct?
questions.explanation: In (A) only the first trigger of the modified opinion rule is satisfied, management having made the necessary changes, so an unmodified opinion in one of the two permitted phrases follows; that pairing eliminates option 0. In (B) both triggers are satisfied and SA 810 specifies an adverse opinion on the Summary FS. In (C) the third cell of the reference table applies, whose distinctive third limb states that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS, which is a different consequence from an adverse opinion on them, so C-1 is wrong. In (D) Note (ii) applies, requiring procedures and an evaluation of possible user misunderstanding, so any matching that places D against the adverse or inappropriateness consequences must fail.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference to Matters in Audited FS Report
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about what the report on summary financial statements must say when the auditor's report on the audited financial statements is modified:
**Statement 1:** Where the audited FS report contains a qualified opinion, the report on the Summary FS must state that fact and describe the basis for the qualification together with the effect thereof on the Summary FS.
**Statement 2:** Where the audited FS report contains a disclaimer of opinion, the report on the Summary FS must itself contain a disclaimer of opinion on the Summary FS and nothing more.
**Statement 3:** Where the audited FS report contains an adverse opinion, the report on the Summary FS must additionally state that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS.
**Statement 4:** The requirement to state that the audited FS report contains an adverse opinion or a disclaimer, to describe its basis and to state that it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS applies in identical terms where the audited FS report contains a qualified opinion.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The qualified opinion cell has two limbs only: a statement that the audited FS report contains a qualified opinion, and a description of the basis for it and of the effect thereof on the Summary FS, so Statement 1 states the rule correctly. The adverse/disclaimer cell has three limbs, the third being a statement that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS; it is not a disclaimer on the Summary FS, and it is not 'nothing more', so Statement 2 is wrong twice over. Statement 4 is wrong because the third limb is confined to the adverse/disclaimer cell and does not travel across to a qualification, where the auditor still expresses his own opinion on the Summary FS. Counting the limbs as two, two and three is the decisive test.

questions.category: SA 810 – Adverse Opinion on Summary FS
questions.question:
**Scenario:** The Summary FS of Ramnad Coir Ltd omit all reference to a contingent liability of Rs. 34 crore disclosed in the audited FS, although the applied criteria require such a disclosure. The auditor has proposed adding a summarised note and management has written confirming that the note will be added before the report is signed.

If, before the report is issued, management reverses its decision and declines to make the change, what changes in the auditor's conclusion on the opinion?
options: Nothing changes, the omitted item being a narrative note rather than a figure, so the Summary FS remain consistent in all material aspects with the audited FS as per the applied criteria.
The opinion moves from unmodified to a qualified opinion on the Summary FS, the matter being material but confined to one disclosure and not pervasive.
The opinion moves from unmodified to a disclaimer of opinion, the point remaining unresolved at the date of the report and evidence being unavailable.
The opinion moves to adverse on the Summary FS, those statements failing the applied criteria and management not making the necessary changes.
questions.explanation: The modified opinion rule in SA 810 has two cumulative parts: the Summary FS must fail to be consistent in all material aspects with, or to be a fair summary of, the audited FS as per the applied criteria, and management must not make the necessary changes. Before the reversal only the first part was met, so an unmodified opinion in one of the two permitted phrases was available; after the reversal both are met and an adverse opinion is required. Option 0 fails because the applied criteria require the disclosure, so omitting it breaks consistency irrespective of whether the item is narrative. Options 1 and 2 import the graded modifications of a complete-set audit; the standard specifies the adverse form here and does not offer a qualification or a disclaimer.

questions.category: SA 810 – Adverse Opinion on Summary FS
questions.question:
**Case:** Two engagements of Suresh Rao & Co., Chartered Accountants, are being reviewed by the peer reviewer:
**Engagement 1:** The auditor's report on the audited FS of Trichy Motors Ltd for 2024-25 is unmodified. Its Summary FS exclude the entire 'Reserve for Exhausted Mines' although the applied criteria require it; management has refused to include it, describing the summarised presentation as 'a matter of style'.
**Engagement 2:** The auditor's report on the audited FS of Coimbatore Spinning Mills Ltd for 2024-25 is a disclaimer of opinion for inability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence on inventories of Rs. 96 crore. Its Summary FS agree, figure for figure, with the audited FS and satisfy the applied criteria completely.

Which conclusion correctly distinguishes the two reports on the Summary FS?
options: Both reports carry an adverse opinion on the Summary FS, the state of the report on the audited FS in Engagement 2 making any further comment about the disclaimer unnecessary in that report.
Engagement 1 carries a qualified opinion on the Summary FS; Engagement 2 carries a disclaimer of opinion on the Summary FS.

Engagement 1 carries an adverse opinion on the Summary FS; in Engagement 2 the report states that the audited FS report contains a disclaimer, describes its basis and states that it is thereby inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS.

Engagement 1 carries an unmodified opinion, the omission being one of presentation only in the words of management; Engagement 2 carries an adverse opinion on the Summary FS mirroring the disclaimer given on the audited FS, both engagements being governed by the same cell of the reference table.
questions.explanation: Engagement 1 is governed by the modified opinion row of the form of opinion table: the Summary FS are not consistent in all material aspects with the audited FS as per the applied criteria and management will not make the necessary changes, so an adverse opinion is expressed on the Summary FS. Engagement 2 is governed by the third cell of the reference table: the defect is not in the Summary FS, which satisfy the applied criteria, but in the report on the audited FS, and the prescribed consequence is a statement of the disclaimer, a description of its basis and a statement that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS. Option 0 collapses two entirely different reasons for trouble into one; option 1 mislabels both modifications; option 3 is wrong in each engagement and in treating one cell as governing both.

questions.question:
The auditor's report on the complete set of financial statements of a company carries an adverse opinion. The same firm is separately asked to report (i) on the statement of sales of a single division of that company, and (ii) on the company's summary financial statements.

Which statement correctly contrasts the position under SA 805 with the position under SA 810?
options: Nothing may be reported in either case, both SA 805 and SA 810 providing in identical terms that an adverse opinion on the complete set of financial statements precludes the expression of any further opinion whatsoever, whether on a specific element or on summary financial statements.

Under SA 805 an unmodified opinion on the specific element is not barred merely because the complete set carries an adverse opinion, subject to SA 805's own conditions; under SA 810 the adverse opinion on the audited FS makes it inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS.

Under SA 810 an unmodified opinion in one of the two permitted phrases remains available on the Summary FS if they agree with the audited FS, the consequence of the adverse opinion being confined to the element dealt with under SA 805.
The adverse opinion must be reproduced in identical terms in both reports, the wording of the opinion on the element and on the Summary FS being that given on the audited FS.
questions.explanation: The two standards take opposite approaches to the same trigger. Under SA 805 an adverse or disclaimed opinion on the complete set does not by itself bar an unmodified opinion on a specific element, subject to that standard's own conditions, because the element can be viewed separately from the matter behind the modification. Under SA 810 the Summary FS are derived from the audited FS as a whole, so where the report on the audited FS carries an adverse opinion or a disclaimer the report on the Summary FS states that fact, describes the basis and states that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS. Option 0 ignores the SA 805 accommodation; option 2 reverses the two positions; option 3 misstates the consequence, which is inappropriateness to opine rather than a mirrored adverse opinion.

questions.question:
**Case:** Esope Agro Inputs Ltd has an adverse opinion on its audited FS for 2024-25 because the treatment of biological assets departs from the applicable financial reporting framework. K. Menon & Co. handles two further assignments for the same company:
(a) an engagement under SA 805 to report on the statement of sales of the company's pesticide division, prepared under specified accounting criteria and constituting a single element, the matter causing the adverse opinion not affecting that statement;
(b) an engagement under SA 810 to report on the company's Summary FS, which the auditor finds to be consistent in all material aspects with the audited FS as per the applied criteria, management having made every change proposed to it.

Which of the following is correct?
options: In (b) too the auditor should express the unmodified opinion in the 'consistent (in all material aspects) with the audited FS as per the applied criteria' form, because the Summary FS satisfy the applied criteria, management has co-operated fully, and the adverse opinion on the audited FS is relevant only to the report on those audited FS.

In (a) an unmodified opinion on the element is not barred by the adverse opinion on the complete set, subject to SA 805's conditions; in (b) the report must state that the audited FS report carries an adverse opinion, describe its basis and state that it is inappropriate to opine on the Summary FS.
Both (a) and (b) must carry an adverse opinion mirroring in terms the opinion given on the complete set of financial statements.
In (b) a qualified opinion is appropriate, describing the basis of the adverse opinion on the audited FS and the effect thereof on the Summary FS.
questions.explanation: The attractive fact in (b) is that the Summary FS are consistent with the audited FS and management has corrected everything proposed, but that is not decisive, because the report on the audited FS itself carries an adverse opinion. The third cell of the reference table then governs: the report on the Summary FS states that the audited FS report contains an adverse opinion, describes its basis and states that, due to such opinion, it is inappropriate to express an opinion on the Summary FS. The position in (a) differs, SA 805 permitting an unmodified opinion on a specific element notwithstanding an adverse opinion on the complete set, subject to its own conditions, and the facts state the adverse matter does not touch the division. Option 0 states the trap conclusion, option 2 wrongly infects the element, and option 3 substitutes a qualification for the inappropriateness statement.

questions.category: SA 810 – Agreement with Management on Form of Opinion
questions.question:
**Case:** While drafting the report on the Summary FS of Nellimarla Ceramics Ltd, the engagement partner decided, without consulting management, to use the phrase that the Summary FS 'are a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria'. Management had prepared the Summary FS under criteria framed by a recognised body and had understood from the previous year's report that the phrase 'are consistent in all material aspects with the audited FS as per the applied criteria' would be used. The Summary FS are in fact fully consistent with the audited FS and satisfy the applied criteria; no law or regulation prescribes any wording for the opinion on the Summary FS.

Which of the following best states the position under SA 810?
options: The form of opinion lies within the auditor's discretion at the drafting stage, no discussion with management being contemplated where the opinion to be given is an unmodified one.

The 'consistent in all material aspects' phrase must be used wherever the applied criteria are established by a recognised body rather than by law, so the wording actually chosen is incorrect on its face.
A difference of view with management about the form of wording obliges the auditor to modify the opinion expressed on the Summary FS.
The auditor shall agree with management the form of opinion to be expressed; both phrases are permitted, so the defect is the absence of agreement and not the phrase selected.
questions.explanation: Note (i) requires the auditor to agree with management the form of opinion to be expressed on the Summary FS, and that requirement is not switched off because the opinion is unmodified. Since SA 810 offers exactly two permitted phrases and either may be the subject of the agreement, the phrase used here is not wrong in itself; what is missing is the agreement, which option 0 denies. Option 1 invents a link between the identity of the body framing the criteria and the phrase to be used, and option 2 confuses the form of the opinion with its content, a modification arising from inconsistency or absence of fair summary where management will not correct, not from a difference over wording.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the form of an unmodified opinion on summary financial statements under SA 810:
**Statement 1:** The words 'in all material aspects' qualify the consistency phrase, so the auditor does not assert complete identity of detail between the Summary FS and the audited FS.
**Statement 2:** The words 'as per the applied criteria' are common to both permitted phrases and remain necessary whichever phrase is used.
**Statement 3:** SA 810 permits a third form of wording, namely that the Summary FS 'give a true and fair view', where the audited FS themselves give a true and fair view.
**Statement 4:** The auditor may use either of the two permitted phrases, the choice between them being a matter to be agreed with management.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 4 only
1 and 2 only
2, 3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: SA 810 permits precisely two phrases for an unmodified opinion on the Summary FS: consistent (in all material aspects) with the audited FS as per the applied criteria, or a fair summary of the audited FS as per the applied criteria. Statement 1 draws out the materiality qualifier, which is why an immaterial difference in presentation does not by itself defeat consistency, and Statement 2 identifies the words common to both phrases, the benchmark being the applied criteria and not the framework used for the audited FS. Statement 4 reflects Note (i), the form being agreed with management. Statement 3 is wrong because no third phrase exists; a true and fair view formula is not one of the permitted forms and cannot be introduced by reference to the opinion on the audited FS.

questions.question:
Case A: Vandana Desai & Co are the statutory auditors of Kaveri Spindles Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X1 and have also accepted an engagement to report on the company's summary financial statements. The chronology is as follows. (1) Sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the audited financial statements was obtained on 26 June 20X1, and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was signed and dated 30 June 20X1. (2) A fire destroyed the company's Yercaud warehouse on 8 July 20X1, causing an uninsured loss of Rs 18 crore, and the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share on 21 July 20X1; neither matter is reflected in the audited financial statements. (3) The board approved the summary financial statements for inclusion in the annual report on 12 August 20X1. (4) The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 16 August 20X1. (5) A junior member of the engagement team had earlier circulated a draft of the report on the summary financial statements bearing the date 20 June 20X1. (6) The annual report containing the summary financial statements was released to the public on 20 August 20X1, and the auditors dated their report on the summary financial statements 20 August 20X1.

What is the earliest date on which Vandana Desai & Co could validly have dated their report on the summary financial statements?
options: 26 June 20X1
30 June 20X1
16 August 20X1
20 August 20X1
12 August 20X1
questions.explanation: SA 810 fixes two independent floors for the date of the report on summary financial statements: it shall be dated not earlier than the date on which the auditor obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, and not earlier than the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements. On these facts the first floor is 16 August 20X1 and the second is 30 June 20X1, so the later of the two, 16 August 20X1, controls. 20 June (the circulated draft) and 26 June breach both floors, and 30 June satisfies only the second floor while the evidence on the summary financial statements did not exist until 16 August. The release of the annual report on 20 August is a publication event and not a dating floor, so 20 August is permissible but not the earliest; 12 August is the board's approval date, which the rule does not use as a measure.

questions.question:
Case A: Vandana Desai & Co are the statutory auditors of Kaveri Spindles Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X1 and have also accepted an engagement to report on the company's summary financial statements. The chronology is as follows. (1) Sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the audited financial statements was obtained on 26 June 20X1, and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was signed and dated 30 June 20X1. (2) A fire destroyed the company's Yercaud warehouse on 8 July 20X1, causing an uninsured loss of Rs 18 crore, and the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share on 21 July 20X1; neither matter is reflected in the audited financial statements. (3) The board approved the summary financial statements for inclusion in the annual report on 12 August 20X1. (4) The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 16 August 20X1. (5) A junior member of the engagement team had earlier circulated a draft of the report on the summary financial statements bearing the date 20 June 20X1. (6) The annual report containing the summary financial statements was released to the public on 20 August 20X1, and the auditors dated their report on the summary financial statements 20 August 20X1.

**Statement 1:** The draft bearing the date 20 June 20X1 cannot be issued as it stands, because that date is earlier than the date of the report on the audited financial statements and also earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements was obtained.
**Statement 2:** Had sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements been obtained on 20 July 20X1 instead of 16 August 20X1, the earliest permissible date of the report on the summary financial statements would have been 30 June 20X1.
**Statement 3:** Because the date of the report on the summary financial statements is later than the date of the report on the audited financial statements, the introductory paragraph must state that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events occurring after 30 June 20X1.
**Statement 4:** Because the report on the summary financial statements is dated 20 August 20X1, the auditors must also extend their work to the 8 July fire and the 21 July dividend and report their effect in the report on the summary financial statements.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1 and 3 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the 20 June draft fails both limbs of the dating rule, being earlier than 30 June 20X1 (report on the audited financial statements) and earlier than 16 August 20X1 (evidence on the summary financial statements). Statement 2 is wrong because the two limbs operate together and the later floor governs; with evidence obtained on 20 July 20X1 the earliest permissible date would have been 20 July 20X1, not 30 June 20X1. Statement 3 is correct and is the consequence that flows from the dating rule: since the report on the summary financial statements cannot be dated earlier than the report on the audited financial statements, a later date triggers the conditional statement required in the introductory paragraph. Statement 4 draws the opposite conclusion: the required response to the later date is that introductory-paragraph statement recording that the summary financial statements do not reflect subsequent events, not an extension of the audit to the July fire and the July dividend.

questions.question:
Case A: Vandana Desai & Co are the statutory auditors of Kaveri Spindles Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X1 and have also accepted an engagement to report on the company's summary financial statements. The chronology is as follows. (1) Sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base the opinion on the audited financial statements was obtained on 26 June 20X1, and the auditor's report on the audited financial statements was signed and dated 30 June 20X1. (2) A fire destroyed the company's Yercaud warehouse on 8 July 20X1, causing an uninsured loss of Rs 18 crore, and the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share on 21 July 20X1; neither matter is reflected in the audited financial statements. (3) The board approved the summary financial statements for inclusion in the annual report on 12 August 20X1. (4) The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 16 August 20X1. (5) A junior member of the engagement team had earlier circulated a draft of the report on the summary financial statements bearing the date 20 June 20X1. (6) The annual report containing the summary financial statements was released to the public on 20 August 20X1, and the auditors dated their report on the summary financial statements 20 August 20X1.

Assume that, in place of facts (3), (4) and the last sentence of fact (6), everything material to the summary financial statements, including their approval by the board and the completion of the auditors' procedures obtaining sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on them, had taken place on or before 30 June 20X1, and that the auditors dated their report on the summary financial statements 30 June 20X1 instead of 20 August 20X1. The annual report continued to be released on 20 August 20X1. Which of the following is the correct consequence of this single change?
options: The report is validly dated, but the introductory paragraph must still state that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events, because the annual report was released on 20 August 20X1.

The report is validly dated and the introductory paragraph need not carry the statement about subsequent events, because that report is not dated later than the report on the audited financial statements.
The report is invalidly dated, because a report on summary financial statements must always bear a date later than the date of the report on the audited financial statements.

The report is validly dated, but the identification of the audited financial statements and the statement that reading them is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements become required only after this change, and must now be inserted.
The report is invalidly dated, because sufficient appropriate audit evidence on summary financial statements cannot exist before the board has approved them.
questions.explanation: 'Not earlier than' permits equality of dates, so a report on the summary financial statements dated 30 June 20X1, the evidence also having been obtained by that date, satisfies both limbs of the dating rule. The statement that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events is conditional: it is required where the date of the report on the summary financial statements is later than the date of the report on the audited financial statements, and identical dates switch it off. Identification of the summary financial statements and their title, identification of the audited financial statements, and the statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements are unconditional requirements of the introductory paragraph, so nothing about them 'now' changes. The release of the annual report on 20 August and the existence of the July fire and dividend do not trigger the conditional statement; the decisive fact is the relative dates of the two auditors' reports.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question:
