Case B: Raghav Iyer & Co have been engaged to report on the summary financial statements of Nalan Logistics Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X2, which are printed in the company's annual report. The auditor's report on the audited financial statements is dated 25 August 20X2. The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 10 September 20X2, and dated their report on the summary financial statements 20 September 20X2. The report laid before the audit committee consists, in successive paragraphs, of: a heading 'Independent Auditor's Report on the Summary Financial Statements of Nalan Logistics Ltd'; the addressee 'To the members of Nalan Logistics Ltd'; an introductory paragraph which identifies the summary financial statements bearing the title 'Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 20X2 derived from the audited financial statements', identifies the audited financial statements, and states that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of events occurring after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, the introductory paragraph containing no other statement; a management responsibility paragraph; an auditor's responsibility paragraph stating that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810; a paragraph referring to matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; an opinion paragraph; an Other Matter paragraph; the signature of the partner in the name of the firm; and the place of signature 'Chennai'. The audited financial statements are available to intended users on the company's website and at its registered office.

Required: Which of the following sets lists the basic elements of the auditor's report on summary financial statements completely and consistently with SA 810, so as to serve as a correct build for a report of this kind?
options: Title; Introductory paragraph; Management responsibility; Auditor's responsibility; Auditor's opinion; Date; Signature.

Title; Addressee; Introductory paragraph; Management responsibility; Auditor's responsibility; Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; Auditor's opinion including any EOM/OM paragraph; Date; Signature; Place of signature.

Title; Addressee; Introductory paragraph; Management responsibility; Auditor's responsibility; EOM/OM paragraph as a separate element; Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; Auditor's opinion; Date; Signature.

Title; Addressee; Introductory paragraph; Auditor's responsibility; Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; Auditor's opinion; Date; Signature; Place of signature.

Title; Addressee; Introductory paragraph; Management responsibility; Auditor's responsibility; Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; Auditor's opinion; Date; Signature; Place of signature; and a statement that the auditor has complied with relevant ethical requirements regarding independence.
questions.explanation: The enumerated elements are Title, Addressee, Introductory paragraph, Management responsibility, Auditor's responsibility, Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, and the Auditor's opinion including the EOM/OM paragraph if any; the source separately requires the date of the report, the auditor's signature and the place of signature. Option 1 is the only set that carries all of these and correctly folds the EOM/OM paragraph into the opinion element rather than promoting it to a stand-alone element. The first set drops the addressee and the reference element and omits the place of signature; the third set misplaces the EOM/OM paragraph as a separate element and drops the place of signature; the fourth drops management responsibility. The last set adds an independence and ethics compliance statement, which is not among the elements enumerated for a report on summary financial statements, and the place of signature is a required element even though it is easily overlooked.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question:
Case B: Raghav Iyer & Co have been engaged to report on the summary financial statements of Nalan Logistics Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X2, which are printed in the company's annual report. The auditor's report on the audited financial statements is dated 25 August 20X2. The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 10 September 20X2, and dated their report on the summary financial statements 20 September 20X2. The report laid before the audit committee consists, in successive paragraphs, of: a heading 'Independent Auditor's Report on the Summary Financial Statements of Nalan Logistics Ltd'; the addressee 'To the members of Nalan Logistics Ltd'; an introductory paragraph which identifies the summary financial statements bearing the title 'Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 20X2 derived from the audited financial statements', identifies the audited financial statements, and states that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of events occurring after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, the introductory paragraph containing no other statement; a management responsibility paragraph; an auditor's responsibility paragraph stating that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810; a paragraph referring to matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; an opinion paragraph; an Other Matter paragraph; the signature of the partner in the name of the firm; and the place of signature 'Chennai'. The audited financial statements are available to intended users on the company's website and at its registered office.

**Action 1:** Insert in the introductory paragraph a statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements.
**Action 2:** Delete the Other Matter paragraph, since the basic elements of a report on summary financial statements admit no such paragraph.
**Action 3:** Retain the paragraph referring to matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements as an element standing by itself, alongside the opinion.
**Action 4:** Advance the date of the report to 25 August 20X2 so that it coincides with the report on the audited financial statements and the need to say anything about subsequent events disappears.
Which actions should Raghav Iyer & Co take before issuing the report?
options: 2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
1 only
questions.explanation: Action 1 is required: the introductory paragraph must carry three things, identification of the summary financial statements including their title together with identification of the audited financial statements, the conditional statement about subsequent events, and the statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements; the Case B paragraph contains only the first two. Action 3 is correct because the reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements is itself an enumerated element, sitting alongside the opinion rather than inside it. Action 2 is wrong, since the auditor's opinion element expressly includes the EOM/OM paragraph, if any. Action 4 fails on the first limb of the dating rule: the report cannot be dated earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements was obtained, which is 10 September 20X2, and back-dating to engineer the conditional statement away is not available.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question:
Case B: Raghav Iyer & Co have been engaged to report on the summary financial statements of Nalan Logistics Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X2, which are printed in the company's annual report. The auditor's report on the audited financial statements is dated 25 August 20X2. The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 10 September 20X2, and dated their report on the summary financial statements 20 September 20X2. The report laid before the audit committee consists, in successive paragraphs, of: a heading 'Independent Auditor's Report on the Summary Financial Statements of Nalan Logistics Ltd'; the addressee 'To the members of Nalan Logistics Ltd'; an introductory paragraph which identifies the summary financial statements bearing the title 'Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 20X2 derived from the audited financial statements', identifies the audited financial statements, and states that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of events occurring after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, the introductory paragraph containing no other statement; a management responsibility paragraph; an auditor's responsibility paragraph stating that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810; a paragraph referring to matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements; an opinion paragraph; an Other Matter paragraph; the signature of the partner in the name of the firm; and the place of signature 'Chennai'. The audited financial statements are available to intended users on the company's website and at its registered office.

**Statement 1:** The report is validly dated, because 20 September 20X2 is not earlier than either the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements was obtained or the date of the report on the audited financial statements.
**Statement 2:** The Other Matter paragraph must be struck out, because the elements of a report on summary financial statements do not contemplate any such paragraph.
**Statement 3:** Nothing further is required of the introductory paragraph, since it already identifies the summary financial statements and their title and identifies the audited financial statements.
**Statement 4:** The signature of the partner and the place of signature are themselves required elements of the auditor's report on summary financial statements.
Which of the above statements are NOT correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
3 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: both dating floors are cleared, the evidence floor being 10 September 20X2 and the audited financial statements report floor being 25 August 20X2. Statement 2 is not correct, because the auditor's opinion element is prescribed to include the EOM/OM paragraph, if any, so an Other Matter paragraph is contemplated. Statement 3 is not correct, because identification of the summary financial statements and of the audited financial statements is only one of the three requirements of the introductory paragraph; the unconditional statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements is still missing, the subsequent-events statement being already present because this report is dated later than the report on the audited financial statements. Statement 4 is correct, the auditor's signature and the place of signature being required alongside the date, and it is the place of signature that is most often left out in practice.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question: Priya Menon & Co have completed an engagement to report on the summary financial statements of Tirupur Exports Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X3. Their auditor's responsibility paragraph reads: 'We are responsible for expressing an opinion on the financial statements of Tirupur Exports Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X3 in accordance with the Standards on Auditing issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.' The paragraph is complete in itself and follows the management responsibility paragraph. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate defect to point out?
options: The paragraph should also record that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements.
The paragraph is required only where the summary financial statements are not accompanied by the audited financial statements.
No defect arises, because the summary financial statements are derived from the audited financial statements and the responsibility is ultimately for those statements.
The paragraph should state that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the audited financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810.
The paragraph should state that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810.
questions.explanation: The auditor's responsibility element requires a statement that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810; both the subject of the opinion and the named standard are part of the element. The draft mis-states the subject by making the responsibility one for the financial statements, and generic reference to the Standards on Auditing does not identify SA 810. The first option transfers to this paragraph a requirement the source places in the introductory paragraph, so it is not the defect to point out here. The second option invents a condition that the enumerated list does not carry, the third would make the element meaningless for this engagement, and the fourth corrects the standard while leaving the wrong subject of the opinion.

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, an Assertion (A) and a Reason (R) are stated. Mark the correct option.
**Assertion (A):** Where the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements on 3 May 20X4, his report on those summary financial statements bearing the date 3 May 20X4 is validly dated even though his report on the audited financial statements is dated 5 May 20X4.
**Reason (R):** SA 810 requires the auditor's report on summary financial statements to be dated not earlier than the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is incorrect.
A is incorrect but R is correct.
Both A and R are incorrect.
questions.explanation: The dating rule has two limbs and each can bite on its own: the report must be dated not earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained and not earlier than the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements. Here the first limb is satisfied on 3 May 20X4, but the second is not, since 3 May is earlier than 5 May 20X4; the assertion is therefore incorrect while the reason correctly states the second limb and is indeed the explanation of why the assertion fails. A candidate who treats the evidence date as conclusive applies one limb in isolation and overlooks the independent floor set by the report on the audited financial statements.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question:
Match each statement or requirement in Column I with the element of the auditor's report on summary financial statements to which SA 810 assigns it, as set out in the list of basic elements.
Column I
(A) Reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements.
(B) The engagement was conducted as per SA 810.
(C) The summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events occurring after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements.
(D) The Emphasis of Matter paragraph, if any.
Column II
(1) Introductory Paragraph
(2) Auditor's Responsibility
(3) Auditor's Opinion
(4) Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements
questions.explanation: The introductory paragraph carries three requirements, namely identification of the summary financial statements including their title and of the audited financial statements, the conditional statement about subsequent events, and the statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements; items A and C therefore both belong to element (1). The reference to SA 810 as the standard under which the engagement was conducted belongs to the auditor's responsibility element, item B to (2). The EOM/OM paragraph, item D, is prescribed as part of the auditor's opinion element, that is (3), and not as a separate element. The tempting error is to attach item C to the reference element and item D to the reference element; the reference element is a distinct enumerated item standing alongside the opinion, whereas the EOM/OM paragraph sits within the opinion itself.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question: While preparing a checklist of the basic elements of the auditor's report on summary financial statements for use across all such engagements, an audit manager recorded the following items. Which one of these is NOT enumerated by SA 810 as a basic element of that report?
options: Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements.
Management responsibility.
Title and Addressee.
A statement that the auditor has complied with the relevant ethical requirements regarding independence and has fulfilled the auditor's other ethical responsibilities.
A statement that the auditor is responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810.
questions.explanation: The enumerated elements are Title, Addressee, Introductory paragraph, Management responsibility, Auditor's responsibility, Reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, and the Auditor's opinion including the EOM/OM paragraph if any, to which the source adds the date of the report, the auditor's signature and the place of signature. An explicit statement about compliance with ethical requirements regarding independence is not among them, so the fourth item is the correct answer to a 'NOT' question of this kind. The remaining items are all listed, the auditor's responsibility item being noteworthy only because it names SA 810 as the standard under which the engagement was conducted.

questions.question: In each of the following options a situation is paired with a consequence said to follow from it under SA 810. Which pairing is CORRECT?
options: Situation: the report on the summary financial statements is dated earlier than the report on the audited financial statements, the auditor having obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements on that same earlier date. Consequence: the report is validly dated, and the only result is that the introductory paragraph need not carry the statement about subsequent events.

Situation: the report on the summary financial statements bears the same date as the report on the audited financial statements. Consequence: the introductory paragraph must still state that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events, because such events may have occurred after the audited financial statements were reported on.

Situation: the report on the summary financial statements is dated 20 August and the report on the audited financial statements is dated 30 June. Consequence: the introductory paragraph must state that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events occurring after 30 June, and those events must also be described in an Other Matter paragraph.

Situation: the report on the summary financial statements is dated 20 August although sufficient appropriate audit evidence on them was obtained only on 16 August, the report on the audited financial statements being dated 30 June. Consequence: the date is valid, being not earlier than both the evidence date and the date of the report on the audited financial statements, and the introductory paragraph must carry the statement that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events after the date of that report.

Situation: the introductory paragraph identifies the summary financial statements and identifies the audited financial statements. Consequence: nothing further is required of that paragraph where the two reports bear the same date.
questions.explanation: The third pairing correctly applies both limbs of the dating rule and the conditional statement in the introductory paragraph: 20 August is not earlier than 16 August, the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements was obtained, nor earlier than 30 June, the date of the report on the audited financial statements, and because the summary financial statements report is dated later, the statement that they do not reflect the effect of subsequent events after the date of the report on the audited financial statements is required. The first pairing overlooks the second limb, since a date earlier than the report on the audited financial statements is invalid however complete the evidence then was. The second wrongly converts a conditional requirement into an unconditional one; equality of dates does not trigger it. The third wrongly attaches a description of the events to the report, and the fifth ignores the unconditional statement that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements, which is required whatever the dates.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question:
Case C: Charudatt Rao & Co report on the summary financial statements of Mysore Ceramics Ltd for the year ended 31 March 20X6. The auditor's report on the audited financial statements is dated 10 July 20X6 and contains a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern section and one Emphasis of Matter paragraph. The auditors obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence on which to base their opinion on the summary financial statements on 5 August 20X6. The report on the summary financial statements is drafted as follows: the heading 'Independent Auditor's Report'; the addressee 'To the members of Mysore Ceramics Ltd'; an introductory paragraph identifying the summary financial statements bearing the title 'Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 20X6', identifying the audited financial statements, and stating that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements; a management responsibility paragraph; an auditor's responsibility paragraph stating that the auditors are responsible for expressing an opinion on the summary financial statements, which was conducted as per SA 810; an opinion paragraph; the signature of the partner in the name of the firm; the place of signature 'Bengaluru'; and the date 1 August 20X6.
**Statement 1:** The date of 1 August 20X6 is not permissible.
**Statement 2:** The introductory paragraph must additionally state that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events occurring after 10 July 20X6.
**Statement 3:** The report is complete so far as elements are concerned, because the going concern section and the Emphasis of Matter paragraph belong to the report on the audited financial statements alone.
**Statement 4:** The report must further contain a statement that the auditors have complied with relevant ethical requirements regarding independence.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 4 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the report on the summary financial statements must be dated not earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained, which is 5 August 20X6, so 1 August is invalid even though it clears the other floor of 10 July. Statement 2 is correct and is the link between the dating rule and the introductory paragraph: the report on the summary financial statements cannot be dated earlier than the report on the audited financial statements, and once it bears a later date the statement that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events after 10 July 20X6 becomes mandatory. Statement 3 is wrong, because the elements include a reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, and the opinion element itself includes the EOM/OM paragraph, if any, so the going concern section and the Emphasis of Matter paragraph already reported cannot simply be ignored in the build. Statement 4 adds an item that is not among the enumerated elements.

questions.category: SA 810 – Elements of Report on Summary FS
questions.question: Kavitha & Sons issued a report on the summary financial statements of Sundara Hills Tea Estates Ltd. That report bears the title 'Independent Auditor's Report on the Summary Financial Statements'; is addressed to the members of the company; contains an introductory paragraph identifying the summary financial statements and their title, identifying the audited financial statements, stating that the summary financial statements do not reflect the effect of subsequent events after the date of the auditor's report on the audited financial statements, and stating that reading the summary financial statements is not a substitute for reading the audited financial statements; contains a management responsibility paragraph and an auditor's responsibility paragraph referring to SA 810; contains the reference about matters included in the auditor's report on the audited financial statements and an opinion paragraph together with an Other Matter paragraph; and is signed by the partner in the name of the firm and dated 4 September 20X6, the auditor's report on the audited financial statements having been dated 12 August 20X6 and sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements having been obtained on 28 August 20X6. Which of the following best describes the position?
options: The report omits the place of signature, which is a required element, while its date is valid.
The report omits the place of signature and is also invalidly dated, 4 September 20X6 being earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained.
The report is complete, the place of signature being required only for the report on the audited financial statements.
The report omits the management responsibility element and is invalidly dated.
The report is complete except that the Other Matter paragraph should not have formed part of it.
questions.explanation: The auditor's signature and the place of signature are required alongside the date of the report, and the place of signature is the item most easily lost in a review because it is not part of the tabulated list of paragraph elements. Here every enumerated paragraph element is present, including the reference element as a distinct item and the Other Matter paragraph within the opinion element, and the introductory paragraph satisfies all three of its requirements. As to the date, 4 September 20X6 is not earlier than 28 August 20X6, the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence on the summary financial statements was obtained, nor earlier than 12 August 20X6, the date of the report on the audited financial statements, so both limbs are met and the second option's dating objection fails. The third option wrongly confines the place of signature to the audited financial statements report, and the fourth wrongly removes management responsibility, which is stated.

questions.category: SA 810 – Association with Audited Summary FS
questions.question:
Vandana Textiles Ltd. has completed its statutory audit for the year ended 31 March 2026. CA Mahesh Desai & Co. is the statutory auditor and was also engaged to report on the summary financial statements derived from those audited financial statements; their report on the summary financial statements has already been signed and dated 2 June 2026. The company proposes to circulate to investors a glossy booklet titled 'Annual Business Companion' which contains the summary financial statements but does not contain the auditor's report on them. Page 3 of the draft booklet states: 'The summary financial statements of the Company have been reported on by our statutory auditors.' The print date is fixed at 20 June 2026. When the wording was discussed, the managing director said that the auditor's report was 'too long for the booklet' and pointed out that the audited financial statements are available on the company's website.

On reading the draft, what is the auditor's FIRST appropriate action?
options: Request management to change the statement on page 3 so that it does not give the impression that the auditor has reported on the summary financial statements.
Request management to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in the booklet.
Take actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring the auditor in the booklet, page 3 being a statement which refers to the auditor.
Require management to delete the statement on page 3, the booklet being a document which is not required to carry the auditor's report.
questions.explanation: Where an entity plans to state that the auditor has reported on summary financial statements in a document which contains those summary financial statements but not the auditor's report, SA 810 requires the auditor to ask management for one thing first: to include the auditor's report. The decisive facts are that these are audited summary financial statements, a signed report on them already exists, and the defect is the absence of that report from the booklet. Asking for the statement to be changed is the remedy for the different situation of unaudited summary financial statements, where no report on them exists to be inserted. Taking action to prevent an inappropriate reference is the escalation step and cannot be the first step while management has not yet refused anything. Deletion of the statement would destroy an accurate statement rather than cure the document, and availability of the audited financial statements on the website does not put the report on the summary financial statements into the booklet.

questions.category: SA 810 – Association with Audited Summary FS
questions.question:
Vandana Textiles Ltd. has completed its statutory audit for the year ended 31 March 2026. CA Mahesh Desai & Co. is the statutory auditor and was also engaged to report on the summary financial statements derived from those audited financial statements; their report on the summary financial statements has already been signed and dated 2 June 2026. The company proposes to circulate to investors a glossy booklet titled 'Annual Business Companion' which contains the summary financial statements but does not contain the auditor's report on them. Page 3 of the draft booklet states: 'The summary financial statements of the Company have been reported on by our statutory auditors.' The print date is fixed at 20 June 2026. When the wording was discussed, the managing director said that the auditor's report was 'too long for the booklet' and pointed out that the audited financial statements are available on the company's website.

Assume in addition that on 10 June 2026 management informs the auditor that the report will not be inserted because the print run is already contracted. What is the auditor required to do now?
options: Take actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring the auditor in that document.
Request management to change the statement on page 3 so that it does not imply any reporting on the summary financial statements.
Do nothing further, the request having already been made and the booklet being management's own document.
Take actions to prevent management from inappropriately associating the auditor with the summary financial statements in that document.
questions.explanation: The requirement has two steps: first a request to management to include the auditor's report, and then, if management does not do so, action to prevent management from inappropriately associating the auditor with the summary financial statements in that document. The first step has been taken and has failed, so the second step is now engaged and the auditor cannot treat a refusal as the end of the matter. The object of that action is important: in this situation the concern is inappropriate association of the auditor with the summary financial statements, which is a wider idea than the 'inappropriately referring the auditor' language used for documents containing unaudited summary financial statements. Requesting a change to the statement belongs to that other situation and would here leave an untrue position in place while the audited summary financial statements still stand reported on nowhere in the booklet. Availability of the audited financial statements on the website is not a substitute for the report on the summary financial statements.

questions.category: SA 810 – Association with Audited Summary FS
questions.question:
Vandana Textiles Ltd. has completed its statutory audit for the year ended 31 March 2026. CA Mahesh Desai & Co. is the statutory auditor and was also engaged to report on the summary financial statements derived from those audited financial statements; their report on the summary financial statements has already been signed and dated 2 June 2026. The company proposes to circulate to investors a glossy booklet titled 'Annual Business Companion' which contains the summary financial statements but does not contain the auditor's report on them. Page 3 of the draft booklet states: 'The summary financial statements of the Company have been reported on by our statutory auditors.' The print date is fixed at 20 June 2026. When the wording was discussed, the managing director said that the auditor's report was 'too long for the booklet' and pointed out that the audited financial statements are available on the company's website.

Consider the following statements on this set of facts.
**Statement 1:** The rule engaged is the one applying to a document containing audited summary financial statements issued without the auditor's report, because the auditor was engaged to report on, and has reported on, the summary financial statements.
**Statement 2:** The auditor's first step is to request management to include the auditor's report on the summary financial statements in the booklet.
**Statement 3:** If management does not include the report, the auditor takes actions to prevent management from inappropriately associating the auditor with the summary financial statements in that document.
**Statement 4:** Since page 3 is a statement referring to the auditor, the auditor must first be satisfied that the reference is made only for his report on the audited financial statements.

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
All of the above
questions.explanation: The two association rules are separated by whether the summary financial statements in the document are audited summary financial statements on which the auditor has reported. Here the auditor was engaged to report on the summary financial statements and his report exists, so the rule applying to a document containing audited summary financial statements without the auditor's report is engaged, and its content is exactly the request to include the report followed, on refusal, by action against inappropriate association. That makes Statements 1, 2 and 3 correct. Statement 4 borrows the two-condition test meant for the different situation in which the auditor is engaged to report on the financial statements but not on the summary financial statements; applying it here would allow management to keep an incorrect impression alive simply by re-wording the sentence, when the cure SA 810 seeks is the presence of the report itself.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference in Document with Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question:
CA Mahesh Desai & Co. audited the financial statements of Vandana Textiles Ltd. for the year ended 31 March 2026 and were also engaged to report on the summary financial statements derived from them; their report on the summary financial statements is signed and dated 2 June 2026. The company's 'Annual Business Companion' will contain those summary financial statements without the auditor's report and will state on page 3: 'The summary financial statements of the Company have been reported on by our statutory auditors.' In that original situation the auditor's first step is to request management to include the auditor's report in the document.

Assume now that the only change is that the company never engaged CA Mahesh Desai & Co. to report on the summary financial statements, and that page 3 is revised to read: 'Our statutory auditors, CA Mahesh Desai & Co., confirm these summary figures.' Which of the following describes the auditor's position correctly under the changed fact?
options: The auditor again requests management to include the auditor's report, that being the first step whenever a document contains summary financial statements.

The auditor must be satisfied that the reference is only for his report on the audited financial statements and that the statement does not imply reporting on the summary financial statements; failing this he requests management to change the statement or not to refer to him.
The auditor takes actions to prevent the reference at once, the revised wording being an express claim of reporting on the summary figures.
No action is required, since the audited financial statements are available to investors on the company's website.
questions.explanation: Changing the single fact that the auditor was never engaged to report on the summary financial statements moves the situation from the rule for documents containing audited summary financial statements to the rule for documents containing unaudited summary financial statements. Under that rule the auditor must be satisfied of two things, that the reference to him is made only for his report on the audited financial statements and that the statement does not give the impression that he has reported on the summary financial statements; if either is not met he requests management to change the statement or not to refer to him, and only if management does not do so does he take action. The remedy of asking for inclusion of the report disappears precisely because there is no report on the summary financial statements to include, so the first option is the trap of carrying the earlier remedy across. Immediate action without the request skips the intermediate step, and website availability of the audited financial statements is irrelevant to whether the auditor is being inappropriately referred to.

questions.category: SA 810 – Association: Audited vs Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question:
Two documents are in issue with different companies.
Document I: contains summary financial statements on which the auditor has reported, but the auditor's report is not included in it, and the entity plans to state in the document that the auditor has reported on those summary financial statements.
Document II: contains summary financial statements which the auditor was not engaged to report on, and the entity plans to make a statement in the document that refers to the auditor.

Consider the following responses.
1. In Document I the auditor's first request is that management include the auditor's report.
2. In Document II, where the conditions the auditor must be satisfied about are not met, the auditor's first request is that management change the statement or not refer to the auditor.
3. Where management does not comply in Document I, the auditor takes actions to prevent management from inappropriately associating the auditor with the summary financial statements in that document.
4. Where management does not comply in Document II, the auditor takes actions to prevent management from inappropriately associating the auditor with the summary financial statements in that document.

Which of the above are correct?
options: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The two blocks have parallel structures but different members, and the difference in the remedies is deliberate. In Document I the auditor has a report on the summary financial statements which the document omits, so the first request is to include that report, and the escalation is directed against management inappropriately associating the auditor with the summary financial statements in that document. In Document II there is no report on the summary financial statements to include, so the first request is that management change the statement or not refer to the auditor, and the escalation is directed against management inappropriately referring the auditor. Item 4 is therefore the swap that must be rejected: it attaches the association language of Document I to the reference situation of Document II. Items 1, 2 and 3 correctly place each remedy with its own document.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference in Document with Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question:
Bharathi Cold Chains Ltd. published a full-page advertisement in a business daily on 12 July 2026. The advertisement carries a table headed 'Summary Financial Information (Unaudited)' for the year ended 31 March 2026, drawn from financial statements audited by CA Sunil Rajagopal & Co. The firm was appointed to audit the financial statements of the company; it was not engaged to report on the summary financial information. The advertisement states: 'Our auditors, CA Sunil Rajagopal & Co., have audited our financial statements and have also reported on the summary financial information appearing alongside, giving investors confidence.' The brand promotion head argues that the sentence is harmless because the firm did sign a report on the full financial statements.

Consider the following statements.
**Statement 1:** The auditor must be satisfied that the reference to the auditor in the advertisement is made only for the auditor's report on the audited financial statements.
**Statement 2:** The auditor must be satisfied that the statement does not give the impression that the auditor has reported on the summary financial information.
**Statement 3:** Since the auditor has in fact reported on the full financial statements, satisfying Statement 1 alone discharges the requirement.
**Statement 4:** Where either condition is not met, the auditor takes actions to prevent the reference at once, without first approaching management.

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1, 3 and 4 only
2 and 4 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
questions.explanation: Where the auditor is engaged to report on the financial statements but not on the summary financial statements and the entity plans a statement in a document that refers to the auditor, the auditor must be satisfied of two matters, and they are conjunctive: the reference is made only for the report on the audited financial statements, and the statement does not give the impression that the auditor reported on the summary financial statements. Statement 3 fails because the second condition can fail even when the first is satisfied, as this advertisement shows: naming the auditors is fine, but asserting that they reported on the summary information is not. Statement 4 fails because the requirement is sequenced: if either condition is not met the auditor first requests management to change the statement or not to refer to the auditor, and action to prevent inappropriate reference follows only if management does not do so. Statements 1 and 2 restate the two conditions correctly, so only 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference in Document with Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question:
Bharathi Cold Chains Ltd. published a full-page advertisement in a business daily on 12 July 2026. The advertisement carries a table headed 'Summary Financial Information (Unaudited)' for the year ended 31 March 2026, drawn from financial statements audited by CA Sunil Rajagopal & Co. The firm was appointed to audit the financial statements of the company; it was not engaged to report on the summary financial information. The advertisement states: 'Our auditors, CA Sunil Rajagopal & Co., have audited our financial statements and have also reported on the summary financial information appearing alongside, giving investors confidence.' The brand promotion head argues that the sentence is harmless because the firm did sign a report on the full financial statements.

The auditor concludes that the second condition he must be satisfied about is not met. Which actions should he take, and in what order?
options: Request management to include the auditor's report on the audited financial statements alongside the table; failing this, take actions to prevent inappropriate association with the summary financial information.
Take actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring the auditor at once, the request to change the statement being optional at this stage.
Request management to change the statement or not to refer to the auditor in the document; if management does not do so, take actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring the auditor.
Request management to change the statement; if management does not, request management to obtain a report on the summary financial information and include it.
questions.explanation: Once a condition the auditor must be satisfied about is not met, the requirement prescribes an approach to management first: change the statement, or remove the reference to the auditor from the document. Only if management does not do so does the auditor take actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring him, which is why treating the request as optional is wrong. Asking for a report to be included is the remedy of the other block, and it is unavailable here because the firm was never engaged to report on the summary financial information and therefore has no such report; the second limb of that option also carries the wrong object, association rather than reference. The fourth option invents an engagement the company never gave, which is not one of the two alternatives SA 810 allows the auditor to demand.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference in Document with Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question:
Bharathi Cold Chains Ltd. published a full-page advertisement in a business daily on 12 July 2026. The advertisement carries a table headed 'Summary Financial Information (Unaudited)' for the year ended 31 March 2026, drawn from financial statements audited by CA Sunil Rajagopal & Co. The firm was appointed to audit the financial statements of the company; it was not engaged to report on the summary financial information. The advertisement states: 'Our auditors, CA Sunil Rajagopal & Co., have audited our financial statements and have also reported on the summary financial information appearing alongside, giving investors confidence.' The brand promotion head argues that the sentence is harmless because the firm did sign a report on the full financial statements.

Which of the following is the MOST appropriate analysis of the brand promotion head's argument?
options: It is valid; the firm did sign a report on the full financial statements, so the reference is only for that report.

It is invalid; the sentence also claims reporting on the summary financial information, so neither condition is satisfied and the auditor first seeks a change to the statement or removal of the reference.
It is invalid; an auditor may not be referred to in any document containing unaudited financial information.
It is partly valid; labelling the table 'unaudited' cures the position, the firm having been engaged to report on the summary financial information.
questions.explanation: The first condition asks whether the reference to the auditor is made only for his report on the audited financial statements; the sentence goes beyond that by asserting a report on the summary financial information, so it fails, and the second condition fails for the same reason because the reader is left with the impression that the auditor reported on the summary information. That is the decisive fact: the truth of the claim about the full financial statements is irrelevant once an untrue claim about the summary information is added. There is no blanket prohibition on referring to an auditor in a document containing unaudited financial information, since the rule positively contemplates such a reference provided both conditions are met, so the third option states the rule too widely. The fourth option is wrong on the facts as well as the law, because the firm was not engaged to report on the summary financial information and a label on the table cannot supply the missing impression test.

questions.category: SA 810 – Reference in Document with Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question:
An entity proposes to include in its investor newsletter a set of summary financial statements on which its statutory auditor was not engaged to report. The draft newsletter contains a paragraph referring to the statutory auditor.

Arrange the following in the order in which SA 810 requires them to occur.
P: The auditor is satisfied that the reference to him is made only for his report on the audited financial statements and that the statement does not give the impression that he has reported on the summary financial statements.
Q: Where P is not achieved, the auditor requests management to change the statement or not to refer to the auditor in the document.
R: Where management does not do so, the auditor takes actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring the auditor.
S: The entity plans to make, in a document containing unaudited summary financial statements, a statement that refers to the auditor.
options: P, S, Q, R
S, Q, P, R
S, P, R, Q
S, P, Q, R
questions.explanation: The rule is triggered by the entity's plan to make a statement referring to the auditor in a document containing summary financial statements which the auditor has not reported on, so S comes first and the auditor's duty arises at the planning stage rather than after circulation. The immediate duty is the satisfaction test in P, which has two limbs that must both be met. Only where P is not achieved does the auditor move to Q, the request to change the statement or to drop the reference, and R follows if management does not comply, so placing R before Q would skip the approach to management which the Standard requires first. Placing P before S inverts cause and effect, since without the planned statement there is nothing for the auditor to be satisfied about.

questions.question:
Nagercoil Coir Exports Ltd. issued on 25 July 2026 an annual report containing 'Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2026' together with the auditor's report on them. The audited financial statements include comparative figures for the year ended 31 March 2025, but the summary financial statements show only the current year. In the audited financial statements the comparative column for 31 March 2025 reflects a bonus issue made during 2025-26; that column does not appear in the summary financial statements at all. Management states that it was free to drop the comparative column because the audited financial statements remain available to users on the company's website.

Consider the following statements.
**Statement 1:** The auditor must determine whether the omission of comparatives from the summary financial statements is reasonable.
**Statement 2:** The auditor must determine the effect of an unreasonable omission on his report on the audited financial statements.
**Statement 3:** The rule is engaged because the audited financial statements contain comparatives while the summary financial statements do not.
**Statement 4:** The omission is automatically reasonable because the audited financial statements remain available to intended users.

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: 1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
1 and 4 only
questions.explanation: The comparatives rule operates where the audited financial statements contain comparatives but the summary financial statements do not; the omission which has to be examined is therefore management's omission in the summary financial statements, here the dropping of the 31 March 2025 column including the bonus issue, and not any omission from the audited financial statements. That makes Statements 1 and 3 correct. Statement 2 misplaces the second determination: where the omission is unreasonable, the auditor determines the effect of that unreasonable omission on his report on the summary financial statements, not on the report on the audited financial statements, which is already issued. Statement 4 substitutes a different requirement for the one in point; the availability of the audited financial statements to intended users is a separate matter and cannot make an omission from the summary financial statements self-justifying, since reasonableness has to be determined on the facts.

questions.question:
Nagercoil Coir Exports Ltd. issued on 25 July 2026 an annual report containing 'Summary Financial Statements for the year ended 31 March 2026' together with the auditor's report on them. The audited financial statements include comparative figures for the year ended 31 March 2025, but the summary financial statements show only the current year. In the audited financial statements the comparative column for 31 March 2025 reflects a bonus issue made during 2025-26; that column does not appear in the summary financial statements at all. Management states that it was free to drop the comparative column because the audited financial statements remain available to users on the company's website.

The auditor concludes that dropping the comparative column is not reasonable. What does SA 810 require the auditor to do next?
options: Express an adverse opinion on the summary financial statements, the omission being unreasonable.
Determine whether the audited financial statements themselves were required to contain comparatives for the year ended 31 March 2025.
Determine the effect of that unreasonable omission on his report on the summary financial statements.
Require management to re-issue the audited financial statements with a comparative column for the year ended 31 March 2025.
questions.explanation: The requirement is deliberately two-staged: first the auditor determines whether the omission of comparatives from the summary financial statements is reasonable, and having concluded that it is not, the auditor determines the effect of that unreasonable omission on his report on the summary financial statements. The second determination is what makes the conclusion operative, and the requirement stops there rather than converting unreasonableness automatically into one particular opinion wording, so the first option runs ahead of the rule. The second option examines the wrong document: the audited financial statements do contain the comparatives, and the omission under review is the one made in the summary financial statements. The fourth option attempts to reopen the audited financial statements and their already issued report, which is neither the omission in question nor the report the rule directs the auditor to consider.

questions.question:
Match each matter arising in an engagement to report on summary financial statements (Column I) with the standard whose treatment SA 810 adopts for it (Column II).
Column I:
A. Unaudited supplementary information presented with the summary financial statements
B. Responding when a material inconsistency exists in other information included in documents containing the summary financial statements
C. Restriction on distribution or use, or alerting readers to the basis of accounting
Column II:
1. SA 700
2. SA 720
3. SA 800
4. SA 810's own independent requirements
questions.explanation: SA 810 disposes of all three matters by cross-reference rather than by setting out independent content: unaudited supplementary information presented with the summary financial statements is dealt with in the same manner as under SA 700, responding to a material inconsistency in other information in documents containing summary financial statements is the same as under SA 720, and restriction on distribution or use or alerting readers to the basis of accounting is the same as under SA 800. The examination trap in the other options is the swapping of these standard numbers, in particular attaching SA 720 to supplementary information or SA 800 to other information. The pairing with item 4 must also be rejected, because for none of these three matters does SA 810 supply a separate treatment of its own. The examinable point is therefore the linkage itself, and the mechanics are those of the referenced standard.

questions.category: SA 810 – Other Information in Documents containing Summary FS
questions.question:
Salem Spinning Mills Ltd. circulated to shareholders a document containing audited summary financial statements together with the auditor's report on them. The same document carries a section headed 'Performance Highlights and Other Information' in which the revenue for the year is stated at a figure higher than the revenue in the audited financial statements, and the auditor concludes that a material inconsistency exists in that other information. The audit senior proposes that SA 810 contains no guidance for this situation and that the auditor need not respond, since the summary financial statements themselves agree with the audited financial statements.

Which is the MOST appropriate advice to the audit senior?
options: The auditor responds in the same manner as SA 720 requires, SA 810 adopting that treatment for other information.
No response is required, since the summary financial statements themselves agree with the audited financial statements.
The auditor applies the treatment of SA 700, the other information being presented with the auditor's report.
The auditor treats the difference as an omission of comparatives and determines whether that omission is reasonable.
questions.explanation: SA 810 disposes of other information in documents containing summary financial statements by stating that responding when a material inconsistency exists is the same as under SA 720, so the absence of detailed guidance in SA 810's own words is not absence of a requirement. The decisive fact is that the inconsistency is in the other information section and not in the summary financial statements, which is why agreement of the summary figures with the audited figures does not answer the point. The SA 700 pointer belongs to a different matter, namely unaudited supplementary information presented with the summary financial statements, and the comparatives rule concerns the dropping of comparative figures from the summary financial statements rather than a conflicting revenue statement elsewhere in the document. The response to be made is therefore governed by SA 720 and is to be found there.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** In an engagement to report on summary financial statements, the auditor works out the treatment of unaudited supplementary information presented along with those summary financial statements from SA 810's own separate requirements on the subject.
**Reason (R):** SA 810 states that the treatment of unaudited supplementary information presented with summary financial statements is the same as under SA 700.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
questions.explanation: The reason is a faithful statement of how SA 810 deals with this matter: it disposes of unaudited supplementary information presented with summary financial statements by adopting the treatment under SA 700. The assertion is not correct, because SA 810 contains no independent body of requirements of its own for this matter; the guidance is to be found in the referenced standard. Since R is precisely what falsifies A, the two cannot stand together as a correct assertion with a correct reason explaining it. The distinction to hold on to is that SA 700 is the pointer for unaudited supplementary information accompanying the summary financial statements, while SA 720 governs a material inconsistency in other information and SA 800 governs restriction on distribution or use and alerting readers to the basis of accounting.

questions.category: SA 810 – Restriction on Distribution or Alerting Readers
questions.question:
Kaveri Grain Marketing Ltd. prepares its financial statements under a special purpose framework prescribed by a commodity marketing board, and its summary financial statements are derived from those financial statements and are intended for the board only. In drafting the auditor's report on the summary financial statements the engagement team debates two points: whether readers should be alerted that the financial statements are prepared under a special purpose basis of accounting, and whether the auditor should restrict distribution or use of the report. The manager notes that SA 810's own list of elements of the report on summary financial statements, comprising title, addressee, introductory paragraph, management responsibility, auditor responsibility, reference to matters included in the report on the audited financial statements and the auditor's opinion, says nothing about either point.

Which is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: These two matters fall outside the report on summary financial statements, SA 810 not repeating them in its list of elements.
SA 700 governs every auditor's report, so its treatment of these two matters alone applies.
SA 810 requires the same treatment as SA 800 on these matters, so SA 800 is applied to the report on the summary financial statements.
The auditor obtains a written confirmation from management restricting distribution, failing which an adverse opinion is expressed.
questions.explanation: SA 810 states that restriction on distribution or use, or alerting readers to the basis of accounting, is the same as under SA 800, so the requirement reaches the report on summary financial statements through that cross-reference rather than through the list of report elements. The manager's observation is therefore a false clue: an element not enumerated in SA 810's list is not thereby excluded, because the cross-reference imports the treatment. The right conclusion is that the auditor looks to SA 800 for what is to be said in the report on the summary financial statements about the special purpose basis of accounting and about restricting distribution or use, and the mechanics themselves belong to SA 800. The SA 700 pointer is for unaudited supplementary information presented with summary financial statements, and the last option invents a confirmation procedure and an opinion consequence that the extract does not support.

questions.category: SA 810 – Association: Audited vs Unaudited Summary FS
questions.question: Consider the following propositions about the SA 810 requirements where a document refers to the auditor. Which ONE proposition is NOT correct?
options: Where the entity plans to state, in a document containing audited summary financial statements but not the auditor's report, that the auditor has reported on those summary financial statements, the auditor requests management to include the auditor's report.
The auditor's obligation in that situation arises only after the document has actually been issued to intended users.

Where a document containing unaudited summary financial statements refers to the auditor, the auditor must be satisfied both that the reference is only for his report on the audited financial statements and that the statement does not give the impression that he reported on the summary financial statements.

If management neither changes the statement nor removes the reference in the unaudited summary financial statements situation, the auditor takes actions to prevent management from inappropriately referring the auditor.
questions.explanation: The trigger in both blocks is what the entity plans to say: the entity plans to state that the auditor has reported on the summary financial statements, or plans to make a statement in the document that refers to the auditor. The auditor's obligations therefore arise while the document is being planned, which is exactly what makes the request to include the report, or to change the statement, capable of achieving anything before circulation; waiting for actual issue would leave only the escalation and would defeat the purpose of the first step. The other three propositions state the rules correctly, including the conjunctive two-condition test for unaudited summary financial statements and the reference-specific escalation. The decisive distinction to notice is between the timing limb, which is pre-issuance, and the remedies, which differ according to whether a report on the summary financial statements exists.
